title: Open-Source Sweep: Archived Official Pages, Shot-Day Weather, and Records Access
summary: Three open-source avenues run to completion: the Internet Archive's capture history of the FBI and Utah DPS statement pages, reanalysis-grade weather for the moment of the shot, and the practical limits of public-records access. Two produce clean negative findings that close off speculation, and one documents a limit rather than a result. Negative findings are recorded here because ruling things out is most of what this app does.
sources_quality: A for the archive captures (Internet Archive CDX, content-hash deduplicated, timestamps verifiable by anyone) and for the weather (Open-Meteo historical reanalysis at the site coordinates); B for the wind-drift figures, which are standard approximations rather than a solved ballistic model
key_takeaway: The archived record shows ordinary evolution, not quiet revision. The FBI's Utah Valley Shooting Updates page changed content at least a dozen times between September 11 and 16, 2025, and the changes are what you would expect: the $100,000 reward offer present on September 11-12 is gone by September 16 and replaced with “A suspect is in custody”; the tip line was split into separate multimedia and information channels and later consolidated; a Virtual Family Assistance Center was added. The early language referred to “individual(s) responsible,” standard hedging when the offender count is unknown, and later text is singular. Nothing located suggests a claim was made and then scrubbed. The weather result is cleaner still and removes a variable from the shot-difficulty argument: at 12:00 MDT on September 10, 2025 the site had 77.7°F, 25% relative humidity, and wind of 2.1 mph from 065°. Against a shot bearing of roughly 280°, that is a full-value crosswind of about 1.2 mph, which moves a 150-grain .30-06 roughly two tenths of an inch at 142 yards. Conditions were effectively calm. Wind did not rise materially until after 14:00, well after the shooting.

findings.claim: Official statement pages were quietly edited to remove earlier claims
findings.detail: The Internet Archive holds at least a dozen content-distinct captures of the FBI's Utah Valley Shooting Updates page between September 11 and 16, 2025, and a further twelve of the Utah DPS press-release page running through July 2026. Comparing the FBI captures shows a progression consistent with an investigation closing: the reward offer and person-of-interest appeal dominate the September 11 version; by September 12 the tip line has been split into a multimedia channel and a separate information channel and four additional items have been released; by September 16 the reward language is gone, the page states a suspect is in custody, and a Virtual Family Assistance Center has been added. This app found no instance of an assertion appearing and then being removed without explanation. This does not speak to the separately documented conflicts between what different officials said aloud — see the Evolving Official Statements entry and contradiction X15 — which concern spoken statements rather than these web pages.

findings.claim: The FBI's early public language committed to a single shooter
findings.detail: The September 11 capture refers to the individual or individuals responsible, using the parenthetical plural form throughout, and solicits help identifying a “person of interest.” By the September 16 capture the framing is singular and custodial. The plural hedging is routine law-enforcement usage when the number of offenders is not established, and its later disappearance coincides with the surrender rather than with any stated finding. It is recorded because commentary in both directions has treated the FBI's early wording as though it committed the Bureau to a position it did not take.

findings.claim: Weather conditions were a material factor in the shot
findings.detail: Historical reanalysis at the site coordinates gives, for 12:00 MDT on September 10, 2025: temperature 77.7°F, relative humidity 25%, wind 2.1 mph from 065° with gusts to 12.3 mph. The firing bearing from the Losee Center toward the courtyard is approximately 280°, making the full-value crosswind component about 1.2 mph. For a 150-grain .30-06 at 142 yards that is on the order of 0.2 inches of deflection — negligible against any aiming error. For comparison, a 10 mph full-value crosswind would produce roughly 1.8 inches at the same range. Wind did not become significant until later in the afternoon, reaching 10-13 mph with gusts of 27-34 mph by 14:00-15:00, well after the shooting. Conditions were warm, dry and effectively calm.

findings.claim: The shot required specialist marksmanship or training
findings.detail: The environmental case for this is now weak. A scoped rifle, a target at roughly 142 yards, a shallow downward angle of about 10.65°, and near-calm air describe a shot within the practical capability of a moderately experienced rifle shooter, and the wind correction required was effectively zero. That said, conditions establish only that the environment was undemanding. Placing a single round precisely on a specific point of a person, from an improvised prone position, under time pressure and with one shot fired, involves factors this analysis does not address, and this app takes no position on the shooter's skill level. What can be said is that no unusual environmental difficulty needs explaining, which removes one argument used to support theories requiring a trained specialist.

findings.claim: Public-records requests were used to obtain primary case documents for this app
findings.detail: They were not, and this is a capability limit rather than a finding. Utah's Government Records Access and Management Act provides a route to underlying records — campus police logs, dispatch audio, incident reports, procurement files — but filing a request requires an identified requester, correspondence, and fee handling, none of which this app can do. The most substantive GRAMA product located is the Daily Caller's April 2026 reporting on UVU's Charlie Kirk files, which the outlet itself described as heavily redacted. That remains the single most promising unexploited avenue in the case: the underlying campus records exist, are in principle obtainable by a person, and have been released once already in redacted form.

Tip line split into multimedia and information channels; four additional items released; 'Photos' section renamed 'Multimedia'
Reward language removed; page states a suspect is in custody; Virtual Family Assistance Center added; tip line consolidated
Utah DPS press-release page shows twelve content-distinct captures over the same period
Site conditions: 77.7F, 25% RH, wind 2.1 mph from 065 deg, gusts 12.3 mph — effectively calm
Wind rises to 10-13 mph with gusts 27-34 mph, well after the shooting

fact_check_gap: Shot-day weather is freely available from multiple reanalysis providers and appears in no filing, expert analysis, or coverage reviewed, despite arguments on both sides turning on how demanding the shot was. Likewise, the archived capture history of the official pages is public and was apparently never consulted by anyone alleging the record had been altered.

title: The Memorial: Venue Ownership, Booking Timeline, Performers, and Who Built It
summary: Who owns State Farm Stadium, when the September 21, 2025 memorial was arranged, who paid, and who produced it. The question underneath is whether an 80,000-seat stadium event assembled in eleven days implies advance planning. It does not, and the reasons are checkable: the stadium was empty that Sunday because the Cardinals were playing away, and the production company had been Turning Point's own highest-paid event vendor for years.
sources_quality: A for the vendor relationship, read directly from IRS Form 990 contractor schedules for two Turning Point entities; A- for ownership, cost and security designation (named city officials, public agencies); B for the booking timeline, which rests on announcement dates because the stadium operator's event contracts are confidential
key_takeaway: State Farm Stadium is owned by the Arizona Sports and Tourism Authority, a public entity, and managed by ASM Global. Turning Point USA and Turning Point Action organised the memorial and reportedly covered the venue rental. The City of Glendale incurred close to $500,000 in fire, ambulance, transport, barricade and police costs, which Deputy City Manager Rick St. John said would be reimbursed by AZSTA and ASM Global. The Department of Homeland Security designated the event SEAR Level 1, the highest tier, the same rating used for the Super Bowl. Kirk was killed on September 10; the venue and date were publicly announced by September 14, four days later, and the event was held on September 21, eleven days after the death. Two facts explain that speed without requiring foreknowledge. September 21, 2025 was a Sunday on which the Arizona Cardinals were playing away at San Francisco, so the building had no conflicting NFL fixture. And the company that designed and produced the memorial, Mosaic Pro Events, is the same Phoenix event-production firm that appears in Turning Point's own IRS filings as one of its largest contractors — $3,636,329 from Turning Point USA in TY2023 for event audio and video production, its second-highest paid vendor that year, plus $450,374 from Turning Point Action in TY2022. An organisation calling its existing multi-million-dollar production partner to build a stadium show is the ordinary explanation for how this came together quickly. On the performer question specifically: a major contemporary Christian lineup was engaged — Chris Tomlin, Brandon Lake, Phil Wickham, Kari Jobe Carnes, Cody Carnes, plus Lee Greenwood and Steve Amerson — performing from around 7 a.m. through the 11 a.m. start. Whether any were paid is not documented anywhere reviewed, and would only become visible in Form 990 filings due around May 2027, and then only if a payee cracked the top-five contractor threshold. Free appearances are common in this genre, so the absence of disclosure is not itself suggestive.

findings.claim: The memorial venue is privately owned by Turning Point or an affiliated party
findings.detail: State Farm Stadium is owned by the Arizona Sports and Tourism Authority, a public entity created by the state, and operated under management by ASM Global, a commercial venue-management company. Turning Point USA and Turning Point Action were the event organisers and reportedly paid to rent the building. Overflow attendees were directed to the adjacent Desert Diamond Arena. No ownership interest connects Turning Point to the venue.

findings.claim: The stadium was booked before Charlie Kirk was killed
findings.detail: No evidence supports this and the public timeline is fully consistent with arrangement after the death: the killing on September 10, a public announcement of venue and date by September 14, and the event on September 21. Fact-checking reviewed for this app found no prior events or institutional ties between Kirk and this venue. The honest limit is that the stadium operator's event contracts are confidential, so the executed booking date is not publicly verifiable in either direction. What can be said is that nothing in the available record indicates advance booking, and that the eleven-day turnaround has two ordinary explanations documented below rather than requiring one.

findings.claim: An NFL stadium being available on eleven days' notice is itself suspicious
findings.detail: September 21, 2025 fell in NFL Week 3, and the Arizona Cardinals were playing that Sunday away at the San Francisco 49ers. State Farm Stadium therefore had no home fixture and was an open date on its own calendar. This is the single most mundane and most checkable answer to the availability question, and it appears in none of the commentary treating the booking speed as anomalous.

findings.claim: The production company was newly engaged for this event
findings.detail: Mosaic Pro Events, which Turning Point tasked with designing and producing the memorial — reportedly involving 37 semi-trucks and hundreds of crew, vendors and partners — corresponds to a long-standing and heavily compensated Turning Point vendor. This app's own review of IRS Form 990 filings found Mosaic Event Productions of Phoenix listed as Turning Point USA's second-highest-paid independent contractor in TY2023 at $3,636,329 for event audio and video production, and separately paid $450,374 by Turning Point Action in TY2022 for event stages, lighting and video production. The relationship substantially predates the assassination and is disclosed on public returns. This is how a stadium-scale production is assembled in days: the organisation phoned the firm that already builds its events.

findings.claim: Public money paid for the memorial
findings.detail: Partly, and the arrangement was reimbursement rather than subsidy as reported. The City of Glendale incurred close to $500,000 in costs for fire personnel and ambulances, transportation staff, barricade installation, and police resources. Deputy City Manager Rick St. John stated the bill would be reimbursed by AZSTA and ASM Global, and characterised the arrangement as routine, noting the city's established partnerships with both and that holding events at these venues is nothing new. Whether reimbursement was completed in full is not established in sources reviewed, and AZSTA is itself a public authority, so the ultimate incidence of some costs is not fully transparent from the reporting.

findings.claim: The security posture was unusual for a private memorial
findings.detail: It was extraordinary, though explicably so given the attendee list. The Department of Homeland Security assigned the event a Special Event Assessment Rating of Level 1, its highest tier, the designation used for events such as the Super Bowl and the Boston Marathon. The Secret Service coordinated joint security planning, Arizona's Department of Public Safety held jurisdiction, and Glendale Police anticipated crowds around 100,000. President Trump, Vice President Vance and Elon Musk attended, and coverage described the security as Super Bowl level with a speaker lineup comparable to a state funeral. Attendees were told to expect TSA-level screening with bags prohibited. The rating follows from protectee presence rather than from anything about the memorial itself.

findings.claim: Outside performers were engaged for the memorial
findings.detail: A substantial contemporary Christian music lineup performed, beginning as early as 7 a.m. local time and continuing for hours as the stadium filled, with the formal proceedings opening at 11 a.m. under worship led by Chris Tomlin. Named performers across reporting: Chris Tomlin, Brandon Lake, Phil Wickham, Kari Jobe Carnes, Cody Carnes, Lee Greenwood, and recording artist Steve Amerson. Wickham, Jobe and Carnes performed together. These are among the largest touring acts in the contemporary Christian genre, not local or incidental bookings, and the lineup was publicised in advance through Turning Point's own event promotion.

findings.claim: Whether the performers were paid appearance fees or donated their time is documented
findings.detail: It is not, in any source reviewed. Coverage across Billboard, Newsweek, Men's Journal, ChurchLeaders and others names the lineup and describes the performances but addresses compensation nowhere, and no organiser statement on the question was located. This is a genuine and checkable gap rather than a mystery: any fees paid to performers by Turning Point USA or Turning Point Action for a September 2025 event would fall in fiscal year 2026 for both entities, and would surface in the Form 990 contractor schedules only if an individual payee ranked among the five highest-compensated independent contractors above $100,000. Those returns are not due until roughly May 2027. Given that Mosaic Event Productions alone drew $3.6 million in TY2023, individual performer fees may well fall below the top-five naming threshold and never be itemised at all. Worth noting for balance that appearing without fee at a memorial is common practice among artists in this genre, and nothing here implies otherwise.

findings.claim: The production was a straightforward memorial service in scale and staging
findings.detail: It was a full stadium production. Reported staging included two large electronic screens, flanking U.S. flags, bulletproof glass panels shielding speakers, and fireworks timed to key speakers' appearances, all built by Mosaic Pro Events using a reported 37 semi-trucks and hundreds of crew, vendors and partners. More than two dozen speeches were delivered. Attendees were required to register with full name, email, phone number and ZIP code, and were asked to wear Sunday best or patriotic colours rather than funeral black. The event carried a branded title, 'Building A Legacy: Remembering Charlie Kirk,' and ran across two venues. In format and production values this was closer to a Turning Point conference than to a funeral, which is consistent with it having been built by the organisation's existing conference-production vendor.

fact_check_gap: Commentary treating the eleven-day turnaround as evidence of advance planning has not engaged either of the two checkable explanations: that the Cardinals were away that Sunday so the building was open, and that the production company was already Turning Point's largest event vendor by disclosed spend. Both are in public records — an NFL schedule and an IRS Form 990. Separately, the stadium operator's contract confidentiality means the actual booking date cannot be independently verified, which no coverage reviewed states plainly in either direction.

title: Claims Surrounding the Kirks: Sourcing Tiers for the Fear, Bloodline, and Epstein Allegations
summary: Four claims circulating about Charlie and Erika Kirk, separated by what each actually rests on. One is a primary document and holds. One rests on a single anonymous source. One has no located source at all. And one is a genealogical claim that the documented record directly contradicts.
sources_quality: A for Kirk's own released message; A- for Erika Kirk's documented ancestry (named grandparents, birthplaces, genealogical records); C for The Grayzone's anonymous-source reporting; D for the bloodline and Epstein-adjacent claims, which trace to fabrication-prone outlets and video commentary
key_takeaway: The base claim is real and this app has carried it for some time: on September 8, 2025, two days before he was killed, Kirk privately wrote that he felt bullied by donor pressure and had no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause. That is a primary document in his own words. Everything built on top of it degrades quickly. The claim that he was frightened of pro-Israel reprisal and had refused a Netanyahu-linked funding offer comes from a single unnamed source published by The Grayzone and amplified by outlets sharing its editorial position. The further claim that Kirk feared being killed traces to a dated primary post: Harrison H. Smith of Infowars, August 13, 2025, saying he would not name names but had been told by someone close to Kirk that Kirk thought Israel would kill him if he turned against them. The date matters — four weeks before the killing and three and a half weeks before Kirk's own September 8 message existed — so it is not a retrospective construction. It remains an anonymous relay by a source who explicitly declines to name his informant, posted inside a factional argument about Kirk declining to debate Nick Fuentes, with no corroborating document or on-record account produced. On Erika Kirk, the Rothschild claim is not merely unsupported but contradicted by the documented genealogy: her paternal grandfather Carl Kenneth Frantzve was born in Falun, Sweden, and her maternal grandfather Joseph Anthony Abbas was born in McKeesport, Pennsylvania to Syrian and Lebanese parents. There is no Rothschild line, and the claim appears to originate in surname confusion and video commentary rather than in any genealogical record.

findings.claim: Kirk privately wrote that he intended to leave the pro-Israel cause over donor pressure
findings.detail: His own message of September 8, 2025, released publicly by Candace Owens, states that he felt bullied by donor pressure and had no choice but to leave the pro-Israel cause. This app has treated it as established and built contradiction X3 around the fact that three people with access to the same private message characterised it three different ways afterwards: Josh Hammer called the idea Kirk was turning on Israel an egregious lie and mere blowing off steam, while Andrew Kolvet described the position as having become complicated and nuanced. Kolvet's version is closest to the document. This finding needs no anonymous sourcing and does not depend on any of the claims below.

findings.claim: Kirk was frightened of reprisal from pro-Israel forces and refused a Netanyahu-linked funding offer
findings.detail: This traces to a September 12, 2025 Grayzone report citing an unnamed “Trump insider and longtime friend”, and was amplified by Press TV, Middle East Monitor and Mondoweiss. It is a single anonymous source, published two days after the killing, by an outlet with a declared editorial position on the subject, and repeated principally by outlets sharing that position rather than independently corroborated. Neither element — the fear of reprisal, nor the refused funding offer — appears in Kirk's own released message, which concerns donor bullying and his intention to withdraw. Anonymous sourcing is not disqualifying and the claim may be true; it has not been corroborated by any named source, document or recording located by this app.

findings.claim: The claim that Kirk feared being killed if he left the Israel movement has an identifiable source
findings.detail: PRIMARY POST OBTAINED (August 2026). The claim traces to Harrison H. Smith, an Infowars host, posting on X on AUGUST 13, 2025. His exact framing: he would not name names, but had been told by someone close to Charlie Kirk that Kirk thought Israel would kill him if he turned against them. Three details from the post itself materially change how it should be weighed, and two of them correct earlier versions of this entry. First, the date. August 13 is roughly four weeks before the killing and, more importantly, about three and a half weeks BEFORE Kirk's own September 8 message about donor bullying, which was not public until after his death. Smith therefore could not have reverse-engineered the claim from that leaked message, and it is not a post-assassination construction. That is a genuine point in its favour and earlier versions of this entry understated it. Second, the wording. Smith wrote “Israel,” not “the Israeli donor lobby” as secondary reporting rendered it; this entry previously repeated the looser paraphrase. Third, the context. The post is a quote-tweet of an August 10 post about Kirk declining to debate Nick Fuentes, in which a commentator characterised mainstream avoidance of Fuentes as a fear response. Smith's claim is thus offered as an explanation for Kirk's conduct inside an intra-right factional argument, not as a standalone warning. It remains unestablished: Smith explicitly declines to identify his source, no document, recording or on-record account from anyone in Kirk's circle has been produced, and an independent fact-check examining the underlying claim found it unsupported. Kirk's own September 8 message describes donor bullying and an intention to leave the pro-Israel cause; it does not mention fear for his life.

findings.claim: Kirk and Erika publicly said he was not afraid of being killed by the political left
findings.detail: This app located no specific statement from either of them in that form. Kirk spoke publicly and often about political violence and risk in general terms, and characterising any of that as a statement that he did not fear the left specifically, as against fearing someone else, would require a direct quotation that has not been produced. Recorded as unverified rather than false: it is the sort of claim that could be settled immediately by a citation, and none has surfaced.

findings.claim: Erika Kirk is related to the Rothschild family
findings.detail: The documented genealogy runs elsewhere entirely. Her father is Kent Frantzve and her mother Loretta Ann “Lori” Frantzve. Her paternal grandfather, Carl Kenneth Frantzve, was born in Falun, Dalarna County, Sweden. Her maternal grandfather, Joseph Anthony Abbas, was born in McKeesport, Pennsylvania to Syrian and Lebanese parents. She was raised in Scottsdale, Arizona. No credible genealogical source contains a Rothschild line, and the claim appears to originate partly in confusion with similar-sounding surnames and partly in video commentary asserting it without documentation. It is worth naming the pattern plainly: attributing a concealed Rothschild bloodline to a public figure is a long-standing antisemitic conspiracy template rather than a genealogical hypothesis, and saying so is not a way of avoiding the factual question, which the records answer directly.

findings.claim: The outlets carrying the Erika Kirk bloodline claim are otherwise reliable
findings.detail: The same information stream carries claims that independent fact-checkers have specifically examined and found unsupported, including that Erika Kirk recruited for Jeffrey Epstein or arranged her husband's death, and that she is banned from Romania. It also includes material from The People's Voice, an outlet with a documented history of fabricated stories, alleging criminal conduct with no evidentiary basis. Source quality is not a substitute for examining a claim on its merits — which is why the genealogical records are set out above — but a claim appearing only in outlets that also publish demonstrably fabricated allegations about the same person warrants correspondingly low prior confidence.

findings.claim: The distinct Kirk-and-Israel claims come from a single origin point
findings.detail: They come from at least three separate origins with different characteristics, which is why they should be weighed separately rather than as one narrative. Kirk's own September 8 message was released by Candace Owens and is a primary document. The refused-Netanyahu-funding and frightened-of-reprisal claims come from The Grayzone on September 12, citing an unnamed Trump insider and longtime friend. The specific fear-of-assassination formulation comes from Harrison H. Smith at Infowars, relaying an unnamed person close to Kirk. Three different publishers, three different sourcing structures, one shared subject. They have circulated as a merged narrative in which the credibility of the primary document is transferred to the other two, which is precisely the transfer this entry exists to prevent.

findings.claim: The fear claim was constructed after the assassination to fit a motive narrative
findings.detail: The timestamp rules this out for the Smith version specifically. His post is dated August 13, 2025, four weeks before Kirk was killed on September 10 and three and a half weeks before Kirk wrote the September 8 message that later became public. Whatever else is true of the claim, it was in circulation before there was an assassination to explain, and before the primary document that retrospective accounts have leaned on existed. This app has repeatedly found that claims in this case escalate after the fact; this particular one did not originate that way, and saying so is required by the same standard applied elsewhere. It does not make the claim true — a contemporaneous anonymous relay is still an anonymous relay — but it removes one specific and commonly offered objection to it.

fact_check_gap: Coverage has tended to treat this cluster as a single question to be accepted or dismissed wholesale, when it is four claims at four different evidentiary tiers. Kirk's own message is a primary document and deserves the weight it carries; the reprisal-fear claim deserves the scepticism due to any uncorroborated anonymous source; the feared-assassination formulation has no source at all; and the bloodline claim is contradicted by ordinary genealogical records that took minutes to locate. Collapsing them together serves whichever side is doing the collapsing.

title: Operational Signature Test: Does This Case Match Documented Israeli Assassination Method?
summary: A falsifiable test rather than a rhetorical one. If Israeli intelligence has a documented operational signature, the Kirk evidence can be measured against it and the hypothesis either fits or it does not. The documented signature turns out to be large, resourced, technically sophisticated teams. The Kirk evidence is the opposite profile on nearly every axis, which is the strongest methodological argument against the hypothesis this app has found — and it comes from taking the premise seriously, not from dismissing it.
sources_quality: A for the Dubai operation, which Dubai police documented publicly in extraordinary detail including CCTV and passport data; A for the Lillehammer case, which produced Norwegian criminal convictions; A for the Aloni quotation, which is an on-record broadcast interview; B for generalising any of it into a 'signature', since intelligence services adapt method to circumstance
key_takeaway: The premise is half right and the half that is right argues against the conclusion. Large multi-operative teams are thoroughly documented: the 2010 Dubai killing of Mahmoud al-Mabhouh involved somewhere between eleven core operatives and roughly twenty-seven who entered the country, with twenty-nine suspects eventually named, using forged passports cloned from several Western nations, a trojan placed on the target's computer, a penetrated email server, weeks of movement study, and duplicated hotel keys. The Lillehammer operation in Norway in 1973 used a team of roughly fifteen. So the 'multiple operatives' element is real and well evidenced. The 'fall guy' element is not. This app located no documented Israeli assassination in which an innocent party was framed as the killer. Lillehammer is the closest superficial match and is actually the opposite case: the team misidentified and killed an innocent Moroccan waiter, Ahmed Bouchikha, then got caught, with six convicted in Norwegian courts — an error producing a wrong victim, not an engineered patsy. The documented false-flag precedent, the 1954 Lavon Affair, involved bombings intended to be blamed on Egyptian factions, which is a different operational category from assassination with a designated culprit. Applied to this case, the signature fits badly. Dubai left roughly two dozen faces on CCTV, cloned passports, and no recovered weapon. The Kirk scene produced one shot, one rifle abandoned in a bush wrapped in a towel carrying the suspect's DNA, one escape route on foot, a screwdriver left on the roof, and a surrender arranged through the suspect's own family. Those are not the same kind of event.

findings.claim: Israeli intelligence assassinations have historically used large multi-operative teams
findings.detail: Well documented and not seriously disputed. The February 2010 killing of Hamas figure Mahmoud al-Mabhouh in Dubai is the canonical case because Dubai police published an unusually complete reconstruction: estimates of the team range from eleven core operatives to roughly twenty-seven entering the country, with twenty-nine suspects eventually named. The operation used passports forged or cloned from several Western countries, a trojan placed on the target's computer, a compromised email server, sustained study of his movements, and duplicated room keys; CCTV recorded four operatives leaving the room. The 1973 Lillehammer operation in Norway used a team of roughly fifteen. Whatever else follows, the premise that these operations are team-based and resource-intensive is correct.

findings.claim: Israeli intelligence assassinations characteristically employ a framed 'fall guy'
findings.detail: This app located no documented Israeli assassination in which an uninvolved person was framed as the killer. The case most often reached for, Lillehammer, is the inverse: the team wrongly identified their target and killed Ahmed Bouchikha, a Moroccan waiter with no connection to Black September, then failed to escape cleanly, with six members convicted in Norwegian courts. That is a lethal misidentification followed by operational failure, not a constructed culprit. The documented Israeli false-flag precedent is the 1954 Lavon Affair, in which Israeli military intelligence ran bombings in Egypt intended to be attributed to local factions — genuine, eventually acknowledged, and a different operational category from an assassination with a designated patsy. The distinction matters because the fall-guy element is the load-bearing part of the argument as applied to this case, and it is the part without documented precedent.

findings.claim: The Kirk evidence matches the documented operational profile
findings.detail: It matches poorly on nearly every axis, and this is the substantive finding. The documented profile is large-team, technically sophisticated, and forensically disciplined: no weapon recovered in Dubai, cloned identities, digital penetration of the target, and an exfiltration completed before the body was found. The Kirk scene presents a single shot from a single position, a bolt-action rifle abandoned nearby in a bush wrapped in a towel bearing the suspect's DNA as the dominant contributor, a screwdriver left on the roof also carrying his DNA, an escape on foot through woods, a vehicle registered in the suspect's own name, engraved cartridges left in the weapon, and a surrender arranged through the suspect's family. An operation conducted to the Dubai standard does not leave the weapon, the DNA, and the registered vehicle behind and then have the alleged operator turn himself in via relatives. If the signature argument is taken seriously as an evidentiary test rather than an association, it points away from state involvement here.

findings.claim: Suspicion of a state's intelligence services based on its documented operational history is inherently antisemitic
findings.detail: It is not, and this app has never treated it as such. Israel demonstrably conducts extraterritorial assassinations; that is a matter of public record including court proceedings in Norway and a published police reconstruction in Dubai. Reasoning from documented state conduct to suspicion of state conduct is ordinary analysis. Every Israel-linked claim in this case has accordingly been tested on its own evidence and refuted, where refuted, on evidence: the HADES aircraft claim by the aircraft's own transponder record placing it 144 miles away in Idaho, the twelve-Israeli-phones claim by its originator's own concession, the Fort Huachuca claim by unrebutted travel records and its amplifier's acknowledgement of possible misidentification. None of those refutations rested on characterising the claim as bigoted. The one place this app has named the template is the assertion that Erika Kirk carries a concealed Rothschild bloodline, which is a genealogical claim about a private individual and was refuted with genealogy — a Swedish paternal grandfather born in Falun, a maternal grandfather born in Pennsylvania to Syrian and Lebanese parents. The template observation followed the factual refutation rather than substituting for it. Bloodline claims about an individual and operational-history claims about a state are different categories and are treated differently here.

findings.claim: A senior Israeli figure has described the antisemitism accusation as a deliberate tactic
findings.detail: Shulamit Aloni, former Israeli Minister of Education and leader of the left-Zionist Meretz party, said exactly that in an on-record Democracy Now interview with Amy Goodman broadcast August 14, 2002, describing it as a trick that is always used, with the Holocaust invoked against European critics and the antisemitism charge against American ones. The quotation is authentic and frequently misattributed in circulation, so the sourcing is worth fixing precisely. Two qualifications belong with it. Aloni was a lifelong human-rights campaigner and a domestic critic making an accusation against the Sharon government, not an official describing policy she administered, so this is a prominent insider's characterisation rather than an institutional admission. And a tactic being real does not make any particular invocation of it dishonest, any more than the existence of false accusations makes all accusations false. Both propositions — that the charge is sometimes deployed to deflect legitimate criticism, and that antisemitism is also a real phenomenon requiring identification — are true simultaneously, and this app applies them that way.

fact_check_gap: The operational-signature argument is made frequently and tested almost never. It is falsifiable in both directions and the documented record supports its first premise while contradicting its application here: the profile that makes Israeli operations recognisable — many operatives, deep technical preparation, no weapon left, clean exfiltration — is close to the inverse of what the Kirk scene produced. Neither those advancing the argument nor those dismissing it appear to have run the comparison.

title: Historical Precedent Audit: King David, USS Liberty, JFK, RFK — What Each Actually Establishes
summary: The four historical cases most often cited to justify suspicion of Israeli involvement in the Kirk killing, each checked against the documentary record and rated for what it does and does not support. Two are documented and do establish real precedent for deception and for lethal action against allies. One points in the opposite direction from how it is usually deployed. One rests on a genuine policy conflict that has never been connected to an assassination by evidence.
sources_quality: A for King David (extensively documented, including by the Irgun's own participants and British inquiry) and for the RFK motive record (Sirhan's own statements, his notebook, trial record); A- for USS Liberty as to the attack itself, with the explanation genuinely contested; B for the JFK-Dimona correspondence, which is declassified but whose interpretation is disputed
key_takeaway: The prior is partly earned and should be stated as such. King David establishes documented false-flag disguise: on July 22, 1946 Irgun operatives dressed as Arabs carried seven milk churns holding roughly 110 pounds of explosives each into the basement of the King David Hotel, destroying the southern wing that housed British Mandate military and government offices and killing 91 people. The operation was led by Menachem Begin, who became Israel's prime minister in 1977. USS Liberty establishes lethal action against an ally with a contested explanation: on June 8, 1967 Israeli aircraft and torpedo boats attacked a US signals-intelligence ship, killing 34 American servicemen and wounding 171, which Israel attributed to misidentification and which many survivors and some US officials have never accepted. Those two are real and they do justify scepticism as a starting posture. The other two do not do the work assigned to them. RFK has a genuine and heavily documented Israel element, but it runs the other way: Sirhan Sirhan was a Palestinian Christian displaced from Jerusalem in 1948 whose stated motive was Kennedy's support for Israel and specifically a pledge of fifty fighter jets, who wrote in his notebook that Kennedy must die by June 5 and who killed him on that date, the first anniversary of the Six-Day War. That is an assassin motivated by opposition to Israel, the inverse of Israeli sponsorship. JFK involves a real and declassified conflict — Kennedy's pressure on Ben-Gurion for inspections of the Dimona reactor — that has never been connected to the assassination by evidence, with the Israeli-involvement thesis resting principally on a single self-published book rather than on the withheld records it invokes.

findings.claim: The King David Hotel bombing involved operatives disguised as Arabs attacking the governing power
findings.detail: Accurate in its essentials. On July 22, 1946 the Irgun carried out the attack with operatives disguised as Arabs transporting seven milk churns, each containing roughly 110 pounds of explosives, into the hotel basement. The southern wing housed the British Mandate's military and government headquarters. Menachem Begin led the operation and became prime minister of Israel in 1977. Three points of precision belong on the record without diminishing the core fact. The Irgun was a Zionist paramilitary organisation and the State of Israel did not exist until 1948, so this is pre-state paramilitary action rather than a state intelligence operation. The target was British; no American facility or personnel were targeted. And of the 91 killed, the largest group was Arab — 41 Arabs, 28 Britons, 17 Jews and 5 others — which matters because the disguise was operational cover rather than an attempt to shift blame onto a party who then suffered the casualties. Begin maintained that three warning calls were placed; a British inquiry concluded no warning reached anyone with authority to order evacuation.

findings.claim: The USS Liberty attack is a documented Israeli attack on Americans with a disputed explanation
findings.detail: On June 8, 1967, during the Six-Day War, Israeli aircraft and torpedo boats attacked the USS Liberty, a United States signals-intelligence vessel, killing 34 American servicemen and wounding 171. Israel attributed the attack to misidentification, apologised and paid compensation. Many survivors, and a number of US officials over the years, have rejected that explanation. This app takes no position on which account is correct; the relevant point for present purposes is that the event is real, the casualties are real, and the official explanation is genuinely contested rather than settled. As a basis for scepticism toward official accounts involving Israeli action against American interests, this is the strongest of the four cases.

findings.claim: The RFK assassination had an Israeli element supporting the sponsorship hypothesis
findings.detail: It had a substantial Israel element that runs precisely opposite to the use it is put to. Sirhan Sirhan was born in Jerusalem in 1944 to a Greek Orthodox Christian family displaced during the 1948 war, resettled in California in 1957. His stated motive, repeated over decades including in a 1989 David Frost interview, was Kennedy's support for Israel and specifically a pledge to supply fifty fighter jets. He wrote in his notebook that Kennedy must die by June 5, and killed him on June 5, 1968, the first anniversary of the Six-Day War. This is an assassin acting from Palestinian nationalist grievance against pro-Israel policy. Citing it as evidence of Israeli involvement inverts the documented record. Separate controversies about that case — the second-gun question, acoustic analysis, Sirhan's hypnosis claims — are genuine disputes but none of them is an Israeli-sponsorship claim.

findings.claim: Withheld JFK records conceal a documented Israeli connection to the assassination
findings.detail: The underlying policy conflict is real and declassified: Kennedy pressed David Ben-Gurion persistently for American inspections of the Dimona reactor, the correspondence is public, and Ben-Gurion resigned in June 1963. That is a genuine and serious dispute between the two governments. The step from there to assassination involvement is not supported by any evidence located. The thesis traces principally to a single self-published book from the 1990s rather than to the records themselves. On the records: the JFK Records Act of 1992 mandated disclosure, with substantial releases in 2017-2018, 2021-2023 and 2025, and some material remains withheld or redacted — which is a legitimate transparency grievance and is not itself evidence of what the withheld material contains. Invoking still-sealed records as proof of a specific claim is unfalsifiable by construction.

findings.claim: These precedents, taken together, support the Israeli-involvement hypothesis in the Kirk case
findings.detail: They support a posture of scepticism, which is legitimate, but they do not support this conclusion, and the reason is the same one identified in this app's operational signature test. Two of the four cases are genuine and establish that deception and lethal action against allies are within the historical repertoire. But precedent establishes capability and willingness, not occurrence in a specific instance, and the Kirk evidence does not match the operational profile those very cases exhibit. King David involved a multi-operative team, weeks of preparation and elaborate cover. Dubai in 2010 involved between eleven and twenty-seven operatives, cloned passports and technical penetration, with no weapon recovered. The Kirk scene produced one shot, a rifle abandoned in a bush wrapped in a towel bearing the suspect's own dominant DNA, a screwdriver on the roof with the same, a vehicle registered in his name, engraved cartridges left in the weapon and a surrender arranged through his family. There is also a decay problem: an eighty-year-old pre-state paramilitary operation and a 1967 wartime incident are weak evidence about the conduct of a different institution in 2025. A prior earned from history still has to survive contact with the evidence in front of it, and here it does not.

findings.claim: This app has assessed 9/11-related claims as part of the Kirk case record
findings.detail: It has not, deliberately, and that boundary is maintained here. Earlier in this project's research 9/11 material was examined at the user's request and explicitly excluded from the case dataset as not bearing on the Kirk evidence. The reasoning is unchanged: the Kirk case is assessed on the Kirk evidence, and importing a separate and vastly larger contested event as background would substitute association for analysis. The one narrow factual point worth recording, because it recurs in this context, is that five men employed by a New Jersey moving company were detained on September 11, 2001, held for weeks and deported without charges related to the attacks — documented, and not evidence about Utah in 2025.

fact_check_gap: These four cases are almost always cited as an undifferentiated bloc, and they are not equivalent. Two are documented and genuinely probative of capability. One is documented and points the opposite way from how it is used. One rests on a real policy conflict plus an appeal to sealed records that cannot be falsified. Anyone making or rebutting the argument benefits from separating them, and this app located no analysis on either side that does.

title: Whereabouts Audit: Where Five Named Figures Actually Were, September 8-10, 2025
summary: An attempt to independently establish the documented locations of Brian Harpole, Erika Kirk, Andrew Kolvet, Blake Neff and Ben Shapiro across the window Mitch Snow's Fort Huachuca allegation concerns. The result is mostly negative, and the negative result is the finding: for four of the five, no independent public record of their September 8-9 movements exists at all. That is unremarkable for private citizens and it is also why allegations about those days are so difficult to settle in either direction.
sources_quality: B for Harpole, whose Dallas location on September 9 rests on travel records described in his own federal complaint rather than on documents this app has examined; A- for the September 12 studio gathering, which is confirmed by a participant's contemporaneous public post; D for everything else, which is absence of record rather than evidence
key_takeaway: Only one of the five has any asserted documentary alibi for the relevant dates, and it belongs to the person the allegation names. Brian Harpole's federal defamation complaint states travel records place him in Dallas, Texas on September 9, not at Fort Huachuca, and reporting indicates Candace Owens had access to those records and dismissed them on the ground that they did not cover the period after the alleged meeting ended — an argument about the window the records cover rather than a claim they are false. Harpole was on the ground with the security team at UVU on September 10; he formed Rockhouse Integrity Group in 2023 and held the TPUSA event security contract. For Erika Kirk, Andrew Kolvet, Blake Neff and Ben Shapiro, this app located no independent public record of where any of them was on September 8 or 9. Kolvet and Neff are firmly placed only from September 12, when Kolvet posted publicly that he, Jack Posobiec, Tyler Bowyer and Neff were together in Kirk's studio for the first show after the killing. The absence matters in a specific way: allegations about these dates cannot be confirmed OR refuted from the public record, which is the condition that lets them persist regardless of merit.

findings.claim: Brian Harpole has an asserted documentary alibi for September 9
findings.detail: His complaint in Harpole v. Owens et al states that travel records place him in Dallas, Texas on September 9, and characterises the Fort Huachuca allegation as fabricated. Reporting on the filing indicates Owens had access to those records and dismissed them because, in her account, they did not establish his location for the period after the alleged meeting concluded. That is a dispute about coverage of a time window, not an assertion that the records are forged or that he was in Arizona. This app has not examined the records themselves; they are described in a pleading, which is an allegation rather than a finding. Harpole is independently documented on the ground with the security team at UVU on September 10.

findings.claim: Independent public records establish Erika Kirk's location on September 8 or 9
findings.detail: None were located. Her documented public timeline begins after the killing: escorting her husband's casket to Arizona aboard Air Force Two with Vice President and Second Lady Vance on September 11, and her first public statement on September 12. The only artefact ever offered for the earlier window is the photograph Gary Melton displayed on air, which this app has already examined in detail and found unable to bear the weight placed on it — it is dated September 9 at 8:33 a.m. while Snow's allegation concerns the evening of September 8, Erika is apparently not visible in it, one of the children was acknowledged not to be her son, and what was described as metadata was a date displayed on a phone screen rather than forensic EXIF. Refuting a bad alibi photograph is not the same as establishing a timeline, and no adequate one exists publicly.

findings.claim: Andrew Kolvet and Blake Neff can be placed during the September 8-9 window
findings.detail: They cannot, from anything public. Both are firmly documented only from September 12, when Kolvet posted contemporaneously that he was in Kirk's studio with Jack Posobiec, Tyler Bowyer and Neff for the first broadcast after the killing, with Kirk's chair left empty. Both continued appearing on the programme through the following weeks. Kolvet's role in the case record is otherwise substantial and already documented elsewhere in this app — he is the single relayed source for the unnamed surgeon's bone-density account, he supplied Melton the Fort Huachuca photograph, and he is one side of the four mutually exclusive factual conflicts with Owens logged at X31. None of that establishes where he was on September 8.

findings.claim: Ben Shapiro's location during the window is documented
findings.detail: Nothing specific to those dates was located. The Daily Wire is headquartered in Nashville and Shapiro is based there, which is background rather than evidence of location on any particular day. His documented involvement in this case is post-event and financial or rhetorical rather than locational: the announcement that The Daily Wire would donate $1 million to TPUSA after the killing, and the Chabad and Carlson disputes already assessed in this app. No claim locating him near the relevant events on September 8-10 has been advanced by any source reviewed, and none is supported.

findings.claim: The absence of public whereabouts records is itself suspicious
findings.detail: It is the normal condition. Private citizens, including well-known ones, do not generate a public record of their daily movements, and the expectation that they should is what makes unfalsifiable allegations about specific dates durable. The asymmetry worth naming is that the burden sits with the person making a positive claim about someone's location, not with the person asked to prove a negative about their own movements weeks earlier. In this instance only one party has produced anything documentary at all, and it is Harpole, the person the allegation names. That is the opposite of the pattern the allegation would predict.

title: Is 1Ten LLC a Real Company? Ownership, Address, and the Operator's Record
summary: A direct look at the vendor itself rather than at the payments. Ownership is now confirmed from a primary document — Arizona state senator Jake Hoffman's own sworn financial disclosure, which lists him as owner of 1TEN LLC. The picture that emerges is neither a fabricated shell nor a conventional agency: a real operating vendor with an unusually thin physical footprint, run by a sitting legislator with a documented platform ban for inauthentic political activity conducted on behalf of the same organisation now paying him.
sources_quality: A for ownership and address, taken from Hoffman's filed Arizona Secretary of State financial disclosure; A for the payment records already established from IRS, FEC and Arizona filings; A- for the Rally Forge platform ban, which was announced publicly by the platform and covered contemporaneously; C for the walked-the-strip-mall reporting, which is secondary and not independently verified here
key_takeaway: Ownership is settled. Hoffman's own sworn disclosure names him as owner of 1TEN LLC at 18521 E Queen Creek Rd, STE 105-503, Queen Creek, and separately as President and CEO of Rally Forge LLC at the identical suite, alongside further entities including Forged Communications. That resolves the question this app previously left open on whether the Hoffman connection was verified — it is, from a primary document, not from reporting. Three things follow. The company is real in the sense that matters legally: it is disclosed, it invoices, it is named on public filings across three record systems, and its service line is consistent throughout. It is thin in physical presence: no website, a mailbox suite shared with multiple affiliated entities, and reporting that a walk of the strip mall at that address found ordinary retail tenants and no 1Ten office. And the operator has a specific documented history — in October 2020 Facebook banned Rally Forge, Hoffman's firm, for coordinated inauthentic behaviour carried out on behalf of Turning Point Action, involving paid teenagers posting scripted political comments through fake accounts. That is the same client relationship that later produced the payments this app has traced. It does not establish that any specific payment was improper, and none of the filings reviewed show anything unlawful on their face. It does mean the vendor is not an arms-length stranger to the organisation paying it.

findings.claim: Jake Hoffman's ownership of 1Ten LLC is confirmed by primary document
findings.detail: His Arizona Secretary of State financial disclosure statement, filed in his capacity as a state senator, lists 1TEN LLC at 18521 E Queen Creek Rd, STE 105-503, Queen Creek, AZ 85142, with Hoffman as owner, and separately lists Rally Forge LLC at the same suite with Hoffman as President and CEO, described as marketing, advertising and communications services. Forged Communications appears alongside them. This app previously recorded the ownership as reported but unverified; it is now verified from a sworn public filing rather than from secondary coverage. Note the address: the disclosure gives 18521, matching the IRS Form 990 filings, while the Arizona campaign finance reports give 18251 — confirming that the state campaign filings carry the transposition error, not the federal ones.

findings.claim: 1Ten LLC is a fabricated entity that does no actual work
findings.detail: The evidence does not support that, and it is worth saying plainly given how the claim circulates. The company is named on public filings across three independent record systems over five years: IRS Form 990 contractor schedules for Turning Point Action across four consecutive tax years, FEC Schedule B disbursements across 86 itemised records and multiple committees, and Arizona Secretary of State campaign finance reports for at least four separate committees. The service descriptions are specific and consistent throughout — social and digital media, ad placement, television, radio, printing, and peer-to-peer texting — and the Arizona filings itemise individual expenditures down to named candidate slates. A fabricated entity does not generate that documentary trail, and does not bill the Arizona Republican Party, a county party committee, Moms for Liberty and multiple individual campaigns.

findings.claim: The company has a normal physical business presence
findings.detail: It does not. There is no website. The address is a suite number at a location reported to be a strip mall, with the suite designation 105-503 consistent with a mailbox rather than a leased office, and Hoffman's own disclosure places several distinct entities at that identical suite. Reporting describes an investigator walking the strip mall and finding ordinary retail tenants but no 1Ten premises; this app has not independently verified that walk-through. None of this is unlawful or even unusual for a small communications firm operating remotely, and mailbox registration is common and legitimate. It is recorded because a company receiving millions in political spending with no public-facing presence is a fair transparency observation, and because the mailbox detail is the specific factual claim this app previously mishandled by checking only federal filings.

findings.claim: The operator has a documented history of inauthentic political activity for the same client
findings.detail: This is the most substantive finding and it has not appeared in coverage of the payment dispute. In October 2020 Facebook banned Rally Forge — Hoffman's firm, listed at the same suite as 1Ten on his own disclosure — for coordinated inauthentic behaviour. The operation was conducted on behalf of Turning Point Action and involved recruiting and paying teenagers to post scripted political comments through fake accounts. Facebook removed 200 Facebook accounts, 55 Pages and 76 Instagram accounts; reporting indicated the network had accumulated over 400,000 likes and that roughly $1 million in advertising had been placed. Hoffman was also suspended by Twitter at the time. The relevance here is precise and limited: the same operator, for the same client organisation, has previously been sanctioned by a platform for misrepresenting the authenticity of paid political messaging. That is context for evaluating later payments for social and digital media services from the same client. It is not evidence that any specific later payment was improper, and nothing in the filings reviewed is unlawful on its face.

findings.claim: The relationship between payer and vendor is arms-length
findings.detail: Not in any ordinary sense, though it may still be lawful. Hoffman is a former Turning Point USA spokesperson; his firm ran the 2020 operation on behalf of Turning Point Action; and Turning Point entities subsequently became among the largest disclosed payers to his company. Turning Point Action separately maintains a legislative scorecard page for Hoffman as a sitting senator. This app has separately documented that TPUSA's own chief financial officer, Justin Olson, ran a Senate campaign that also paid 1Ten, and that Turning Point Action's independent expenditures through 1Ten benefited a slate including Austin Smith, himself a Turning Point Action figure and Arizona state representative. Whether any of this required Schedule L related-party disclosure turns on tax definitions this app has not resolved, and a former spokesperson is not automatically an interested person. But the network is dense enough that describing these as ordinary vendor transactions understates the relationship.

findings.claim: Anything located here establishes misuse of funds
findings.detail: No. Nothing in the IRS, FEC or Arizona filings reviewed is unlawful on its face. Political organisations routinely hire ideologically aligned vendors, mailbox registration is legal, remote firms without websites exist, and every payment traced was disclosed where disclosure was required. What the record establishes is a real, disclosed, consistently-described vendor with a thin physical footprint, owned by a sitting legislator with a prior platform sanction for inauthentic activity on behalf of the same client, receiving substantial sums across federal, state and nonprofit channels. Whether the amounts represent fair value for services delivered cannot be determined from filings, which record what was paid and for what category, not what was produced. That question requires records no public disclosure contains.

fact_check_gap: The 2020 Rally Forge platform ban is directly relevant to a dispute about payments for social and digital media services, involves the same operator and the same client organisation, and appears in none of the coverage of the 1Ten payments on either side. Equally, Hoffman's own sworn financial disclosure — which settles the ownership question outright and shows multiple affiliated entities sharing one mailbox suite — is a public document that neither those making the allegation nor those rebutting it appear to have retrieved.

title: Jake Hoffman: The Vendor's Owner, His Public Record, and the Turning Point Overlap
summary: A record audit of the sitting Arizona state senator who owns 1Ten LLC, the vendor at the centre of the Turning Point payment thread. Three things are documented and each is independently significant: a platform ban of his firm for inauthentic political activity conducted for Turning Point Action, a felony indictment in the Arizona fake-electors case that was dismissed without prejudice in 2026, and a co-defendant list that includes Turning Point Action's own chief operating officer.
sources_quality: A for his offices and business holdings (Arizona Senate Republicans caucus page, his filed Secretary of State financial disclosure, legislative records); A for the indictment and its dismissal (grand jury indictment, court rulings, wire coverage); A- for the 2020 platform enforcement, announced by the platform and covered contemporaneously
key_takeaway: Hoffman is an Arizona state senator for Legislative District 15, in office since 2023, chairman of the Arizona Freedom Caucus since its founding in 2022, chairman of the Senate committees on Executive Nominations and on Government, and vice chairman of Appropriations. Before the Senate he served on the Higley School Board, the Queen Creek Town Council, as chairman of a large county Republican organisation, and in the Arizona House. He is a former Turning Point USA spokesperson. He is also, per his own sworn financial disclosure, owner of 1TEN LLC and President and CEO of Rally Forge LLC, both at the same Queen Creek suite. Two entries on his record bear directly on the payment thread this app has been tracing. In October 2020 Facebook banned Rally Forge for coordinated inauthentic behaviour conducted on behalf of Turning Point Action, an operation using paid teenagers posting through fake accounts, which cost 200 Facebook accounts, 55 Pages and 76 Instagram accounts. In April 2024 a state grand jury indicted him on nine felony counts in the Arizona fake-electors case; he pleaded not guilty, retained his committee assignments, and was named to an RNC position days after the indictment. That case was dismissed in 2026 after defence counsel successfully argued the grand jury had not been shown relevant certification law, and the Arizona Supreme Court declined to revive it — but the dismissal was expressly WITHOUT prejudice, and Attorney General Kris Mayes has stated she will return to a grand jury. He has been convicted of nothing.

findings.claim: Hoffman holds senior positions in Arizona state government
findings.detail: Arizona state senator for Legislative District 15 since 2023. Chairman of the Senate Committee on Executive Nominations and the Committee on Government, and vice chairman of the Committee on Appropriations. Founding chairman of the Arizona Freedom Caucus since 2022. Prior offices include the Higley School Board, the Queen Creek Town Council, chairmanship of one of Arizona's larger county Republican organisations, and the Arizona House of Representatives. Education: bachelor's degree from Arizona State University in 2008, with graduate study at Northwest Christian University and Bushnell University. The Executive Nominations chairmanship is worth noting on its own — it is the committee through which gubernatorial appointments pass.

findings.claim: Hoffman's firm was sanctioned by a platform for inauthentic activity on behalf of Turning Point Action
findings.detail: In October 2020 Facebook banned Rally Forge, of which Hoffman is President and CEO per his own disclosure, for coordinated inauthentic behaviour. The operation was carried out on behalf of Turning Point Action and involved recruiting and paying teenagers to post scripted political comments through accounts that misrepresented their origin. Facebook removed 200 Facebook accounts, 55 Pages and 76 Instagram accounts; reporting indicated the network had accumulated more than 400,000 likes and that roughly $1 million in advertising had been placed. Hoffman was separately suspended by Twitter. This matters here for a narrow reason: it is the same operator and the same client organisation that later produced the payments to 1Ten traced across IRS, FEC and Arizona filings in this app, for services in the same category.

findings.claim: Hoffman is currently under felony indictment
findings.detail: He is not, as of August 2026, and precision matters here. On April 24, 2024 an Arizona state grand jury indicted him on nine felony counts — forgery, fraud and conspiracy — arising from his signing of a December 2020 document purporting to certify him as one of Arizona's presidential electors and awarding the state's votes to Donald Trump, who had lost Arizona by more than 10,000 votes. He pleaded not guilty in June 2024. In 2026 the case was dismissed after defence counsel successfully argued the grand jury had not been presented the relevant provisions of the law governing certification of presidential contests, and the Arizona Supreme Court declined to revive it. Critically, the judge rejected defence requests to dismiss WITH prejudice, and Attorney General Kris Mayes has stated she intends to seek a fresh indictment. So: charged, pleaded not guilty, charges dismissed on a procedural defect, potentially revivable, never tried, convicted of nothing.

findings.claim: The indictment carried professional consequences for him
findings.detail: It did not, and the sequence is documented. He retained his Senate committee assignments following the indictment. Within days of it he was named to a Republican National Committee position. He remains a committee chairman. Whatever one concludes about the merits of the now-dismissed charges, the institutional response was continuity rather than distancing, which is itself part of the record.

findings.claim: The fake-electors co-defendants include people who also appear in the Kirk case record
findings.detail: They do, and this is the connection that makes his record case-relevant rather than merely adjacent. Among the eighteen indicted alongside Hoffman was Tyler Bowyer, chief operating officer of Turning Point Action. Bowyer appears independently in this app's record: Andrew Kolvet's contemporaneous post of September 12, 2025 places Bowyer with Kolvet, Jack Posobiec and Blake Neff in Charlie Kirk's studio for the first broadcast after the killing. Other co-defendants included then-state senator Anthony Kern — whose campaign committee 'Vote Kern' was among those benefiting from Turning Point Action independent expenditures placed through 1Ten, per the Arizona filings reviewed here — along with then-AZGOP chairwoman Kelli Ward, Rudy Giuliani and Mark Meadows. The overlap between the Turning Point operational leadership, the elector defendants, and the vendor network is dense and documented.

findings.claim: Anything in Hoffman's record establishes involvement in or knowledge of the Kirk killing
findings.detail: Nothing does, and no source reviewed alleges it. His relevance to this app is confined to a single thread: he owns the company that received substantial disclosed payments from Turning Point entities, which is why his record was examined at all. There is no evidence connecting him to the events of September 10, 2025, no claim placing him in Utah, and no allegation by any party linking him to the case. The findings above are recorded because a vendor's ownership and the owner's documented conduct history are legitimate inputs when assessing whether payments to that vendor were ordinary commerce — and for no wider purpose.

title: The Arizona Fake-Electors Co-Defendants: Full Roster, and Which Ones Actually Touch This Case
summary: The complete list of the eighteen people indicted alongside Jake Hoffman, with relevance to the Kirk case graded honestly rather than implied by inclusion. Three of the eighteen connect to the Turning Point network this app has been tracing. The other fifteen do not connect to the Kirk case at all, and saying so is the point of listing them.
sources_quality: A for the roster, charges and procedural history (Maricopa County grand jury indictment, court rulings, wire and Arizona outlet coverage); A for the pardon and its legal effect, which the Attorney General's office addressed directly
key_takeaway: On April 24, 2024 a Maricopa County grand jury indicted eighteen people: eleven who signed the elector document and seven Trump advisers and attorneys. The eleven electors were Turning Point Action COO and RNC committeeman Tyler Bowyer, electors chair Nancy Cottle, state senator Jake Hoffman, state senator Anthony Kern, 2022 Senate candidate Jim Lamon, former Cochise County GOP chair Robert Montgomery, former Gila County GOP official Samuel Moorhead, electors co-chair Loraine Pellegrino, former Arizona GOP executive director Greg Safsten, former Arizona GOP chair Kelli Ward, and Michael Ward. The seven others were Christina Bobb, John Eastman, Jenna Ellis, Boris Epshteyn, Rudy Giuliani, Mark Meadows and Michael Roman. Each elector faced nine counts: one conspiracy, two fraudulent-schemes counts, and six forgery counts. Two procedural facts are widely misreported. Trump issued federal pardons to all eighteen on November 10, 2025, but a president can pardon only federal offences and these were state charges — the Attorney General's office stated the pardons would have no impact on the state case. And the case's 2026 dismissal was without prejudice on a grand-jury instruction defect, not an acquittal. Nobody has been convicted in this case. Of the eighteen, only three have any connection to the Kirk case record, and the connection is institutional rather than evidentiary.

findings.claim: Tyler Bowyer is the co-defendant with the most direct connection to the Kirk case record
findings.detail: He is chief operating officer of Turning Point Action and a Republican National Committeeman, and has described himself as the person who essentially runs the organisation's operations. He appears independently in this app's record: Andrew Kolvet's contemporaneous post of September 12, 2025 places Bowyer with Kolvet, Jack Posobiec and Blake Neff in Charlie Kirk's studio for the first broadcast after the killing, with Kirk's chair left empty. Separately, Turning Point sued the Arizona Attorney General seeking to quash a warrant for three months of Bowyer's emails after a judge granted it — the organisation litigating to protect its COO's communications from an election-fraud investigation. That is an institutional relationship between the organisation and a defendant, not evidence about the Kirk shooting, and nothing connects Bowyer to the events of September 10, 2025.

findings.claim: Anthony Kern's connection runs through the vendor network this app has traced
findings.detail: Kern was an Arizona state senator at the time of indictment. His relevance here is specific and documentary: Arizona Secretary of State campaign finance filings reviewed by this app show Turning Point Action independent expenditures placed through 1Ten LLC benefiting the committee 'Vote Kern', among a slate of other Arizona candidates. So the vendor owned by one co-defendant, Hoffman, placed political spending benefiting another co-defendant, Kern, on behalf of the organisation employing a third, Bowyer. That is a documented three-way overlap within a single filing system. It bears on how tightly connected this network is; it says nothing about the Kirk case.

findings.claim: Kelli Ward's role is institutional rather than case-connected
findings.detail: Ward was chair of the Arizona Republican Party and a two-time U.S. Senate candidate; her husband Michael Ward was also among the eleven electors. The Arizona Republican Party appears in this app's financial research as a payer to 1Ten LLC — $300,680.71 through its federal account per FEC records, plus state-account payments documented in its own Arizona filings including a $75,000 entry. That places the state party she led among the vendor's clients. She has no documented connection to the Kirk case.

findings.claim: The remaining fifteen co-defendants connect to the Kirk case
findings.detail: They do not, and this finding exists to prevent guilt-by-roster. Nancy Cottle, Jim Lamon, Robert Montgomery, Samuel Moorhead, Loraine Pellegrino, Greg Safsten and Michael Ward were Arizona Republican figures who signed the elector document. Christina Bobb, John Eastman, Jenna Ellis, Boris Epshteyn, Rudy Giuliani, Mark Meadows and Michael Roman were national Trump advisers and attorneys. None has any documented link to Charlie Kirk's death, to Utah, to Tyler Robinson, or to any evidentiary question in this case. Charges against Jim Lamon were separately dropped before the wider dismissal. They are listed here for completeness because an incomplete roster invites speculation, not because their inclusion implies relevance.

findings.claim: Trump's pardons resolved the Arizona charges
findings.detail: They did not, and this is the most consistently misreported element. On November 10, 2025 Trump issued federal pardons covering all eighteen defendants. The presidential pardon power reaches federal offences only; these were Arizona state charges brought by a state grand jury. A spokesperson for Attorney General Kris Mayes stated directly that the pardons would have no impact on the state's case. The pardons were issued while Mayes faced a court-ordered deadline of November 21 to revive or abandon the prosecution following earlier appellate setbacks.

findings.claim: The case ended in acquittal or exoneration
findings.detail: It ended in dismissal without prejudice. Defence counsel successfully argued that the grand jury had not been shown relevant provisions of the law governing certification of presidential contests; the Arizona Supreme Court declined to revive the case on appeal; and the trial judge dismissed while expressly refusing defence requests to dismiss with prejudice, leaving the Attorney General free to seek a fresh indictment. No defendant in the Arizona case has been tried or convicted. Precision matters in both directions here: 'charges dismissed on a procedural defect, revivable' is neither 'convicted' nor 'cleared'.

findings.claim: This roster establishes anything about the Kirk case
findings.detail: It does not, and the honest summary is narrow. What the roster establishes is that the owner of a Turning Point vendor, the chief operating officer of Turning Point Action, and a candidate whose committee received spending placed through that vendor were co-defendants in the same state prosecution. That is a real, documented, institutional density worth recording in an app that traces the organisation's financial and personnel networks. It is not evidence about a shooting in Utah in 2025, no source alleges that it is, and treating an unrelated election-law prosecution as background for a homicide would be exactly the association-over-analysis error this app has refused elsewhere.

timeline_sequence.event: Eleven Arizona Republicans sign a document declaring themselves the state's duly elected presidential electors, awarding Arizona to Trump despite his loss by over 10,000 votes
Facebook bans Rally Forge, Hoffman's firm, for coordinated inauthentic behaviour on behalf of Turning Point Action
Maricopa County grand jury indicts 18 — eleven electors on nine counts each, plus seven Trump advisers and attorneys
Hoffman retains Senate committee assignments and is named to an RNC position
Hoffman pleads not guilty
Charges against Jim Lamon dropped; Turning Point sues the Arizona Attorney General to quash a warrant for three months of Bowyer's emails
Trump issues federal pardons to all 18; AG's office states they have no impact on the state case, as only federal offences can be pardoned
Court-ordered deadline for Mayes to revive or abandon the prosecution
Case dismissed without prejudice on grand-jury instruction defect after the Arizona Supreme Court declines to revive it; AG states intent to re-present
Separately: Kolvet posts that he, Bowyer, Posobiec and Neff are together in Kirk's studio for the first broadcast after the killing

fact_check_gap: Two things go consistently unreported. The federal pardons cannot reach state charges, yet were widely covered as though they ended the Arizona matter; and the dismissal was without prejudice on a procedural defect, not a vindication. Separately, no coverage located connects the vendor thread to the defendant roster — that Hoffman owns the company, Bowyer runs the organisation that is its largest client, and Kern's committee received spending placed through it, all three being co-defendants in the same case.
