title: Tyler Bowyer: Operational Control, the Succession Claim, and a Warrant Turning Point Fought
summary: The Turning Point Action chief operating officer is the single individual who sits at the intersection of almost every institutional thread this app has traced: the vendor network, the fake-electors prosecution, the studio in the days after the killing, and the succession that installed Erika Kirk. He is also the named public source for the load-bearing claim in this app's existing succession contradiction, which had not previously been attributed.
sources_quality: A for his offices, the indictment and the warrant litigation (organisational bios, grand jury indictment, court filings, Phoenix New Times); A- for his September 2025 public statements and the studio gathering, which rest on contemporaneous posts; D for several biographical claims circulating on content-farm sites, which are excluded; A for the FY2025 Form 990 officer/compensation data, pulled directly from ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer (IRS-sourced, not a secondary characterization)
key_takeaway: Bowyer met Charlie Kirk in 2014 while chairing the Maricopa County Republican Committee, joined Turning Point the following year, and rose to chief operating officer of Turning Point Action, the political arm. He is also a Republican National Committeeman and was appointed to Arizona's Board of Regents by Governor Jan Brewer. He has described himself as effectively running the organisation's operations. Four documented facts make him case-relevant. He was one of the eleven indicted electors, facing the same nine counts as Jake Hoffman. Turning Point litigated against the Arizona Attorney General to quash a warrant for three months of his emails — the organisation spending resources to shield its COO's communications from an election-fraud investigation. Andrew Kolvet's post of September 12, 2025 places him in Kirk's studio with Kolvet, Posobiec and Blake Neff for the first broadcast after the killing. And most significantly for this app's existing record, he is the named public voice asserting that Erika Kirk's succession was what Charlie Kirk wanted, stating on social media that this was what Charlie hoped for and had said so numerous times. This app's contradiction X32 logs that succession dispute without identifying who advanced the claim; it was Bowyer, and the attribution matters because he is simultaneously the organisation's operational head and a criminal co-defendant of the vendor owner.

findings.claim: Bowyer is the named source for the succession claim logged at contradiction X32
findings.detail: This app's X32 records the dispute over whether Charlie Kirk personally intended Erika Kirk to succeed him, with the board voting unanimously eight days after the shooting and Candace Owens publicly challenging the evidentiary basis. What X32 did not record is who publicly asserted Kirk's intent. It was Bowyer, who stated on social media that the succession was what Charlie hoped for and wanted and that he had said so numerous times. That attribution changes how the claim should be weighed. It is a first-person assertion from the organisation's chief operating officer, who by his own description runs its operations and who had known Kirk for more than a decade — which makes him unusually well placed to know, and also an interested party in the outcome. It is not a document, and no contemporaneous written instrument has been produced. Reporting that he was instrumental in implementing the succession plan appears on content-farm sites without sourcing and is not credited here.

findings.claim: Bowyer's institutional position is peripheral
findings.detail: He is central by every available measure. Chief operating officer of Turning Point Action; a Republican National Committeeman; formerly chairman of the Maricopa County Republican Committee, one of the largest county party organisations in the country; a gubernatorial appointee to Arizona's Board of Regents under Jan Brewer; and involved in advisory roles for allied student-mobilisation groups. He joined Turning Point in 2015, the year after meeting Kirk, and has been in senior management since. Sources differ on whether the COO title dates from 2017 at Turning Point USA or 2023 at Turning Point Action, which may reflect movement between the affiliated entities rather than a conflict.

findings.claim: Turning Point took legal action to protect Bowyer's communications from investigators
findings.detail: After a judge granted the Arizona Attorney General a warrant for three months of Bowyer's emails in connection with the fake-electors investigation, Turning Point sued the Attorney General seeking to quash it. That is the organisation itself, not merely Bowyer personally, expending legal resources to prevent investigators obtaining its chief operating officer's communications. Nothing about resisting a warrant is improper — challenging the scope of compelled disclosure is ordinary litigation and often succeeds on legitimate grounds. It is recorded because it establishes that the organisation treated Bowyer's exposure as an institutional matter rather than a personal one.

findings.claim: Bowyer's criminal exposure has been resolved
findings.detail: Not conclusively. He was among the eleven electors indicted on April 24, 2024, facing nine counts: one conspiracy, two fraudulent-schemes counts and six forgery counts, arising from signing the December 2020 document declaring the signatories Arizona's duly elected presidential electors. Trump's federal pardons of November 10, 2025 do not reach Arizona state charges, and the Attorney General's office said so directly. The 2026 dismissal was without prejudice on a grand-jury instruction defect, with the judge refusing to dismiss with prejudice and the Attorney General stating intent to seek a fresh indictment. He has not been tried and has not been convicted.

findings.claim: Bowyer connects to the vendor payments this app has traced
findings.detail: Institutionally rather than personally. He is the operational head of Turning Point Action, the entity whose IRS Form 990 contractor schedules disclose $2,418,676 to 1Ten LLC across TY2021-TY2024, and whose Arizona independent expenditures placed through 1Ten benefited a slate including co-defendant Anthony Kern's committee. The vendor is owned by his co-defendant Jake Hoffman, and Hoffman's other firm, Rally Forge, was banned by Facebook in 2020 for coordinated inauthentic behaviour conducted on behalf of Turning Point Action — the entity Bowyer runs. No source reviewed alleges Bowyer personally directed or benefited from any specific payment, and none of the filings show anything unlawful on their face. What is documented is that he heads the organisation at the centre of the vendor relationship.

findings.claim: Anything documented about Bowyer bears on the Kirk shooting
findings.detail: Nothing does. No source alleges any involvement, no claim places him in Utah, and his only appearance in the case timeline is the September 12 studio gathering two days after the killing, alongside three colleagues, for a memorial broadcast. He publicly remembered Kirk as a friend of more than a decade. The findings above concern organisational governance, an unrelated election-law prosecution, and a vendor relationship. They are recorded because this app maps Turning Point's financial and personnel networks and he is the densest single node in that map — not because any of it constitutes evidence about a homicide.

findings.claim: Bowyer still holds a formal officer position at Turning Point USA itself (the 501(c)(3), as distinct from Turning Point Action, the political arm)
findings.detail: TPUSA's own most recent Form 990 (fiscal year ending June 30, 2025, filed May 15, 2026, pulled directly from ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer) lists him as 'Former Assistant Secretary' — a formal TPUSA officer position he no longer holds. The departure predates Kirk's death: the fiscal year covered ends three months before the September 10, 2025 shooting, so this is not part of any post-death restructuring. The same filing nonetheless reports $369,913 in compensation paid to him by a related organization during that fiscal year — current, not deferred, compensation, just routed through an affiliated entity rather than TPUSA itself. This does not contradict his documented, continuing role as Turning Point Action's chief operating officer elsewhere in this entry; TPUSA and Turning Point Action are related but legally distinct filers, and the $369,913 most plausibly reflects Action-side compensation disclosed on TPUSA's related-party schedule rather than a TPUSA-specific severance payment. The filing's full current officer and director list, for the record: John McGovern and Hutz Hertzberg (Managers), Daniel Flood (Manager), Marina Minas (Manager), Justin Olson (Assistant Treasurer/CFO), Tom Sodeika (Secretary & Treasurer), Doug DeGroote (Director), Mike Miller (Director), David Englehardt (Director), and Frank Carni II (Assistant Secretary). Erika Kirk does not appear on this filing, because it covers a fiscal year that ended before Charlie Kirk's death; any 990 reflecting her board chairmanship will not be due until roughly May 2027.

That combination of roles is documented and has gone unremarked.

title: Material Supplied to Commentators: The Kolvet-Melton Channel, and Whether It Recurred
summary: One documented instance of a senior TPUSA communications figure privately supplying purported alibi material to an outside commentator, never publicly explained. A second suspected instance around the August 14, 2026 Owens-Wilson debate, which this app cannot establish and which has a mundane alternative explanation worth testing first.
sources_quality: A- for the Kolvet-Melton supply, which this app documented from the livestream in which Melton displayed the material and acknowledged its origin; C for the Owens-Wilson debate, which occurred three days before this entry and where sourcing is still thin and largely commentary rather than reporting
key_takeaway: The first instance is real and this app has carried it since the Fort Huachuca work. Andrew Kolvet, TPUSA spokesperson, privately supplied Gary Melton with a photograph presented as proof Erika Kirk was with her children on the morning of September 9. Melton displayed it on a livestream, immediately realised he had shown material apparently not intended for release, and apologised on air. The photograph then collapsed on examination: it was dated the wrong day for the allegation it was meant to rebut, Erika was apparently not visible in it, one child was acknowledged not to be her son, and what was described as metadata was a date on a phone screen rather than forensic EXIF. Kolvet has never publicly explained why the organisation's communications lead was routing purported evidence to a YouTube commentator rather than releasing it institutionally, and no source reviewed has asked him. The question is legitimate: material distributed that way carries no organisational accountability, and if it fails, the organisation has not formally asserted anything. On the suspected repeat, this app cannot get there. Andrew Wilson displayed Robinson's messages during the August 14, 2026 debate and said the defence was not contesting their authenticity — but substantial portions of that text thread have been public since July 9, 2026, when they were shown in open court and published as hearing exhibits, including by ABC4. Publicly available exhibits are the ordinary explanation and must be excluded before an insider channel is inferred.

findings.claim: A senior TPUSA communications figure privately supplied purported alibi material to an outside commentator
findings.detail: Documented in this app's Fort Huachuca work. Andrew Kolvet, TPUSA's spokesperson, supplied Gary Melton (Paramount Tactical) with a photograph presented as proof Erika Kirk was with her children on the morning of September 9, 2025. Melton displayed it during a livestream, realised on air that he had shown material apparently not meant for public release, and apologised — the transcript preserves the moment. The material did not survive scrutiny: it was timestamped September 9 at 8:33 a.m. while the allegation concerned the evening of September 8, Erika was apparently not visible in it, Melton later acknowledged one child was not her son, and the claimed metadata was a date displayed on a phone screen rather than original file EXIF.

findings.claim: The reason for supplying it that way has been explained
findings.detail: It has not, by anyone. No public explanation from Kolvet, TPUSA, or Melton addresses why purported exculpatory material went to an independent commentator privately rather than being released by the organisation, and no source reviewed has put the question to him. The available explanations span a wide range and this app has no basis to choose between them. Ordinary press practice would cover it: organisations routinely brief friendly commentators informally, and a spokesperson passing a photo to a sympathetic YouTuber during a crisis is unremarkable in itself. The structural feature worth naming is that material distributed this way carries no institutional accountability — if it fails, as this did, the organisation has formally asserted nothing and can distance itself from the commentator. That asymmetry exists whether or not anyone intended it, and it is the reason the question deserves an answer rather than an assumption.

findings.claim: The same channel demonstrably operated again for the August 2026 Owens-Wilson debate
findings.detail: This app cannot establish it, and the ordinary explanation has not been excluded. Andrew Wilson displayed Robinson's messages during the debate on August 14, 2026 and stated that the defence was not contesting their authenticity. But large portions of that text thread entered the public domain on July 9, 2026, when they were shown in open court on day four of the preliminary hearing and published as exhibits — this app has itself retrieved and examined those images, catalogued as UTSH118 through UTSH129, from ABC4. Anyone could display them. Before inferring a private supply channel, the material Wilson showed would need to be compared against the published exhibit set and found to contain content that is not in it. That comparison has not been done here and no source reviewed has done it. The debate occurred three days before this entry and the record around it is still forming.

findings.claim: The question of TPUSA backing for Wilson was live before the debate
findings.detail: Explicitly, and by Owens' own doing. Among the conditions she set in the pre-debate negotiation was a requirement that Blake Neff, Andrew Kolvet, or Erika Kirk state publicly that Wilson was debating on TPUSA's behalf. That is a direct attempt to force disclosure of institutional backing, which indicates the question was already live for her rather than raised afterward. Whether the condition was met, and whether any of the three responded, is not established in sources reviewed. Its existence establishes that the provenance question was being asked before any messages were displayed, not constructed after the fact.

findings.claim: Owens has produced the underlying material for her own competing claims
findings.detail: Not consistently, and the same standard applies to her. This app has repeatedly found her claims resting on material described but not produced or independently verifiable: a receipt she says she has seen unredacted but which circulated blurred, an incident report characterised rather than published, and a Fort Huachuca identification she has herself acknowledged may be misidentification. Whatever is true of TPUSA's supply practices, a critic who declines to publish her own documents while demanding provenance from others is subject to the same objection. This app applies the standard in both directions.

findings.claim: This pattern bears on the criminal case against Robinson
findings.detail: It does not. How an advocacy organisation manages its public relations, and whether commentators receive private briefings, has no bearing on whether the state can prove its case in court. The reason it is tracked here is narrower: this app assesses claims by provenance, and material whose route into public circulation is undisclosed cannot be weighted properly. The Fort Huachuca photograph is the demonstration — presented as decisive, sourced privately, and worthless on examination. The lesson is about handling evidence claims, not about the shooting.

fact_check_gap: Nobody appears to have asked Andrew Kolvet why purported alibi material went to a YouTube commentator privately rather than being released by the organisation, despite the photograph's public collapse and its role in an ongoing dispute that has since become federal defamation litigation. Separately, the obvious first test on the Wilson question — comparing what he displayed against the published hearing exhibit set — is straightforward and appears undone by anyone, including this app.

title: The September 9 Security-Team Messages Wilson Revealed: Content, Provenance, and What They Contradict
summary: During the August 14, 2026 debate, Andrew Wilson stated he held never-before-seen messages between Charlie Kirk and his security team dated September 9, 2025, and read them publicly for the first time. If authentic they are among the most consequential documents in the case: Kirk reportedly states, the day before he was killed, that he was worried the LEFT was trying to kill him. That is directly opposite to the Israel-fear thread this app assessed separately. They are unverified, and the obvious source is not the one being assumed.
sources_quality: B for the existence and wording of the messages, which rest on a debate transcript in which Wilson read them aloud and claimed possession; NOT RATED for authenticity, which no independent party has established; A- for the contradiction analysis, which compares them against material already documented in this app
key_takeaway: Wilson said he holds never-before-seen messages from Kirk to his security team dated September 9, 2025, and that he was revealing them publicly for the first time. Per his reading: the security team wrote that law enforcement had been fully supportive and had agreed to a security plan and posture, and that the next day's event would be covered by both his team and the campus. Kirk replied to remind them they were there for one person's security only, “because I'm somewhat worried the left is trying to kill me.” Two things follow if that is genuine. It is a contemporaneous statement of Kirk's own perceived threat the day before his death, and it names the political left, not Israel — which cuts directly against the Harrison Smith and Grayzone material assessed elsewhere in this app. And it establishes that law enforcement had agreed a security plan and posture for the event, which bears on the 96-99% security-failure finding and on the Harpole rooftop dispute at X8 and X30. On provenance: these are messages BETWEEN Kirk and his security team, so every member of that team holds a copy on their own device. Brian Harpole, who headed that team, is currently suing Candace Owens for defamation and has an evident interest in material showing his team had secured a law-enforcement plan and that Kirk feared the left. That is a far more direct route than Kirk's widow, and no phone is required for it. On the reading of “remind them”: the fuller passage makes the campus police the likely referent rather than Kirk's own detail. The security team's message distinguishes its own team from the campus PD and patrol units, and the qualifier “only” makes sense addressed to a body with competing duties, not to a protective detail that has no other function. Kirk was not reminding his bodyguards what their job was; he appears to have been directing them to ensure the police understood theirs. That is less strange, and more consequential — because it is the same police coverage Harpole says his team stood down the rooftop for.

findings.claim: Wilson claimed possession of previously unreleased Charlie Kirk messages
findings.detail: He said so explicitly in the August 14, 2026 debate, stating he held in his possession never-before-seen messages from Charlie Kirk to his security team dated September 9, 2025, and that he was sharing them for the first time publicly. He later referred to possibly having further never-before-seen evidence. This is a first-person claim of possession made on the record, distinct from the Robinson text-thread exhibits which have been public since the July 9, 2026 hearing and which anyone could display.

findings.claim: The messages, if authentic, show Kirk feared the political left rather than Israel
findings.detail: Per Wilson's reading, the security team reported that law enforcement had been fully supportive and had agreed to a security plan and posture, with the next day's event covered by both his team and the campus. Kirk replied asking that they be reminded they were there for one person's security only, “because I'm somewhat worried the left is trying to kill me.” That is a specific, dated, operational-context statement of perceived threat from Kirk himself, made the day before he was killed. It contradicts the claim assessed at contradiction X47 that Kirk feared Israel would kill him if he turned against it — a claim which traces to Harrison Smith of Infowars relaying an unnamed intermediary, and which no document supports. Between an alleged private remark relayed anonymously and a dated message read from a thread with a named counterparty group, the latter is the stronger artefact if it is genuine.

findings.claim: The messages must have come from Erika Kirk because she holds Charlie's phone
findings.detail: The premise is sound and the inference does not follow. Erika Kirk has publicly stated she is in possession of her husband's cellphone and has released messages from it, including his final message. But these are messages BETWEEN Kirk and his security team, which means every counterparty on that thread holds an identical copy on their own device. No access to Kirk's phone is required to produce them. This app has already documented the same principle in another context: contradiction X3 records that Josh Hammer was in the same private chat as Kirk's September 8 Israel message and had direct access to Kirk's actual language. The pool of possible sources here is the security team, not the estate. And one member of that team, Brian Harpole, is currently plaintiff in a federal defamation action against Candace Owens, whom Wilson was debating, and the messages as read make his team look diligent — they had secured a law-enforcement plan — while undercutting Owens' narrative. Motive and access both point there more directly than to the widow. This app takes no position on who actually supplied them; it establishes only that the stated inference is not compelled.

findings.claim: The messages have been independently authenticated
findings.detail: They have not, by anyone. No forensic examination, no named custodian, no device or metadata verification, and no confirmation from TPUSA, the security team, the estate, or law enforcement has been located. Wilson read them aloud and asserted possession. That is a materially better evidentiary posture than an anonymous relay, because he is named, on the record, and describes a specific dated exchange with an identifiable counterparty group who could confirm or deny it. It is nonetheless an unverified assertion, and this app applies the same standard here it applied to Owens' unproduced receipt and to the Kolvet photograph: described is not produced, and produced is not authenticated.

findings.claim: The messages bear on the security-failure finding
findings.detail: Directly, and in a way that sharpens rather than softens it. If the security team told Kirk on September 9 that law enforcement had been fully supportive and had agreed a security plan and posture, with coverage by both the private detail and the campus, then a plan existed and was communicated to the principal the day before. That makes the outcome harder to explain, not easier: six campus officers for roughly 3,000 attendees, an unsecured rooftop with direct line of sight, and this app's separately logged dispute at X8 and X30 over whether Harpole raised rooftop access specifically. It also cuts against any suggestion that the event was under-planned by inadvertence. This app's security-failure confidence stands at 96-99% and nothing here lowers it.

findings.claim: This resolves the pattern question about material reaching commentators
findings.detail: It sharpens it without resolving it. The documented instance remains Kolvet supplying Melton a photograph privately, which then collapsed publicly. Here a commentator again displays material the public has not seen, again without disclosing its route, in a dispute where the organisation and its former security lead both have interests. Owens' own pre-debate condition — that Neff, Kolvet or Erika Kirk state whether Wilson was debating on TPUSA's behalf — shows the provenance question was live before a word was spoken. What would settle it is simple and nobody has done it: ask Wilson who gave him the messages, and ask the security team whether the thread is genuine.

findings.claim: Kirk was reminding his own detail of their basic responsibility
findings.detail: The fuller passage resolves this and the antecedent points elsewhere. The security team's message lists four distinct parties: law enforcement generally, “my team,” the campus PD, and patrol units available if additional support were required, closing with a headcount of eleven on site. Kirk's reply asks that “them” be reminded they are there for one person's security only. The writer's own team is not a natural referent for “them” in a message written by that team's leader — a principal addressing his own detail would say your guys, not them. The word doing the real work is “only.” A private protective detail has no function other than the principal, so the qualifier would be redundant addressed to them. Campus police at a university event ordinarily carry divided responsibilities: crowd management, traffic, general campus safety. An instruction that they are there for one person's security ONLY reads as a correction to a body with competing duties, not a reminder to a body with one. The best reading is that Kirk was directing his security lead to ensure the campus police understood their assignment was his personal protection rather than general event support.

findings.claim: The exchange shows the principal actively directing his own security posture the day before
findings.detail: Whichever reading of “them” is correct, this holds and it is the substantive point. Kirk did not simply acknowledge the security briefing; he issued an instruction narrowing the mission and gave his reason for it. A principal who is confident in an arrangement approves it. A principal who intervenes to restate priorities is not fully confident, and Kirk supplied the specific cause of his concern in the same sentence. The exchange also corroborates Brian Harpole's separate account on the Shawn Ryan Show: the team message states law enforcement had been fully supportive and had agreed a security plan and posture, with coverage by both the private detail and campus PD and patrol units in reserve. That is the arrangement Harpole describes relying on when his team stood down the rooftop zone, and it is the arrangement that failed the following day.

findings.claim: The staffing figures in the two accounts match
findings.detail: They are close but not identical, and the discrepancy is small enough to be innocuous while worth recording. The September 9 message as read states eleven on site. Harpole told the Shawn Ryan Show he had twelve, with six given for the rest of the campus. The difference is one person and has obvious mundane explanations — the writer counting or not counting himself, a late addition, or a figure quoted from memory months later. It is logged because both numbers describe the same detail on the same day and this app records rather than reconciles small conflicts between accounts, and because the second figure comes from an interested party recalling it after the fact.

title: The Drone Question: Why Rooftop Coverage Was Dropped, and the Aircraft Nobody Explained
summary: Brian Harpole's account on the Shawn Ryan Show (SRS #254) contains the clearest mechanism yet offered for how the rooftop went unwatched: his team stood down rooftop coverage because campus police said they had it. The same interview contains a loose end nobody has resolved — an unexplained drone flown over the site earlier that day that Harpole says his team could not account for.
sources_quality: B+ for Harpole's account, which is a named first-person interview with texts read on air and offered for FOIA verification, but is one interested party's version; A for the corroborating findings on drone absence and officer numbers, which come from an Associated Press investigation independent of him
key_takeaway: Two things emerge and they pull in different directions. The first is a causal mechanism for the security failure that this app had not previously captured. Harpole says his team's rooftop zone was dropped because campus police told him the rooftops were covered — his summary of the exchange is that PD said they had it covered, and so that zone was dropped. His detail numbered twelve, of whom six were assigned to the rest of the campus. He also says he raised the specific rooftop with UVU's police chief by text on September 8, two days before, read those texts on air, and invited a FOIA request on the chief's phone. That is a falsifiable claim with a documentary trail. The second is the drone question, and the user's recollection is broadly right with one correction. Harpole did not say drones were prohibited generally; he said HE could not fly one because the site sits in Provo controlled airspace requiring Part 107 authorisation he did not have for that area, and he would not break the rules. He is emphatic that others could have flown: Orem PD operates an active professional drone unit and holds a mutual-aid agreement with the university, and when he asked whether they had been called, he says the answer was that they were never asked. And then the loose end: he confirms an unexplained drone went up over the site earlier that day. His words are that they did not know where it came from. He notes an audio-video team throwing up a small drone for a shot is not unusual, while distinguishing this from the little ones such teams use.

findings.claim: Harpole said drones were not permitted at the event
findings.detail: That is a compression of what he said and the distinction matters. His account is that HE could not fly, because the location falls within Provo controlled airspace and he lacked the Part 107 authorisation for it, with likely secondary restrictions given campus foot traffic — and that he was not prepared to break the rules, both on principle and because he has to protect the client's reputation as well as their person. He is explicit that others could have flown. He states the university and its police department could have operated drones but did not have them, that Orem PD has an active and professional drone unit, that Orem PD holds a mutual-aid agreement with the school, and that when he asked Orem PD whether they had been requested to assist, the answer was that they had not been asked. So the constraint he describes is on his own team's authorisation, not a blanket prohibition on aerial coverage.

findings.claim: An unexplained drone was airborne over the site on the day of the shooting
findings.detail: Harpole confirms it in the interview. The exchange has Ryan noting that they knew there were no police drones and then someone flew a drone up earlier that day, which Harpole affirms, adding that they did not know where it came from and were asking what the deal with it was. He offers the ordinary explanation unprompted — that an audio-video team putting up a small drone for a shot is not uncommon and they have seen it before — while distinguishing the small units such teams typically use. This app has located no subsequent public accounting identifying the operator of that aircraft. Separately and distinctly, drone footage of the deserted campus and the rooftop firing position circulated after the shooting; that is aftermath footage and should not be conflated with the aircraft Harpole describes during the event.

findings.claim: The rooftop was left uncovered by oversight rather than by a specific handoff
findings.detail: Harpole describes a handoff, and this is the most consequential thing in the interview. His account is that the rooftops were to be covered by police, that PD told him they had it covered, and that his team consequently dropped that zone. Personal security details are, as he puts it, personal — his twelve-man team was configured for close protection with roughly 3,000 people inside 50 metres, and six were given for the rest of the campus. If accurate, this converts the security failure from a diffuse institutional shortcoming into a specific reliance: a private detail stood down an assigned zone on a police assurance, and the assurance was not met. That is a materially different finding from a general staffing complaint, and it is the mechanism this app's 96-99% security-failure confidence had lacked.

findings.claim: Harpole's rooftop warning claim rests only on his own assertion
findings.detail: He read the underlying texts aloud on the programme, said they were real, agreed to their being displayed on screen, and invited a public-records request on the police chief's phone to verify them. Reporting indicates the texts show him flagging the specific rooftop later used by the shooter to UVU's police chief on September 8, two days before the event. Whether the texts say what he says they say is checkable by anyone willing to file the records request he suggested, which is a stronger evidentiary posture than most claims assessed in this app. It remains one interested party's account — he is a plaintiff in active litigation and has obvious reason to establish that he warned and was ignored — and UVU's position at contradictions X8 and X30 is unchanged by his repeating it.

findings.claim: Independent reporting corroborates the absence of aerial coverage
findings.detail: An Associated Press investigation, independent of Harpole, found that campus police did not fly a drone to monitor rooftops and did not coordinate with local law enforcement to secure the event, and that six campus officers monitored it. Conditions were clear and sunny, which is to say ideal for aerial observation of the surrounding roofs including the position the shot came from. Those findings match Harpole's account on the points where they overlap, which is meaningful because AP reached them without relying on him.

findings.claim: The unexplained drone connects to the shooting
findings.detail: Nothing suggests it does and no source alleges it. The ordinary explanation Harpole himself offers — an event AV team taking aerial footage — is unremarkable and probably correct. It is logged as an open item for two narrow reasons. It went unidentified by the professional security detail on site at the time, which is itself a small security finding. And this app's standing practice is to record loose ends rather than tidy them away, exactly as it did with the unfired round on the second rooftop and the unattributed handgun holster. If the operator was ever identified, this app has not located that record.

Harpole says he cannot fly drones — Provo controlled airspace, Part 107 limits; states UVU PD lacked drones and Orem PD's drone unit was never asked despite a mutual-aid agreement
Per Harpole, police indicate rooftops are covered; his team drops that zone. Detail of 12, with six for the rest of campus
An unexplained drone is flown over the site; Harpole says they did not know where it came from
Kirk shot from the Losee Center roof
Separate drone footage of the deserted campus and rooftop position circulates publicly — aftermath, not the event-day aircraft

Nobody has publicly identified who operated the drone airborne over the site earlier on September 10, despite the on-site security lead saying he could not account for it. And nobody appears to have filed the records request Harpole explicitly invited on the police chief's phone, which would settle the rooftop-warning dispute logged at X8 and X30 rather than leaving it as a named-individual-versus-institution standoff.

title: Cui Bono: Who Actually Gained, Ranked — and Why the Frame Misleads Here
summary: A ranked accounting of who materially benefited from Charlie Kirk's death, built from documented positions and figures rather than inference. The exercise is worth doing and its limits are worth stating plainly: benefit accrues downstream of every major event regardless of cause, and in this case the ranking cuts against the hypotheses it is usually deployed to support.
sources_quality: A for positional and financial facts (IRS filings, board announcements, litigation records already established elsewhere in this app); B for characterisations of audience and commercial gain, which are directional rather than measured; NOT RATED for motive, which none of this evidence speaks to
key_takeaway: The largest single positional gain went to Erika Kirk, who moved from spouse to CEO and board chair of a 115-million-dollar organisation within eight days. The largest operational gain went to Tyler Bowyer, already chief operating officer, who became the institutional anchor beside a new chief executive with no prior executive role there, and who is himself the named public voice asserting that the succession was what Charlie Kirk wanted. The largest institutional gain went to Turning Point itself, which converted a founder's death into martyrdom-scale mobilisation. And a genuinely underexamined beneficiary class is the commentary economy: the dispute over this killing has become directly monetisable content, with a debate over it negotiated in the range of several hundred thousand dollars. But the ranking does not do the work it is usually asked to do. One correction matters: the revenue jump from roughly $85 million to $115.5 million occurred in a fiscal year that closed on June 30, 2025 — more than two months BEFORE the killing. It cannot be a consequence of it. The post-death financial picture is not yet public and will not be until roughly May 2027. Meanwhile the person accused gained nothing whatsoever, which is itself analytically significant.

findings.claim: Erika Kirk received the largest single positional gain
findings.detail: Factually yes, and the framing needs care. On September 18, 2025, eight days after the killing, the board unanimously elected her chief executive and board chair of Turning Point USA. She moved from spouse of the founder to head of an organisation reporting $115.45 million in revenue. That is the largest discrete positional change of anyone in this case. Three things sit against reading it as motive. The succession has a documented pre-death basis: Kirk reportedly told a donor at an Aspen retreat in August 2025, a month before his death, that if something happened the board would sort it out and that he appointed his wife (logged at contradiction X32). She lost her husband and is raising two young children. And the specific allegations circulating about her — Epstein recruitment, arranging her husband's death, a concealed Rothschild lineage — have each been examined here or by independent fact-checkers and found unsupported, in one case contradicted outright by ordinary genealogical records.

findings.claim: Tyler Bowyer gained the most operational power
findings.detail: He was already chief operating officer of Turning Point Action and, by his own description, effectively ran operations. The death removed the founder and installed a chief executive with no prior executive tenure at the organisation, which structurally elevates the person holding institutional continuity. He is additionally the named public voice asserting that Kirk intended Erika to succeed him — meaning the individual whose position was most enhanced by that particular succession is also its principal public witness. That combination is worth recording plainly. It is not evidence of anything: he had known Kirk since 2014, is a plausible custodian of Kirk's intentions, and no source alleges his involvement in the death. But it is the sort of structural fact a serious beneficiary analysis should not omit.

findings.claim: Turning Point's revenue growth was a consequence of the killing
findings.detail: This is the correction that most changes the picture, and it is checkable. Turning Point USA's fiscal year ends June 30. The reported jump from $84.99 million in FY2024 to $115.45 million in FY2025 covers the year that CLOSED on June 30, 2025 — two and a half months before Kirk was killed on September 10. The growth predates the death entirely and cannot have been caused by it. Anyone citing that increase as evidence of who profited is citing the wrong year. The genuine post-death financial picture falls in FY2026, whose return is not due until roughly May 2027 and has not been filed. Nobody currently knows what it shows, including this app.

findings.claim: The organisation nonetheless gained substantially in non-financial terms
findings.detail: On documented evidence short of the unfiled accounts: donors and allies publicly recommitted within a day of the killing; the memorial filled an NFL stadium with a reported 100,000 attendees across two venues, carrying a DHS Level 1 security rating and a speaker roster including the President and Vice President; and AmericaFest in December 2025 drew a reported record 30,000 attendees. A movement organisation acquiring a martyr acquires mobilisation, and that is visible without needing the accounts. Whether it converted into revenue is the FY2026 question above.

findings.claim: The commentary economy is a significant and underexamined beneficiary
findings.detail: This is the beneficiary class that requires no conspiracy and gets the least scrutiny. The dispute over the killing has become directly monetisable: Candace Owens has built sustained programming around it and has herself described the dynamic — that presenting material the public has not seen builds audience trust which then transfers to her other claims. Andrew Wilson's debate with her was negotiated with figures reported in the $300,000 to $500,000 range. Multiple YouTube channels assessed in this app — ValhallaVFT, Paramount Tactical, TriggerSmart, HeavyDutyCountry, JesseOnFire, Wolves & Finance — have produced extended series on it. Attention is the currency and the case generates it in volume. This beneficiary class also has a structural incentive against resolution: a settled case stops producing content, which is a bias worth naming in every direction, including toward this app's own sources.

findings.claim: The accused gained anything
findings.detail: Tyler Robinson gained nothing on any reading of the evidence. He faces aggravated murder with the death penalty still available following the June 2026 contempt ruling, is represented by taxpayer-funded counsel after a finding of indigency, and by the state's own account surrendered through his family. This is analytically relevant rather than merely sad. Instrumental crimes have beneficiaries who are traceable through gain; expressive or ideological ones do not. A perpetrator whose own outcome is catastrophic and who took no step to secure any benefit is the pattern of the latter. It is one of several reasons this app's confidence in self-directed rather than externally-tasked action sits at 80-90%.

findings.claim: Ranking beneficiaries is evidence about causation
findings.detail: It is not, and this is the load-bearing point. Every violent death redistributes position, attention and money, and the redistribution happens identically whether the cause was conspiracy, lone action or accident. Cui bono identifies who to examine; it cannot establish what happened. In this case the examining has been done. The institutional beneficiaries have each been specifically tested against evidence rather than inference — aircraft transponder records, travel documents, DNA proportions, the Fort Huachuca allegation, the vendor payment trail across three record systems — and none of it connected. That is why this app's confidence in a directed assassination sits at 0-5%: not because nobody benefited, but because every specific mechanism proposed to link a beneficiary to the act has failed on its own evidence.

title: Bowyer, the Cancelled Audit, and an Eleven-Year Record of Contested Finances
summary: Charlie Kirk removed Tyler Bowyer from the TPUSA chief operating officer role and ordered a DOGE-style efficiency review eight days before he was killed. The review never happened. This entry documents that sequence, a 2015 no-confidence resolution alleging misuse of funds that Bowyer survived by casting the deciding vote on himself, and a set of far more serious allegations that remain unverified and are recorded as such.
sources_quality: A- for the 2015 Maricopa County matter (the resolution text is public, the vote count was confirmed by Arizona Capitol Times); B for the September 2 memo, whose contents are consistently described across multiple accounts but which this app has not examined directly; C for the litigation timeline; NOT RATED and expressly unverified for the whistleblower and assault-suppression allegations
key_takeaway: The September 2, 2025 memo is the most motive-adjacent documented fact anyone has produced in this case, and it deserves to be stated precisely. Eight days before he was killed, Kirk issued an internal memo that moved Bowyer out of the TPUSA chief operating officer role he had held for roughly eight years, redirected him to focus on Turning Point Action, installed fundraiser Justin Strife as chief operating officer, and empowered Strife to run a DOGE-style efficiency review. Kirk had reportedly raised internal concerns that the organisation was burning through cash. Kirk was shot on September 10. The review was cancelled. Separately, an eleven-year pattern of contested financial governance is documented: in November 2015, as chairman of the Maricopa County Republican Committee, Bowyer faced a no-confidence resolution alleging misuse of funds without receipts, federal election law violations, and embezzlement of $50,000. Fourteen of twenty-nine officers voted against him. Rather than recuse himself from a vote on his own conduct, he cast the deciding vote and survived by one. What is NOT established is any crime. There has been no conviction, no criminal charge for financial misconduct, and the fake-electors indictment was dismissed. The accurate description is a documented pattern of allegations and of resisting scrutiny — not a pattern of established crimes, and the distinction is not a technicality.

findings.claim: Kirk removed Bowyer as COO and ordered an audit shortly before his death
findings.detail: Multiple accounts describe an internal memo dated September 2, 2025 in which Kirk reassigned Bowyer out of the TPUSA chief operating officer role after roughly eight years, directing him to focus on Turning Point Action; named fundraiser Justin Strife as chief operating officer; and empowered Strife to lead a DOGE-style efficiency initiative with a mandate to make the organisation more cost-effective, align goals with metrics and reshape culture. Kirk had reportedly expressed concern internally that the organisation was burning cash too quickly. Kirk was killed eight days later and the review did not proceed. This app has not examined the memo itself and rates this supported rather than verified: the descriptions are consistent and specific but circulate largely through Candace Owens' programming and allied commentary, and at least one social-media rendering gives a conflicting date. The memo is the kind of document that could be settled immediately by publication or by TPUSA confirming or denying it, and neither has happened.

findings.claim: The cancelled audit is evidence of involvement in the killing
findings.detail: It is not, and the distinction between significant and probative matters here. A demotion and pending financial review eight days before the principal's death is a genuine motive-adjacent fact, and this app has not previously recorded one of comparable specificity. But motive is the weakest link in any causal chain and this one has no other links: nothing places Bowyer anywhere near Utah, no source alleges his involvement, the shooter's identification runs through DNA and a family-arranged surrender, the operational-signature analysis in this app points away from directed action, and the accused gained nothing. An audit being cancelled after the person who ordered it dies is also the default outcome, not an anomaly requiring explanation. What the sequence legitimately does is raise the priority of the FY2026 financial disclosures, due around May 2027, which will be the first public accounting covering the period Kirk was reportedly concerned about.

findings.claim: Bowyer has a documented history of contested financial governance
findings.detail: In November 2015, while chairman of the Maricopa County Republican Committee, Bowyer faced a formal resolution of no confidence. The resolution alleged misuse of committee funds without receipts, violations of federal election law, and embezzlement of $50,000. The resolution text is publicly available. Arizona Capitol Times reported the vote as fourteen of twenty-nine officers against him. The governance detail is the notable part: with the vote deadlocked, rather than recusing himself from a ballot on his own conduct, he cast the deciding vote and defeated the resolution by one. No criminal charge or prosecution arising from those allegations has been located by this app. They are allegations in an internal party document, not findings — but they are contemporaneous, formal, and made by his own officers.

findings.claim: There is a documented pattern of resisting external scrutiny
findings.detail: Three separate instances, spanning eleven years, are documented. In 2015 he declined to recuse and cast the deciding vote on a resolution examining his own financial conduct. In February 2026 Turning Point USA and Turning Point Action filed a federal lawsuit to block the Arizona Attorney General from obtaining his email records in the fake-electors investigation. And the DOGE-style review of the organisation's finances ordered days before Kirk's death did not proceed after it. Each has an ordinary explanation available: parliamentary rules may have permitted the vote, resisting the scope of a warrant is routine litigation, and reviews commonly lapse when the executive who ordered them dies. The pattern is in the aggregate rather than in any single instance, and it is a pattern of contesting scrutiny — which is lawful — not of established wrongdoing.

findings.claim: Bowyer has been convicted of, or charged with, financial crimes
findings.detail: He has not. No conviction of any kind exists. No criminal charge for financial misconduct has been located in any jurisdiction. The 2015 allegations produced an internal party resolution and no prosecution. The only criminal charges he has faced are the nine counts in the Arizona fake-electors case, which concerned election certification rather than finances, to which he pleaded not guilty, and which were dismissed in 2026 without prejudice on a grand-jury instruction defect. He was never tried. This finding exists because the allegations catalogued above circulate as though they were established, and they are not.

findings.claim: The whistleblower and assault-suppression allegations are substantiated
findings.detail: Neither is, and both are recorded here with care because both are grave. A report circulated that a TPUSA whistleblower went missing after alleging that Bowyer and Erika Kirk were involved in a £10 million donation fraud; the outlet carrying it stated no verified evidence had been publicly confirmed, and this app has located no confirmation of the fraud allegation, the whistleblower's identity, or any missing person report. Separately, independent journalist Brian Ference published an allegation that a Turning Point employee sexually assaulted a colleague and that Bowyer, as chief operating officer, helped suppress or mishandle the complaint. TPUSA has denied this and stated a proper investigation occurred; Bowyer has called the allegation false and referenced a cease-and-desist. Ference is also the author of the 2015 no-confidence writeup, meaning he is a long-standing critic — which cuts both ways, indicating sustained familiarity and also a possible adversarial posture. This app takes no position on either allegation beyond recording that they exist, are denied, and are unverified.

findings.claim: This app has adopted the framing that Bowyer covered up crimes
findings.detail: It has not and will not on the current record. What the evidence supports is that allegations of financial impropriety have followed him since 2015, that he has more than once acted to limit external examination of his conduct, and that a financial review of the organisation he had just been removed from leading was cancelled after the person who ordered it was killed. Those are documented and they are legitimately unflattering. They are categorically different from established crimes, and treating an unproven allegation as a proven one is the same error this app has refused in every other direction in this case — including where the target was Erika Kirk, Brian Harpole, or Mitch Snow.

Equally, no outlet appears to have asked the obvious follow-up: whether the efficiency review was formally cancelled, deferred, or quietly abandoned, and whether Justin Strife remains in the role Kirk appointed him to. Both are answerable by asking named people at a functioning organisation.

title: Bowyer Crossover Test: Robinson, Twiggs, and the FBI — A Negative Result
summary: A direct search for any documented intersection between Tyler Bowyer and Tyler Robinson, Lance Twiggs, or the FBI personnel connected to this case. Nothing was found in any direction. Recorded because a negative result on a specific, falsifiable question is worth as much as a positive one, and because the geography actively works against the hypothesis.
sources_quality: B — this is an absence-of-evidence finding drawn from open-source search across charging documents, hearing coverage, organisational records and reporting. Absence in public sources is not proof of absence, and this app has no access to phone records, financial accounts, or non-public communications for any party.
key_takeaway: No documented crossing was found between Bowyer and Robinson, Bowyer and Twiggs, or Bowyer and any named FBI official in this case. The geography is the strongest single point against it: Robinson and Twiggs shared a townhome in St. George, Washington County, in Utah's far southwest corner, roughly 240 miles from the UVU campus and several hundred from Bowyer's Arizona base. Robinson was an apprentice electrician enrolled at Dixie Technical College; Twiggs attended Utah Tech University and is described as an aspiring professional gamer with no reported political involvement of any kind. Neither has any documented Turning Point affiliation, employment, volunteering, donation, or event attendance. On the FBI side, Bowyer's only documented contact with federal process is as a subject of the Arizona fake-electors investigation conducted by a state attorney general, not a federal one, and this app found no record of interaction with Robert Bohls, Mehtab Syed, or any Salt Lake City field office personnel. This app's existing crossover work reached the same result from the other direction: the only confirmed same-day contact Robinson had with anyone from TPUSA was with unidentified representatives in the courtyard on the morning of September 10, and those representatives have never been publicly named.

findings.claim: Any documented contact exists between Bowyer and Tyler Robinson
findings.detail: None located. No phone contact, message, email, financial transaction, employment relationship, shared organisation, event attendance, or mutual associate appears in charging documents, preliminary hearing coverage, or reporting reviewed. Robinson lived in Washington, Washington County, in Utah's far southwest, roughly 240 miles from the UVU campus and considerably further from Bowyer's Arizona base. Robinson's documented associations are a Discord friend group, an apprenticeship at Dixie Technical College, and his family. This app's separate crossover analysis found no verified pre-death connection between Robinson and Kirk or anyone in Kirk's circle either, with one exception noted below.

findings.claim: Any documented contact exists between Bowyer and Lance Twiggs
findings.detail: None located, and Twiggs is if anything a less plausible candidate. He is 22, from St. George, attended Utah Tech University, is described as an aspiring professional gamer, and reporting indicates he was forced out of the family home at eighteen over religious and political disagreements with his father. No political involvement of any kind is reported, let alone Turning Point affiliation. Federal officials stated he had no advance knowledge of the plan, both federal and county prosecutors granted him use immunity rather than charging him, and he has not been accused of any offence.

findings.claim: Any documented contact exists between Bowyer and FBI officials in this case
findings.detail: None located. The named federal figures in this case are Salt Lake City Special Agent in Charge Robert Bohls, his predecessor Mehtab Syed, and Director Kash Patel; the investigative work was co-led with Utah state agencies and no FBI case agent has ever been publicly named. Bowyer's own exposure to legal process runs through the Arizona fake-electors matter, which was a STATE prosecution brought by Attorney General Kris Mayes before a Maricopa County grand jury — not an FBI investigation. The February 2026 litigation over his email records was against the state attorney general. The federal pardons issued in November 2025 were a presidential act, not a Bureau interaction. Patel and Bowyer occupy overlapping political space, Bowyer being an RNC committeeman, but political proximity is not documented contact and this app treats it as neither.

findings.claim: The unidentified TPUSA representatives Robinson spoke to could be a crossing point
findings.detail: This is the one genuine gap and it should be stated rather than smoothed over. Surveillance placed Robinson in the courtyard around 8:30 a.m. on September 10 speaking with TPUSA representatives before leaving at approximately 9:25 a.m. Those representatives have never been publicly identified. Nothing suggests Bowyer was among them — no account places him in Utah that day, and a chief operating officer is not typically staffing a campus table — but the honest position is that an unidentified person cannot be excluded by name. Identifying who Robinson spoke to that morning remains an open investigative question in this app's record regardless of who it turns out to be.

findings.claim: Bowyer's role in venue selection creates a connection to the shooting
findings.detail: The venue timeline has an ordinary explanation that Bowyer himself gave publicly. The UVU stop was approved in July, which has been cited as suspiciously late; his response was that many universities will not permit bookings before a set date near the start of the academic year, and that the tours team and local chapters reserve space as soon as campuses allow. That is a checkable claim about standard university scheduling practice rather than a deflection, and it is consistent with how campus event booking generally works. No source reviewed establishes which individual selected UVU, and nothing connects the selection to Robinson, who by all available evidence learned of the appearance the way the public did.

findings.claim: A negative result here settles the question
findings.detail: It constrains it rather than settling it, and the limits should be explicit. This app searched open sources: charging documents, hearing coverage, organisational records, litigation filings and reporting. It has no access to phone records, financial accounts, private messages, travel data, or non-public communications for Bowyer, Robinson or Twiggs. A connection conducted privately would not surface here. What can be said is that after specific searching, no crossing appears in the public record in any direction, the geography is unfavourable, and neither Robinson nor Twiggs has any documented political or organisational footprint that would create an occasion for one.

fact_check_gap: The identity of the TPUSA representatives Robinson spoke with in the courtyard on the morning of September 10 has never been published, despite surveillance capturing the interaction and the encounter being described in open court. They are, on the available record, the only people from the organisation known to have spoken with him. Naming them would close the single genuine gap in every crossover analysis this app has run.

title: Shot Reconstruction: External Ballistics Check, and What the Second-Roof Round Can and Cannot Show
summary: A worked reconstruction of the shot from the reported firing position, testing whether the external ballistics are consistent with the official account. They are, comfortably. The reconstruction also resolves one item this app had logged as an anomaly, corrects a premise about the round found on a second roof, and leaves the genuine problem exactly where it already was — in the terminal ballistics, not the flight.
sources_quality: A for the trigonometry and the published ballistic tables, which are independently verifiable and not case-specific; A- for the recovered-weapon condition and Hull's testimony on the second round; B for the geometry, which uses building centroids rather than the actual firing and stage points
key_takeaway: Everything about getting the bullet from the roof to the target is unremarkable. The reported 80 ft elevation and 10.65° declination give a horizontal distance of 129.7 m (141.8 yd) and a line-of-sight distance of 131.9 m (144.3 yd). Angle compensation under the rifleman's rule is 2.3 m — negligible. Bullet drop at that range with an ordinary zero is one to two inches. Time of flight is about 0.16 seconds, and the muzzle report takes 0.385 seconds to cover the same distance, so the bullet arrives roughly 0.22 seconds BEFORE the sound — which matches the witness pattern of impact preceding the bang. Combined with the near-calm conditions established earlier (about 1.2 mph crosswind, roughly 0.2 inches of drift), the shot required no compensation of any kind. Two corrections follow. The absence of a shell casing at the firing position is NOT an anomaly and this app previously treated it as one: a bolt-action retains the fired case until manually cycled, and the rifle was recovered holding one spent and three unspent rounds, all engraved — the case was never at the scene to be found. And the second-roof round cannot be reconstructed at all, because it was unfired. An unfired cartridge has no trajectory. It is a dropped object, not a ballistic event.

findings.claim: The external ballistics are consistent with the official account
findings.detail: On every computable measure. Horizontal distance from the reported figures is 129.7 m (141.8 yd), line-of-sight 131.9 m (144.3 yd), independently consistent with the 112 m building-centroid separation measured from OpenStreetMap once the offset between centroids and actual positions is allowed for. Rifleman's-rule compensation for a 10.65° declination is 2.3 m and irrelevant at this range. Drop with a conventional 100-yard zero is about 1.6 inches. Wind drift, from the reanalysis data, is about 0.2 inches. Time of flight is roughly 0.16 seconds. There is nothing about the trajectory that requires explanation, unusual skill, or specialist equipment beyond a scoped rifle.

findings.claim: The absence of a shell casing at the firing position is an anomaly
findings.detail: CORRECTION to this app's earlier treatment, which logged it at contradiction X24 as a genuine gap. It is not. A bolt-action rifle does not self-eject: the fired case remains in the chamber until the shooter manually works the bolt. The recovered rifle held one spent and three unspent rounds, all carrying the engraved text. The spent case was therefore accounted for inside the weapon and was never deposited at the firing position at all. Hull's testimony that no bullets or casings were recovered on or near the Losee building is exactly what the mechanism predicts. This removes an item the app had carried as unexplained, and it removes it in the state's favour.

findings.claim: The second-roof round can be ballistically reconstructed or tied to the shot
findings.detail: It cannot, for a reason that ends the inquiry: the round was UNFIRED. An unfired cartridge has no trajectory, no impact point, no terminal behaviour and no ballistic signature to reconstruct. It is a dropped object. The only inference it supports is that a person with a rifle was on that roof at some point, which is unsurprising on a campus where armed officers responded. It cannot indicate a second firing position, because nothing was fired from it, and it cannot be geometrically related to the wound because it never travelled.

findings.claim: The second-roof round has been identified as a .223
findings.detail: No caliber has been publicly established. Under cross-examination Hull said he could not recall the type of bullet or the type of gun it came from. A .223 or 5.56 is a reasonable guess, since American patrol rifles are predominantly AR-pattern in those chamberings and that would fit the officer-cycling explanation, but it is a guess and no source reviewed states it. The more significant point is what Hull's non-recollection does to the explanation itself: the round was excluded from the crime scene on the basis that an officer had cycled his rifle, yet the investigator could not recall its caliber, no officer has been named, and no documentation of when or by whom that determination was made has been produced. The explanation is mechanically plausible — clearing or making ready an AR ejects a live round — and remains undocumented.

findings.claim: A different firing position fits the evidence better than the Losee roof
findings.detail: The physical evidence is heavily one-sided. On the Losee roof: gravel impressions of elbows, knees and feet with direct line of sight to the stage, described by officer Chris Bagley as looking like a sniper's pad; a red-and-black screwdriver carrying DNA with Robinson as the dominant contributor; reported fingerprints and a palm print near the northeast edge; and surveillance of a figure accessing the roof at approximately 12:15, crawling to the edge by 12:22, and leaving immediately after the 12:23 shot. On the other roof: one unfired cartridge of unrecorded caliber. Relocating the firing position would require explaining away the pad, the DNA, the prints and the surveillance sequence, and would gain nothing, because the item at the alternative location was never fired. The geometry also works from Losee without strain.

findings.claim: The reconstruction resolves the case's ballistic problem
findings.detail: It resolves the flight and leaves the arrival untouched, and the distinction is the whole point. Everything up to impact is ordinary: a short-range shot, negligible drop, negligible wind, negligible angle compensation, a fast and unremarkable time of flight. What remains unexplained is what the bullet did on arrival. The identified load is a Remington .30-06 150gr Core-Lokt, engineered around a mechanical jacket-to-core lock specifically to resist separation, rated at 65-80% weight retention, and penetrating roughly 23 inches of ordnance gelatin. The recovered evidence is a separated jacket plus four lead fragments, from a structure some five to six inches across, with no exit. That contradiction (logged at X43) is untouched by anything computed here. The shot was easy; the wound is the anomaly.

location_b.name: Target — courtyard stage position
location_b.claimed_time: Horizontal 129.7 m / 141.8 yd; line of sight 131.9 m / 144.3 yd

route_math.minimum_drive_time: Time of flight ~0.161 s; muzzle report arrival ~0.385 s
route_math.available_window: Bullet precedes the sound by ~0.22 s at the target
route_math.shortfall: None in the external ballistics. Rifleman's-rule compensation 2.3 m; drop ~1.6 in at a 100-yd zero; wind drift ~0.2 in at the measured 1.2 mph crosswind. No compensation of any kind was required.
route_math.note: Measured OSM centroid separation is 112.0 m against 129.7 m implied — an 18 m difference well inside centroid-versus-actual-position error. The 200-yard figure would require a 7.59 deg angle and a firing point beyond the courtyard complex.

fact_check_gap: Both parties in the death-penalty aggravator dispute are arguing about whether the bullet passed above or through the crowd, and neither has produced a trajectory reconstruction — despite the inputs being a declination angle, an elevation, a distance, a stage height and a terrace profile, all of which are obtainable. Separately, the casing-absence question circulated for months as an anomaly when the mechanism of a bolt-action explains it completely, and the caliber of the second-roof round has never been published despite being the one detail that would confirm or refute the officer explanation.
