title: Terryl Farnsworth, the SD Card, and the Chain of Custody the Judge Broke Off
summary: TPUSA's audio-visual lead removed the camera positioned directly behind Kirk, pulled its SD card, and delivered the footage to law enforcement as a copy on a flash drive rather than as original media. A judge later sustained a defence objection and required the state to produce the original unaltered footage. That is a real, court-documented evidentiary problem, and it does not require him to have done anything wrong. Layered on top of it is a set of claims that are not documented at all.
sources_quality: A- for the courtroom facts — the flash-drive transfer, the defence objection to the TPUSA authentication statement, and Judge Graf's ruling requiring originals — which come from hearing coverage; C for the selfie video, which circulates via a Candace Owens release and an X account with no primary provenance; F for the 'Mormon Mafia' cluster asserting a Burt family relation, which is self-refuting on its own sourcing and is framed in ethno-religious terms
key_takeaway: Terryl Farnsworth, also rendered Terrell, is TPUSA's AV lead and principal of Visual Impulse LLC — which is the 'Impulse' named in preliminary-hearing testimony as having supplied four video angles from the day, of which one was shown. Within minutes of the shooting he removed the camera positioned directly behind Kirk, and it was subsequently established that he took the SD card out and transferred its contents to a flash drive, which is what law enforcement received. That single fact is the whole finding, and it stands independently of motive: police did not seize original recording media at the scene from the camera with the best angle on the victim; they received a copy made by a private party. The consequences played out in court. The state moved to admit a TPUSA statement authenticating the footage and defence counsel Kathryn Nester objected. Judge Tony Graf sustained an objection and required prosecutors to produce the original, unaltered footage before proceeding. TPUSA's position is that officers instructed staff to secure equipment, which if correct makes the handling lawful and directed rather than a private seizure; Candace Owens disputes that account. The behavioural claims layered on top — the selfie video, the premature death declaration, an alleged family tie to Robinson's defence counsel — range from weakly sourced to unverified, and the last is contradicted by the very record it is drawn from.

findings.claim: Original recording media from the camera behind Kirk was secured by police at the scene
findings.detail: It was not. Farnsworth removed that camera within minutes and it was subsequently established that he took the SD card out and put its contents onto a flash drive, and the flash drive is what went to law enforcement. Court testimony indicates the TPUSA footage reached investigators first on a flash drive and later as downloadable files. This is the finding that matters and it is entirely independent of what anyone intended: the camera with the most direct angle on the victim had its media handled, copied and transferred by a private party before investigators took possession, so what the state holds is a copy of a copy rather than the original recording. Every authentication and completeness question in the case downstream of that footage traces back to this handling.

findings.claim: The court treated the resulting authentication problem as significant
findings.detail: It did, but not in the direction this app previously stated, and the correction matters. When the actual Visual Impulse video (exhibit 8) was offered, defence counsel Kathryn Nester objected under Rule 901 that nobody who made any clips or edits was available to authenticate them. The prosecutor responded that Agent Hull's testimony, combined with Farnsworth's own authentication as owner-director of Visual Impulse, satisfied the rule. The judge OVERRULED the objection and ADMITTED the video. The only restriction that followed concerned publication, and it was requested by the STATE, not the defence: prosecutors themselves asked that it not be shown in the courtroom or broadcast, citing Utah's crime victims' rights provision, because the video depicts the moment Kirk is shot. The judge granted that request; it was watched by the court and parties on monitors only. An earlier revision of this entry stated that Graf sustained an objection and required the state to produce original unaltered footage. That is not supported by the transcript and is withdrawn. What the record actually documents is an authentication objection that failed, followed by a dignity-based publication restriction unrelated to alteration.

findings.claim: Four angles were supplied and one was shown
findings.detail: This app flagged the claim as worth pursuing when reviewing the Olivia Swing corpus, and pursuing it resolved what 'Impulse' referred to. Visual Impulse LLC is Farnsworth's company, and preliminary-hearing testimony has a witness confirming that Impulse supplied four videos encompassing everything provided, and agreeing that there were other angles not shown at the hearing. The plain reading is procedurally unremarkable — a preliminary hearing establishes probable cause and the state shows what it needs, not everything it has, and the remaining angles are presumably in discovery. It becomes material only in combination with the finding above: the same private entity that supplied the angles is the entity that handled the media, and the public has seen one quarter of what that entity produced.

findings.claim: TPUSA's explanation that police directed the equipment handling has been established
findings.detail: It is asserted and disputed and nothing located resolves it, which is unsatisfactory given how much rests on it. TPUSA's position is that officers instructed staff to secure equipment; if accurate, that converts the handling from a private party removing evidence into a lawful direction and largely disposes of the issue. Candace Owens has publicly called that account false and asked why inexpensive SD cards would be prioritised over the far more valuable cameras. No incident report, officer statement, radio log or testimony naming the instructing officer has been produced by anyone. This is the single cheapest outstanding question in the entire matter and it is answerable from records that exist: either an officer gave that instruction and can be identified, or none did.

findings.claim: TPUSA has offered a single consistent explanation for the SD card removal
findings.detail: Two explanations exist and they exclude each other. Andrew Kolvet, executive producer of Kirk's show, posted on X that the individual who took the cards is a longtime staffer, a loyal man and a dear friend, that he made the right call, and that Kolvet remains stunned he had the presence of mind to ensure no one stole them; Kolvet has also said the cards went to the FBI. Tyler Bowyer, TPUSA's chief operating officer, posted that Farnsworth was commanded by police to take down the cameras. Praise for a man's presence of mind is not how anyone describes compliance with an order, and spontaneous initiative and police instruction are different accounts of the same act. Kolvet's version is in his own words on his own account, so this is a documented internal inconsistency rather than an opponent's characterisation. It matters because the police-direction account was the most exculpatory explanation available and it is now contradicted from within.

findings.claim: The theft-prevention explanation is internally coherent
findings.detail: It has a logical difficulty that deserves stating regardless of who raised it. If the concern was that property would be stolen from an abandoned position in a panicking crowd, the rational response is to secure the camera body, which is worth thousands, rather than to extract a memory card worth on the order of fifteen dollars and leave the camera behind. Owens makes this argument and it stands on its own terms; this app credits it while noting her documented unreliability elsewhere in this case, because an argument's validity does not depend on its author. There is a possible reconciliation: a person may value the irreplaceable recording over replaceable hardware, in which case 'so no one steals them' means the footage rather than the equipment. That reading is coherent, and it also concedes the point that matters — the object of the exercise was custody of the recording.

findings.claim: Farnsworth filming and declaring Kirk dead indicates foreknowledge
findings.detail: The same reasoning applies here that this app applied to Mikey McCoy and to Victor Marx, and consistency is the point. Footage circulated by Candace Owens is said to show him recording rather than assisting, and saying 'he's dead' toward the end. He is the AV lead; operating cameras in a crisis is the thing he is there to do, and he was not the medical or security response. On the death declaration, this app has already established through timestamped Wikipedia revisions that people worldwide were inferring death from the footage within an hour, and a man standing feet away with a direct line of sight to a catastrophic neck wound had far better grounds for that inference than any of them. The footage itself reaches the public through an X account with no established provenance and TPUSA has not commented, so even its integrity is unestablished.

findings.claim: Robinson's defence counsel Michael Burt is Farnsworth's cousin
findings.detail: Unverified, and the claim is self-defeating against the record it draws on. Burt's role is real and documented — he is co-counsel on Robinson's defence, a capital specialist who represented Lyle Menendez at the first trial. The family relation is asserted by an X account and associated blogs and is confirmed by no genealogical, court or public record; even automated checks run by the accounts promoting it returned that no reliable source establishes a relation. The framing should also be named plainly: the material presenting it does so under a 'Mormon Mafia' banner, which is an ethno-religious conspiracy frame rather than an evidentiary one. And the theory it serves — that a compromised defence is steering Robinson into a patsy role — is contradicted by the same hearing in which this entry's central finding arose. It was Robinson's defence that objected to the TPUSA authentication and won a ruling forcing the state to produce original footage. A defence in on a frame does not do that.

findings.claim: This matters mainly because of what Farnsworth may have intended
findings.detail: It matters mainly because of what happened, and the distinction is what keeps this finding usable. The most probable explanation for the conduct is the most boring one: an AV technician whose instinct after a catastrophe is to secure his gear and his footage, possibly on an officer's instruction, doing it without a thought for chain of custody because chain of custody is not his job. Assume that is exactly what happened and every evidentiary consequence remains identical. Original media from the best-positioned camera was not seized at the scene, the state ended up authenticating video through the statement of the private party who handled it, a judge found that insufficient, and three of four supplied angles remain unseen publicly. Those are facts about the record, not about a man's character, and they are the ones worth carrying forward.

findings.claim: This app has assessed the newly released footage
findings.detail: It has not and should not be read as having done so. Owens released material on an approximately 55-minute livestream on August 18, 2026, since archived with roughly 277,000 views, in which she lists what she calls ten verifiable lies and states she has every second of Farnsworth's movements, including a claim that about four minutes after Kirk was carried to the SUV he went to the camera positioned behind Kirk's head. YouTube has generated no captions for the stream and none were available at the time of writing, so this app has no transcript and cannot evaluate what the footage shows. The findings recorded above rest on the Kolvet and Bowyer statements, which are independently documented. One further provenance claim circulating — that Farnsworth himself showed Owens the material and she recorded it on her phone — rests on a single social media account and is not established; if true it would be significant, since it would make the subject of the allegation its source.

findings.claim: APP OPERATOR'S OWN ACCOUNT of the Owens footage (source: direct viewing, not examined by this app)
findings.detail: Recorded as a first-hand observation by this app's operator, who watched the August 18, 2026 livestream directly. This app has not seen the footage — no captions were generated and the audio could not be retrieved — so nothing below is verified here and it should not be cited as though it were. The account: Farnsworth is standing over a camera and begins looking around; he removes the SD card from ONE of FOUR cameras; he walks back a few feet into the first section of a walkway that has a second-storey building directly overhead; in the walkway he places the single card into a side pocket; he then appears to take out a phone and make a call. The countable element is the one that matters and is checkable independently of the video: one card taken, four cameras present.

findings.claim: The 'one of four' detail is consistent with either TPUSA explanation
findings.detail: If accurate it defeats both, and that is why it is worth pursuing. Kolvet's account is that the staffer acted to stop the cards being stolen; securing property does not mean extracting a single memory card and leaving three cameras and three further cards behind. Bowyer's account is that police commanded him to take down the cameras; a compliance narrative does not end with four cameras still standing and one card removed. The same fact also cuts against evidence destruction, which would require taking all four. What one card from four is consistent with is selection — prioritising the angle that mattered. That reading has an entirely ordinary version, since an audio-visual lead knows immediately which camera held the critical view and securing it first is competent behaviour under pressure, and he may have been moved on before reaching the others. It also has a less ordinary version, since selection implies knowing which camera mattered and acting on it within roughly four minutes. Nothing in the observation distinguishes those two.

findings.claim: The behavioural elements of the account are probative
findings.detail: They are weak individually and this app applies to them the same reasoning it applied to Mikey McCoy and Victor Marx. Moving under a second-storey overhang roughly four minutes after a shot fired from an elevated position, with the shooter unaccounted for, is what everyone on that campus had reason to do; reading it as evasion requires ignoring that the obvious motive for seeking overhead cover was not wanting to be shot. Looking around after gunfire is universal. Placing a small object in a pocket is how a person carries it when hands are needed, and Kolvet states the cards reached the FBI, so pocketing is concealment only if something shows it was never handed over. Taking out a phone in the first minutes is expected of staff, and this app has already established that a colleague was making the call to Erika Kirk in that window. The behavioural read does not move; the arithmetic one does.

findings.claim: OPERATOR ACCOUNT: no law enforcement officer appears to be directing him, and the card came from the rear wide-angle camera
findings.detail: Second observation from this app's operator, again from direct viewing of footage this app has not examined. No officer is visible directing him at the moment shown, and the camera from which the card was taken appears to be the rear wide-angle unit positioned behind Kirk — the frame covering the platform he was set up on with the equipment visible, Kirk himself, and the crowd in front of him. Two consequences if accurate. First, this is the first direct evidence bearing on contradiction X50, and it points against Tyler Bowyer's account that police commanded the removal, consistent with Andrew Kolvet's own description of spontaneous initiative; the qualification is that absence of an officer in one frame is not proof no instruction was given earlier off camera. Second, of the four cameras this is the one with the widest evidentiary value — not merely the best view of the shooting but the frame documenting stage layout, equipment positions, the victim and crowd behaviour simultaneously. That sharpens rather than settles the selection question: it is both the angle a competent AV lead would secure first and the angle whose loss would matter most.

findings.claim: The released footage is narrower than the camera's normal field of view
findings.detail: Claimed with a real control group, which is why it merits recording. A commentary channel compared the American Comeback Tour's setup across a stated 18-plus campus stops — naming USC, San Francisco, San Diego, Long Beach, Boise, Washington State and others — and reports that the rear camera is a wide-angle unit consistently used as such, with the ground around Kirk visible in every prior event. In the material Farnsworth showed Candace Owens, the ground is not visible. The stated inference is that either the framing was changed that day or the footage was zoomed afterwards. This app's operator independently reports the same impression of heavy cropping. The methodology is sound in structure: an established baseline across many instances, tested against the anomalous one. But a decisive caveat sits inside the claim itself, and the video states it: Owens did not receive raw footage. She screen-recorded Farnsworth showing it to her. A screen recording of another person's playback establishes nothing about the framing of the source file, since the zoom may belong to the display, the player window, or the recording. Rated plausible rather than supported for that reason.

findings.claim: This adds to a documented pattern about the completeness of the video record
findings.detail: A narrower pattern than this app previously stated, now corrected against the primary transcript. Preliminary-hearing testimony does establish that Visual Impulse supplied four videos and that only one was shown. But the claim that Judge Graf excluded an enhanced compilation containing zooms and circles describes a DIFFERENT video entirely — UVU's own surveillance compilation (exhibits 12.1/12.4), built by the county attorney's office, not by TPUSA or Farnsworth, and addressed in a separate Deep Dive and in anomaly A4. That version was not excluded; it was admitted for the court's private review after UVU's own custodian authenticated it, while a clean version was published publicly. And the claim that Graf required original unaltered footage specifically for the TPUSA video is withdrawn, since the actual ruling on that video was an overruled objection and admission, restricted from publication for victim-dignity reasons the state itself requested. The genuine documented items are: four videos supplied, one shown; the SD card leaving the scene before investigators took possession; and two mutually exclusive TPUSA explanations for why. That remains a real pattern. It should not be padded with rulings the transcript does not support.

findings.claim: The other claims in that comparison video are equally well founded
findings.detail: They are not, and the difference in quality within a single video is instructive. The assertion that the audio-visual and security team positions were reversed at UVU relative to prior stops is checkable and may be accurate, but venue geometry dictates placement — a sunken courtyard with fixed seating constrains stage orientation, cable runs, sightlines and sun position in ways an open quad does not — so deviation is expected rather than anomalous without an account of the site. The body-language analysis of a named security team member is weaker still: covering the mouth while speaking into a lapel microphone is standard protective-detail practice, taught to prevent lip-reading and reduce ambient pickup, so the one behaviour presented as most suspicious is the one most clearly indicating training. Arms folded versus at the sides falls within ordinary variation, and an observer scanning for postural differences will find them between any two clips of anyone. The claim that an object in a bystander's pocket in a photograph is the size of a microphone is shape-of-a-blob analysis of the same class this app rejected regarding the vehicle interior photographs. Note also the video's stated purpose: it is pursuing the exploding-microphone theory and wants the ground visible in order to look for device debris. That theory is refuted in this app by independent acoustic evidence of a supersonic projectile in flight. A sound observation can be made in service of a failed theory, and the cropping question survives on its own merits.

fact_check_gap: Whether an officer instructed TPUSA staff to secure equipment remains the load-bearing question and is answerable from an incident report, radio log or that officer's testimony, none of which either side has produced. Two further questions now sit alongside it and are answerable from the hearing record rather than from any video: which of the four cameras the removed card belonged to — specifically whether it was the unit positioned behind Kirk with the direct angle — and whether all four cards are accounted for in discovery. Testimony already establishes that Visual Impulse supplied four videos, which suggests all four were eventually produced; if so, the significance of the single removal is that one angle was prioritised, not that any angle was withheld. Nobody appears to have asked either question.

title: Tracing Robinson's Path: Measured Distances, and the Shot Time Settled at 12:23:28
summary: The full documented path across UVU on September 10, rebuilt from testimony and measured against real building coordinates pulled from OpenStreetMap. Every walking leg checks out at ordinary pace — nothing in the route is physically impossible or even hurried. The anomalies are elsewhere: an unexplained 21-minute gap between campus entry and roof access, and four different official times for the shot spanning 18 minutes.
sources_quality: A for the geometry, computed from OpenStreetMap centroids and reproducible; A for the timeline, now taken from the Day 2 preliminary-hearing transcript in which Agent Hull gives times to the second under oath, superseding the secondary reporting this entry previously relied on; NOT ESTABLISHED for the recurring white SUV
key_takeaway: The hearing transcript settles it. Agent Hull, under oath: the reported shot was fired at 12:23:28. That confirms the figure this app has used throughout and disposes of the competing values — UVU's same-day 12:10 was approximate, and the 12:20 and 12:28 figures in circulation are reporting errors. Hull's sequence, with timestamps read from the video: vehicle arrives at the parking structure about 8:30; back at the vehicle from the amphitheatre area about 9:25; returns on foot just after 10:00 carrying a blue backpack; accesses the Losee staircase and walks off campus just prior to 11:00; approaches the Losee exterior staircase about 12:15; on the roof at the southwest corner crawling to the edge at a video timestamp of 12:22 into 12:23; shot at 12:23:28; off the roof at 12:24:42. Against measured distances the movement is unremarkable — the longest leg, Gunther to Losee at 232 metres, is under three minutes at ordinary pace, and Losee to the Sorensen Student Center beside the courtyard measures 112 metres, independently reproducing the reported shot distance of roughly 130 to 140 yards. Two numbers now sharpen: the figure was on the roof about eight and a half minutes before firing, and the interval between the shot and leaving the roof was 74 seconds.

findings.claim: The walking legs require an implausible pace
findings.detail: They do not, and the measured numbers leave no room for argument. The longest single documented leg is Gunther Technology to Losee Center at 232 metres, which is under three minutes at a normal 1.4 metres per second and under four minutes at a slow amble. The morning route through Gunther, then Computer Science, then the Losee railing totals roughly 300 metres of outdoor movement. The final approach from the Institute of Religion to Losee is 133 metres, about 95 seconds. Every leg is comfortably achievable, and the one independently timestamped pair available — 11:51 campus entry and the 11:53:07 staircase clip — yields almost exactly the walking time the geometry predicts. Whoever the figure on camera is, the route as described is walkable at an unhurried pace with time to spare, and no distance-versus-time impossibility exists anywhere in it.

findings.claim: The 21-minute gap this entry previously reported was real
findings.detail: It was an artefact of mixing two sources and is withdrawn. An earlier revision set a Fox News figure of an 11:51 campus entry, with an 11:53:07 staircase timestamp from circulated footage, against Hull's testimony placing roof access about 12:15, and reported roughly 21 unaccounted minutes. The Day 2 transcript contains no 11:51 entry. Hull's own sequence is internally consistent: the figure walks off campus just prior to 11:00 and is next placed approaching the Losee exterior staircase about 12:15. The genuine unobserved window is therefore the roughly 75 minutes spent off campus between those two points, which is not a gap in the surveillance so much as a period during which the subject was somewhere else and for which no account has been published. Where the Fox 11:51 figure originates is unresolved; it may describe a re-entry within that window that Hull did not narrate, or it may be an error. Either way this app should not have built a finding on a timeline assembled across two sources when a transcript was available.

findings.claim: The time of the shot is settled
findings.detail: Four published values span eighteen minutes, which for the single most basic fact in the case is a remarkable state of affairs. UVU's own post on the day said a shot was fired at about 12:10. One Fox account of the route gives 12:20. CBS reported a single gunshot heard in the quad at 12:23, which is the figure this app has used throughout and which is consistent with Hull's sequence of roof access about 12:15 and crawling to the edge by 12:22. Hearing coverage from Fox and East Idaho News reports Robinson remaining on the roof until 12:28, when Kirk was shot. Some of this is the ordinary drift of early reporting — UVU's same-day figure was necessarily approximate — but 12:20, 12:23 and 12:28 all postdate the hearing and cannot all be right. The consequence is direct: whether the figure lay prone for five minutes or thirteen before firing is not currently answerable from public sources, and that interval is exactly what an exposure analysis would need.

findings.claim: A midsize white SUV recurs near Robinson in the footage
findings.detail: This app could not corroborate it and records that plainly rather than dismissing it. No source located — testimony coverage, charging materials, or reporting — describes a white SUV in proximity to the figure identified as Robinson. The vehicle in the record is a dark grey or charcoal Dodge Challenger of the 2008-2014 generation, which arrived at the parking garage about 8:29 and was seen leaving shortly before 9:30. The only other vehicle documented anywhere in the sequence is a passing van that Robinson is said to have narrowly avoided while sprinting across Campus Drive after the shot. An observation drawn from watching footage directly is not worthless because reporting has not picked it up — reporters were not looking for background vehicles — but it cannot be entered as a finding without a frame reference, a timestamp and a camera. Note separately that this app's existing vehicle analysis already flags wheel-style discrepancies between the confirmed Challenger and surveillance stills, so the vehicle identification thread is genuinely open on its own terms.

findings.claim: The observation that the video contains many cuts is well founded
findings.detail: It is, and this app has now traced why from several directions at once. What was shown is a compilation rather than continuous footage. Hearing testimony establishes that Visual Impulse supplied four video angles and that only one was presented, with the witness agreeing other angles existed. Judge Tony Graf excluded the state's enhanced version containing zooms and circles. The TPUSA material reached investigators as a copy on a flash drive after the SD card was removed from the camera behind Kirk, and Graf sustained a further objection requiring the state to produce original unaltered footage. Circulating analysis additionally points to timestamp jumps and a 26-second gap. Cuts in a compilation are ordinary and expected; a compilation assembled from privately handled copies, with three of four angles unseen and two adverse judicial rulings on video integrity, is why the ordinary thing is worth noticing here.

findings.claim: The measured campus geometry corroborates the reported shot distance
findings.detail: It does, which is a useful independent check on the official reconstruction. Losee Center to Sorensen Student Center, adjacent to the courtyard where Kirk was speaking, measures 112 metres centre to centre, about 367 feet or 122 yards. Actual firing position to actual seated position would differ somewhat since both are points rather than building centroids, and the elevated firing position adds slant range. That places the true distance in the region of 130 to 145 yards, matching the roughly 130 to 140 yards reported. Independently reproducing a headline figure from public map data is worth doing precisely because it is one of the few numbers in this case that can be checked without relying on anyone's testimony, and it holds.

findings.claim: The shot-to-departure interval is 74 seconds
findings.detail: Hull gives the shot at 12:23:28 and the figure jumping from the roof at a video timestamp of 12:24:42, an interval of 74 seconds spent on the roof after firing before descending. That number materially reinforces a finding this app reached earlier on weaker grounds. In testing the proposal that a second operator was positioned to eliminate Robinson and was defeated by a weapon malfunction, this app argued that immediate-action clearance takes a trained operator two to four seconds while Robinson's escape took appreciably longer, so a cleared weapon would still have had a firing opportunity. That argument was made without the actual interval. It is 74 seconds, during which the figure stood, ran north across the roof and dropped to the ground in the open. A cleared weapon would have had more than a minute of opportunity, which strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion.

findings.claim: Reports of a man in black tactical gear with a long gun on a roof are real, and describe Robinson
findings.detail: The reports are real and the timing rules Robinson out. Dispatch audio at 12:27:00 reports a person on the roof of a building carrying a long rifle, with a later transmission adding black tactical gear and a helmet; a dispatcher's description circulated as all black, black long gun, black tactical helmet, black mask, possibly a tactical vest, and jeans. That description became the initial public picture of the suspect. But Hull's timestamps place the shot at 12:23:28 and the figure off the roof at 12:24:42. The dispatch call is timestamped 12:27:00 — two minutes and eighteen seconds after Robinson had already left the roof. Whoever was seen on a roof in tactical gear at 12:27 was not Robinson, who was gone, and was almost certainly a responding officer: armed officers were converging, the perimeter around Losee expanded at 12:29, and radio traffic at 12:30 carried a since-corrected report of shots near the library. The documented clothing also does not match — Robinson is described in a black T-shirt bearing an American flag, not a helmet, mask and vest. This additionally supports the existing explanation for the unfired cartridge recovered on an adjacent roof, offered in testimony as an officer having cycled a patrol rifle: the dispatch traffic is independent evidence that armed personnel in tactical gear were on rooftops within minutes of the shot.

findings.claim: Circulating video said to show a second shooter has held up
findings.detail: The two most-circulated examples both fail on basic checks performed by fact-checkers rather than on interpretation. A video presenting two clips as showing the shooter in action was found to show the wrong building in one of them: it depicts a structure to Kirk's right, an impossible firing angle, while the accurate clip shows the Losee Center rooftop across from him. Separately, footage promoted as showing the shooter fleeing toward a parking lot was filmed on July 28, more than a month before the killing. That date is worth noting on its own account — the same erroneous July 28 date attaches to the article promoting the Mikey McCoy footage claim examined elsewhere in this app, which suggests a single miscaptioned clip recirculating with a stale timestamp attached.

title: The Vehicle That Took Kirk to Hospital, and the Self-Transport Decision
summary: Kirk was not taken by ambulance. His own protective detail carried him to a private SUV and drove him roughly four miles to Timpanogos Regional Hospital, with the door held open the whole way because he was too tall to fit inside with it closed. That decision is defensible under protective doctrine and is also the single most consequential medical choice made that day. It additionally offers the most economical explanation for a mid-size SUV recurring in campus footage.
sources_quality: A- for the transport itself, which is on video and described consistently by two named eyewitnesses close to Kirk; B for the four-mile distance and the door detail, from Frank Turek's and Rob McCoy's accounts; NOT ESTABLISHED for the claim that standby EMS were prevented from reaching him; C for the 2:40 p.m. pronouncement time, which may be an artefact of timezone conversion
key_takeaway: Video shows Kirk carried by six men to a waiting SUV. He was moved by his own security detail in a private vehicle rather than by ambulance, driven roughly four miles to Timpanogos Regional Hospital in Orem, and the car door could not be closed for the journey because of his height. Two named eyewitnesses in his circle have described the drive: Frank Turek, who said afterwards that better first aid, better medical facilities or a faster trip might have saved him and that they could not manage it, and Rob McCoy, who has given an account of the final moments. The decision to self-transport is not obviously wrong — 'scoop and run' to definitive care is recognised protective-detail practice, particularly for a penetrating neck wound where the intervention needed is surgical and cannot be delivered at the roadside. But it is a decision rather than a necessity, and it becomes the day's most consequential medical choice given that reporting indicates EMS were on standby. For this app's purposes it also does useful work on a separate question: a mid-size SUV appearing repeatedly near the event in campus footage is most economically explained as the protective detail's own vehicle, which by definition stays close to the principal and was staged for rapid egress.

findings.claim: Kirk was transported by ambulance
findings.detail: He was not. He was moved by his own security detail in a private vehicle to Timpanogos Regional Hospital, which is on video: six men carrying him to a waiting SUV, which then leaves campus. Timpanogos is roughly four miles from the UVU Orem campus. Accounts from Kirk's circle add that the vehicle door could not be closed during the drive because he was too tall to fit with it shut, meaning the door was held open for the entire journey. This is one of the few elements of the day that is both fully documented on video and uncontested by any party.

findings.claim: Self-transport was an obvious error
findings.detail: It is a defensible choice and this app is not qualified to second-guess it, though it should be recorded as a choice. Moving a principal off the point of attack immediately is standard protective doctrine, and for a penetrating neck wound the intervention required is surgical: the treatment is an operating theatre, not a roadside. Against a four-mile transit, waiting for an ambulance to arrive, load and depart can plausibly cost more time than it saves. What cuts the other way is that an ambulance carries suction, airway management and blood-product capability that a passenger seat does not, and reporting indicates EMS were on standby at the venue rather than absent. Turek's own account — that better first aid, better facilities or a faster trip might have saved him — is the most direct available comment and comes from someone who was there.

findings.claim: Standby EMS were prevented from reaching Kirk
findings.detail: Circulated in late October 2025 as video said to show EMS personnel held back while the detail loaded Kirk for private transport, and asserted by accounts identifying themselves as part of the on-site response. It has not been established in court, in any after-action review, or in any agency statement, and this app has not obtained the footage or verified its framing. The distinction that matters is between EMS being actively prevented, which would be a serious allegation, and a detail simply moving faster than EMS could deploy, which is the ordinary dynamic of a protective evacuation and implies nothing. Nothing located distinguishes the two. The claim is recorded because it circulates widely and because the underlying fact it rests on — that EMS were present and did not transport — appears to be true.

findings.claim: Kirk was pronounced dead at 2:40 p.m.
findings.detail: Reported, but the figure warrants a caution this app has not seen raised anywhere. 2:40 p.m. Mountain time is exactly 4:40 p.m. Eastern, which is the documented moment Trump posted the confirmation of Kirk's death on Truth Social. That coincidence may be genuine — the President plausibly posted immediately on being told — but it is also precisely the shape of a reporting artefact, in which a widely-cited announcement time is converted into local time and then repeated as the clinical pronouncement time. This app has not located a medical examiner or hospital record establishing the pronouncement independently. Given the shot is now fixed at 12:23:28, the interval between wounding and pronouncement is a real quantity of interest and it currently rests on a number that may be circular.

findings.claim: The transport vehicle explains the recurring mid-size SUV in campus footage
findings.detail: It is the most economical explanation available and is offered as a hypothesis rather than a finding. A protective detail's vehicle is staged close to the principal's location for exactly the contingency that occurred, and is moved and repositioned during an event; it would therefore appear repeatedly in campus footage covering the courtyard and surrounding drives, including in frames that also contain other people moving through the same area. Kirk's detail was an eight-person private team, so more than one vehicle may have been present. This does not confirm any particular sighting: without a frame, a timestamp and a camera identifier this app cannot match an observed vehicle to the detail's. But it means a recurring SUV near the venue is expected rather than anomalous, and any analysis of such sightings should exclude the detail's vehicles first.

findings.claim: The self-transport bears on the security-failure finding
findings.detail: It belongs to the same picture, though it is a distinct issue from the one this app rates at 96-99%. That finding concerns pre-event posture — unmonitored rooftops with clear sightlines, roughly six campus officers for 3,000 attendees, and the disputed handling of a rooftop warning. Medical response is a separate limb of event planning: what casualty care was arranged, where EMS were staged, and what the evacuation plan was. On the available record the detail improvised a transport in a passenger vehicle that could not accommodate the casualty with the door shut, which suggests no rehearsed medical evacuation plan was in place, or that one existed and was not used. Either way it is an event-planning question of the same family, and it is one the withheld security plan would answer.

fact_check_gap: Three things nobody appears to have established. Whether EMS were staged at the venue and what their instructions were, which would settle the prevented-access claim in either direction and should exist in event documentation. Whether an independent record fixes the pronouncement time, given that the widely-repeated 2:40 p.m. is exactly Trump's 4:40 p.m. Eastern post converted to Mountain time. And what the event's medical evacuation plan actually provided for — a question that falls squarely inside the security plan UVU has declined to release and that the targeted records request drafted elsewhere in this app does not currently ask for.

Frank Turek's account of the drive and his statement that better first aid, better facilities or a faster trip might have saved him
Rob McCoy's account of Kirk's final moments during the transport

title: The RØDE Mic Theory, the SUV Photos, and the Acoustic Evidence That Settles It
summary: The claim that Kirk was killed by a lavalier microphone or battery pack rigged with a shaped charge rather than by a bullet, with photographs said to show the interior of the transport SUV offered as corroboration. The autopsy disposes of it: five bullet fragments were recovered from the body, including a jacket fragment, and the wound track runs from the cervical spine down into the thorax and up into the cranium. That is a projectile path. A charge at the throat cannot produce it.
sources_quality: A for the acoustic analysis, from Rob Maher of Montana State University, the leading academic authority on gunshot audio forensics, working from recordings made at the podium; A for the casing identification and fragment examination, given first-hand by ATF examiner Samantha Carner under cross-examination; B for the autopsy findings, which reached the record through an investigator relaying a sealed report without the medical examiner present; F for the SUV photographs
key_takeaway: The theory holds that a lavalier microphone or battery pack — in one telling a RØDE unit — carried a shaped charge that detonated at Kirk's throat, with photographs said to show the transport SUV's interior offered as corroboration because they contain small black shards described as device shrapnel. The acoustic record disposes of it independently of any medical evidence. Rob Maher of Montana State University, the leading academic authority on gunshot audio forensics, found the crack-and-pop signature of a supersonic rifle shot in audio recorded near the podium, with roughly 240 milliseconds between the ballistic shock wave and the muzzle blast. A ballistic crack is an N-wave produced only by an object travelling through air faster than sound, and the separation between crack and blast encodes the distance to the muzzle — analysts derived roughly 153 metres, the same neighbourhood as the 112-metre Losee-to-courtyard measurement this app computed from map data once firing position and slant range are allowed for. A charge at the victim's throat produces one report, from one place, with no crack and no separation. Supporting this: the spent casing was positively identified to the recovered rifle by firing pin impression, and the fragments were determined to be .30 calibre, both from live cross-examined testimony by ATF examiner Samantha Carner. The autopsy adds the internal wound path — C2 through C7, cervical cord transected, energy carried into thorax and cranium, five fragments recovered, cause of death gunshot wound to the neck — but that evidence reached the record through an investigator relaying a sealed report without the medical examiner present, and is the weakest link in the chain rather than the strongest.

findings.claim: A microphone or battery pack explosive caused the fatal wound
findings.detail: Refuted by the autopsy on two independent grounds. First, five bullet fragments were recovered from the body, including a deformed jacket fragment; these were examined by the ATF and shown to the court. A bullet jacket inside a body is not produced by a device attached to clothing. Second, the wound track is wrong for a surface detonation by a wide margin: damage to the left side of C2 through C7, the cervical cord transected with a significant portion traumatically absent, energy carried down into the thorax to damage heart and lungs and up into the cranium to damage the brain. That is a deep axial projectile track with the remote energy transfer characteristic of a high-velocity rifle round. A shaped charge at the throat would leave burns, blast effect and surface fragmentation, all of which a medical examiner would document and none of which is reported. Cause of death was recorded as gunshot wound to the neck, manner homicide.

findings.claim: An audible report establishes that a bullet was fired
findings.detail: It does not, and this app stated it carelessly before being challenged on it. A single undifferentiated bang establishes a rapid pressure event — an explosion of some kind — and is consistent with a gunshot without being diagnostic of one. Blanks, pyrotechnics and a stationary charge all produce reports. Anyone reasoning from 'three thousand people heard a shot' to 'a projectile traversed space' is skipping a step, and the mic theory exists precisely in that gap. The correction matters because the acoustic evidence in this case is far better than an audible report, and citing the weak version obscures the strong one.

findings.claim: The acoustic record independently establishes a supersonic projectile in flight
findings.detail: It does, and this is the finding that resolves the mechanism question without relying on the sealed autopsy at all. Rob Maher of Montana State University, the leading academic authority on gunshot audio forensics, analysed audio captured near the podium and identified the signature crack-and-pop pattern of a supersonic rifle shot, with roughly 240 milliseconds separating the ballistic shock wave from the muzzle blast. The physics is what makes this decisive. The crack is an N-wave, a shock cone generated only by an object moving through air faster than sound; it cannot be produced by anything stationary. The pop is the muzzle blast from the weapon. The two reach a microphone by different paths and therefore arrive separated by an interval that encodes distance, and analysts working from that 240-millisecond figure derived a shooter roughly 153 metres away depending on assumed velocity. That is the same neighbourhood as the 112-metre Losee-to-courtyard measurement this app computed from map data once actual firing position and slant range are allowed for. A charge detonating at the victim's throat produces one report from one location with no crack, no separation and no distance term. The recording contains all three.

findings.claim: The recovered fragments are of indeterminate calibre
findings.detail: They were determined to be .30 calibre, which is consistent with the .30-06 rifle recovered and is a determination separate from the inconclusive toolmark comparison. This distinction is routinely collapsed in coverage and should not be. Calibre and general rifling class can often be established from deformed fragments by measurement and material analysis; individualising a fragment to one specific barrel requires continuous striation detail that fragmentation destroys, which is why Carner reported neither sufficient agreement nor disagreement. So the fragments are .30 calibre jacketed bullet material consistent with the recovered weapon, and are not individualised to it. Both statements are true simultaneously.

findings.claim: The autopsy findings rest on evidence the public or the defence could test
findings.detail: They do not, and this app previously stated the autopsy evidence more firmly than the record supports. The medical examiner did not testify at the preliminary hearing. The report was introduced through State Bureau of Investigation Agent David Hull — an investigator, not a pathologist — relaying its contents. Defence counsel Kathryn Nester objected in terms that name the problem precisely: an expert report without an expert present, leaving no foundation to test credibility and no opportunity to cross-examine. Judge Graf overruled every hearsay objection except the one to the edited video compilation, and admitted the report. Utah's rules expressly permit reliable hearsay at a preliminary hearing, so this is procedurally normal and not a defect — the standard there is probable cause, not proof. But the consequence for anyone assessing the evidence today is real: the wound path, the recovery of five fragments from the body, and the cause and manner of death all reach the public as an investigator's summary of a document that Utah law makes non-public, unexamined by the person who wrote it. Nobody outside the case has read it, and nobody has questioned its author under oath.

findings.claim: The fragments are established as bullet fragments by first-hand expert testimony
findings.detail: This link is stronger than the provenance link and the distinction matters. ATF firearms examiner Samantha Carner testified in person and was subject to cross-examination. She examined the recovered material as bullet fragments and attempted a toolmark comparison against the rifle, reporting neither sufficient agreement nor sufficient disagreement. Identifying jacketed bullet material — copper alloy jacketing with a lead core, and its characteristic deformation — is a routine and reliable identification within a firearms examiner's expertise, and is a far easier determination than matching a fragment to a particular barrel. So the proposition that these are pieces of a fired bullet rests on live, cross-examined expert testimony. The separate proposition that they came out of Kirk's body rests on the medical examiner's report, relayed second-hand. Those two links are not equally well supported and should not be cited as though they were.

findings.claim: The black shards in the SUV photographs are device shrapnel
findings.detail: Assume for argument that the photographs are genuine. Kirk was wearing a lavalier microphone with a battery pack, a fact nobody disputes and which is the premise of the theory itself. He was then lifted and carried by six men into a vehicle in an emergency, and driven roughly four miles with the door held open because he did not fit inside with it closed. A clip-on plastic transmitter subjected to that is very likely to be torn loose, dropped, trodden on and broken, and broken plastic looks like small black shards. Their presence establishes that the microphone assembly came apart, which everyone already expects; it does not establish that it detonated. The distinguishing evidence between a broken device and an exploded one is not in the vehicle at all, it is in the body, and the body contained five bullet fragments and no reported blast injury.

findings.claim: The photographs are FBI crime-scene material
findings.detail: Their provenance is unestablished at every step. Reporting describes them only as reportedly documented by the FBI and as leaked, without specifying by whom or from where. No official source has authenticated them, confirmed they depict the transport vehicle, or commented on them at all. They surfaced on March 12, 2026 through a viral X post and were subsequently amplified on Candace Owens's podcast. There is a sourcing convergence worth recording: the account that introduced the analysis is the same one this app assessed separately as the origin of the unverified claim that Robinson's defence counsel is Terryl Farnsworth's cousin, promoted under a 'Mormon Mafia' banner. That does not make these images fake, but it means the same unverified channel is supplying material in two separate strands of this case, and neither strand has produced a document.

findings.claim: A single gauze pack visible in the vehicle indicates deliberately withheld treatment
findings.detail: It indicates the transport this app documented separately. The detail performed a scoop-and-run: Kirk was carried to a private vehicle rather than waiting for an ambulance and driven about four miles to Timpanogos Regional Hospital. In that posture the intervention that matters is surgical and happens at the destination; roadside care in a passenger seat is limited to what hands can do. More to the point, the injury described in the autopsy — cervical cord transected with a portion absent, damage through the thorax to heart and lungs and into the cranium — is not a bleed that gauze addresses. The absence of extensive visible dressings is what this wound and this evacuation method would produce. Whether self-transport was the right call is a legitimate question and is assessed separately in this app; it is not evidence of intent.

findings.claim: The visible bulge under Kirk's shirt supports the device theory
findings.detail: Fact-checkers examining the footage concluded the bulge was consistent with a magnetic microphone Kirk regularly wore, and that the bleeding visible in the video is consistent with a gunshot wound rather than a concealed device. The bulge is in fact evidence for the mundane account: he wore a lavalier rig at every event, and it is visible in footage from events at which nothing happened. An object that appears in months of prior video is poor evidence of a bomb planted for one occasion.

findings.claim: The autopsy report is publicly available for independent review
findings.detail: It is not, and that limitation should be stated plainly since it is the reason theories like this persist. Under Utah law autopsy reports are not public documents and may be released only to next of kin, law enforcement, a legal representative, and a physician who attended the deceased. What is publicly known comes through the preliminary hearing: Agent Hull confirming the cause and manner of death from the report, the five recovered fragments displayed to the court, and the described wound path. That is substantial and it is sworn, but it is a summary presented by an investigator rather than a document any member of the public can read. The evidence available is sufficient to refute this theory; it is not sufficient to satisfy someone who distrusts the institutions relaying it, which is a different problem and not one more testimony will solve.

findings.claim: This evidentiary gap persists into trial
findings.detail: It should close, and the mechanism is well established. The Confrontation Clause applies with full force at trial, and forensic reports are testimonial: Melendez-Diaz established that a defendant is entitled to confront the analyst, and Bullcoming established that surrogate testimony by someone who did not perform the analysis does not satisfy that right. Agent Hull relaying another professional's autopsy findings is precisely the posture Bullcoming addresses, and it is permitted now only because a preliminary hearing operates under a lower standard. To convict on this evidence the state will in the ordinary course need the medical examiner on the stand and available for cross-examination. That is also when the defence gets to probe chain of custody from body to laboratory, which has not been publicly detailed by anyone. The current gap is a function of the stage of proceedings rather than a permanent feature, but it is genuinely open right now.

findings.claim: The refutation of the mic theory depends entirely on the autopsy
findings.detail: It does not, and this app's previous concession that it largely did was too generous. That concession was written before locating the acoustic work, and the acoustic work is independent of the autopsy in every respect: it is physics performed on a recording by a named academic expert, requiring no access to the body, no medical examiner, and no sealed document. It establishes a supersonic projectile in flight arriving from roughly the distance the campus geometry predicts. Alongside it stand the spent casing positively identified to the recovered rifle by firing pin impression and the .30 calibre determination on the fragments, both from live cross-examined testimony, plus the rifle recovered along the escape route carrying DNA and a figure recorded prone on the Losee roof. The autopsy uniquely supplies the internal wound path, and that link genuinely does rest on relayed hearsay until the medical examiner testifies. But the mechanism question — whether a bullet flew or a device detonated — is answered by the acoustics alone.

fact_check_gap: Two gaps, pointing in opposite directions. The autopsy is sealed by Utah statute, its author has never been questioned under oath, and the chain of custody from autopsy table to ATF laboratory has not been publicly described — a genuine limitation that should close at trial, where Melendez-Diaz and Bullcoming require the analyst rather than a surrogate. Against that, the acoustic analysis is the strongest publicly available evidence on the mechanism of injury, is independent of every disputed institutional link in the case, and has been almost entirely absent from coverage of the competing injury theories. Proponents of those theories do not engage it, and the outlets debunking them lead with the autopsy instead — the one piece of evidence their audience is least disposed to accept and which currently rests on relayed hearsay.
external_sources: Rob Maher, Montana State University, audio forensics analysis of podium-adjacent recordings: crack-and-pop signature of a supersonic rifle shot, ~240 ms between ballistic shock wave and muzzle blast; derived shooter distance ~153 m depending on assumed velocity (CNN, Raw Story)
Fragment calibre determination: .30 calibre, consistent with the recovered .30-06, separate from the inconclusive individualising toolmark comparison (KUTV, PBS NewsHour, Forbes)

Preliminary hearing: Agent David Hull confirming the medical examiner's cause of death as gunshot wound to the neck and manner as homicide; five bullet fragments recovered at autopsy, including a deformed jacket fragment, displayed to the court

Autopsy-described wound path: left side of C2-C7 damaged, cervical spinal cord transected with a significant portion traumatically absent, extending into the thorax (heart and lungs) and cranium (brain)

title: Can a Match Be Predicted? Fragment Measurements, Class vs Individual Characteristics, and Why There Is No Probability
summary: What was actually recovered, what the ATF could and could not do with it, and whether a match likelihood can be calculated. The short answer to the last is no — firearms toolmark identification produces a subjective three-way conclusion, not a probability, and PCAST found the discipline short of foundational validity. The useful number is different: in validation studies the inconclusive rate exceeds one in three on pristine test material, which makes an inconclusive result on a jacket fragment recovered from bone close to the expected outcome.
sources_quality: A for the ATF report contents, which a judge unsealed in April 2026; A for the PCAST findings and the AFTE response, both published documents; the exact fragment masses and dimensions are NOT in any public reporting located and the analysis below is explicit about where that leaves things
key_takeaway: What was recovered at autopsy, per the unsealed ATF report: one deformed .30 calibre bullet jacket fragment and four lead fragments. The lead fragments were not suitable for microscopic comparison, which is expected — rifling engraves the jacket, not the core, so lead carries no comparable toolmarks. That means the entire comparison rested on a single deformed jacket fragment. The ATF found insufficient quality and quantity of individual characteristics and reported inconclusive; separately it positively identified the .30-06 cartridge case as fired from Robinson's Mauser. Exact masses in grains and dimensions in millimetres are not in any public reporting this app located, which matters because without recovered mass the one genuinely available independent check cannot be run. On predicting a match: it cannot be done numerically, and this is a property of the discipline rather than of this case. Firearms identification yields identification, inconclusive or elimination as an examiner's judgement under a 'sufficient agreement' standard. There is no likelihood ratio and no error rate attached to a specific conclusion. PCAST in 2016 found firearms analysis fell short of foundational validity on the ground that only one appropriately designed study existed; AFTE disputes that. The best available figures from the study PCAST accepted: a false positive rate estimated at about 1 in 66, upper confidence bound around 1 in 46, and an inconclusive rate above 1 in 3.

findings.claim: A match probability can be calculated for these fragments
findings.detail: No such calculation exists in this discipline, and expecting one imports a framework from DNA that firearms examination does not have. DNA typing produces likelihood ratios because allele frequencies in reference populations are known and the statistics are established. Toolmark comparison produces a categorical opinion — identification, inconclusive, or elimination — reached under the AFTE standard of 'sufficient agreement' of individual characteristics, which is explicitly a matter of trained examiner judgement rather than measurement against a validated scale. PCAST concluded in 2016 that firearms analysis fell short of foundational validity because only a single appropriately designed black-box study existed to estimate reliability, while noting it had not found the technique inaccurate as practised. AFTE rejects that conclusion. Whichever view one takes, the practical consequence is the same: nobody can state a percentage likelihood that this jacket fragment came from that barrel, and anyone offering one is inventing it.

findings.claim: The inconclusive result is surprising or suspicious
findings.detail: It is close to the expected outcome and there is a base rate to anchor that. In the validation study PCAST relied on, examiners working with cartridge cases from a single handgun type returned inconclusive results at a rate above one in three, and that was on comparison material in good condition. This case presents the opposite of good condition: a jacket fragment deformed by striking the cervical spine, which is exactly the mechanism that destroys the continuous striation detail comparison depends on. Add that four of the five recovered fragments were lead and therefore carried no rifling engraving at all, leaving one candidate object. An inconclusive finding here is what the physical circumstances predict, and this app has separately established that fragmentation is itself the predicted behaviour of an expanding hunting round striking bone.

findings.claim: Class characteristics and individual characteristics were both insufficient
findings.detail: They were not, and the distinction is the whole substance of what the fragments can and cannot show. Class characteristics are features shared by all firearms of a type: calibre, number of lands and grooves, direction of twist, land and groove widths. They are measurable on deformed material and they can exclude a weapon outright. Here they did not exclude: the jacket fragment was determined to be .30 calibre, consistent with the recovered .30-06 Mauser. Individual characteristics are the microscopic striae imparted by one specific barrel's imperfections, and identifying a particular weapon requires them. Those were insufficient in quality and quantity. So the correct statement of the evidence is that the fragment is consistent at class level with the recovered rifle and cannot be individualised to it. Both halves are true and coverage routinely reports only one.

findings.claim: The measurements needed to run an independent check are public
findings.detail: They are not, and their absence blocks the one useful test an outside analyst could actually perform. No public reporting located gives the recovered mass of the jacket fragment or the four lead fragments in grains, nor their dimensions. That matters because the ammunition class is known and its behaviour is characterised: a Remington Core-Lokt in .30-06 is loaded commonly at 150, 165 or 180 grains, and the design's mechanical jacket-to-core lock is documented to retain roughly 65 to 80 percent of original mass on expansion. Total recovered mass could therefore be compared against the 98 to 144 grain range those figures imply. A recovered total sitting inside that band would corroborate the stated round type and the stated mechanism; a total far below it would indicate either fragmentation beyond what the design predicts or incomplete recovery, and either would be worth knowing. The ATF report was unsealed by the court in April 2026, so the masses may well be in the document itself even though they have not reached reporting.

findings.claim: The casing identification carries the same uncertainty as the fragment comparison
findings.detail: It does not, and conflating the two is the most common error in commentary on this evidence. The spent .30-06 cartridge case was positively identified as having been fired in Robinson's Mauser. Breech face, firing pin and extractor marks are impressed on a case at the moment of discharge under high pressure against relatively soft brass, and the case is then not driven through a body at high velocity. Those marks survive; the bullet's rifling engraving did not. So one item in this evidence set produced a positive identification and another produced an inconclusive, and the difference is explained entirely by what happened to each object after firing. A case identification establishes that a round was fired in that weapon. It does not by itself establish that this particular bullet was the round in that case, which is the gap the fragment comparison was meant to close and did not.

findings.claim: Nothing further can narrow the question
findings.detail: Several things could and at least one may already exist in the unsealed report. Consecutive matching striae counts, if any were recorded, would indicate how near the comparison came to the identification threshold rather than leaving 'inconclusive' as an undifferentiated category. Land and groove impression widths measured on the jacket would tighten the class comparison against the specific barrel. Fragment masses would enable the retention check described above. Jacket alloy and thickness analysis could be compared against Core-Lokt manufacturing specification to test the stated ammunition type independently of packaging or purchase records. None of this would produce a probability, because the discipline does not generate them, but each would move the class-level consistency from a single word to a described range. This app has not obtained the unsealed report itself and cannot say which of these it contains.

fact_check_gap: The ATF report has been unsealed since April 2026 and this app has not located any coverage that goes beyond its conclusion to its measurements. Reporting has repeated 'inconclusive' and 'deformed .30 calibre jacket fragment' without publishing masses, dimensions, striae counts or land and groove widths — the actual content of a firearms report and the only material from which anyone outside the case could evaluate how close the comparison came. Separately, no coverage located explains to readers that firearms identification produces no probability at all, with the result that both 'the ballistics prove it' and 'the ballistics clear him' circulate freely and neither is a statement the discipline can support.
external_sources: ATF report unsealed by court order, April 16 2026: one deformed .30 calibre bullet jacket fragment and four lead fragments recovered at autopsy; lead fragments not suitable for microscopic comparison; insufficient quality and/or quantity of individual characteristics; .30-06 cartridge case identified as fired from Robinson's Mauser (Fox News, KATV, ABC4)

President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST), 2016: firearms analysis found short of foundational validity; false positive rate ~1 in 66 with upper bound ~1 in 46; inconclusive rate above 1 in 3
AFTE published position rejecting the PCAST foundational-validity conclusion; OSAC and NIST responses to PCAST

title: The Rest of the Physical Evidence: Prints That Excluded Robinson, and Two Items Nobody Has Accounted For
summary: An audit of the physical evidence outside the rifle and the body: three processed crime scenes, latent prints on a Losee Center window from which Robinson was formally excluded, and a striking absence — no public account exists of Kirk's shirt or his lavalier microphone being collected or examined, despite those being the two items that would most directly settle the competing injury theories.
sources_quality: A- for the scene processing and the print exclusion, both from Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina's and a fingerprint examiner's preliminary-hearing testimony; A for the defence motion regarding fragment testing; the absence of shirt and microphone evidence is an absence in public reporting, which is not the same as an absence in the case file, and this entry is careful about that distinction
key_takeaway: Three scenes were processed and described in testimony by Utah State Bureau of Investigation Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina: the Losee Center rooftop, where a screwdriver, shoe impressions and what was characterised as a firing position were recovered; the courtyard where Kirk was struck; and a wooded area northeast of the Losee Center across Campus Center Drive, where the rifle was found. The most consequential single item is one that runs against the state. Several latent fingerprints and a smeared palm print were lifted from a window on the Losee Center, and a fingerprint examiner testified that Robinson was excluded as their source. Faumuina's testimony is to the same effect on the palm print. Those prints therefore belong to someone unidentified. Set against that, reporting elsewhere describes Robinson's own prints being found near the rooftop, so there appear to be two distinct sets and headlines have conflated them. Separately, and more surprising the longer one looks: this app could find no public account of Kirk's shirt being collected, examined for a projectile defect, or tested for residue, and none of the lavalier microphone being collected or examined. Those are the two objects that would most directly resolve the mechanism dispute, and neither appears in any published evidentiary account.

findings.claim: Robinson was excluded as the source of latent prints recovered at the scene
findings.detail: A fingerprint examiner testified at the preliminary hearing that Robinson was excluded from the latent fingerprints and the smeared palm print recovered from a window on the Losee Center, and crime scene investigator Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina's testimony is consistent: the palm print on the glass was not ultimately matched to him. This is a defence-favourable forensic finding delivered by the state's own witnesses and it belongs on the record as such. Its weight should not be overstated — a window on a public university building will carry prints from many people and there is no established time of deposition — but it means unidentified latent prints exist at a processed scene in a capital case, and no public account identifies whose they are or whether they were run against any database beyond Robinson.

findings.claim: Reporting on prints in this case is internally consistent
findings.detail: It is not, and readers encountering headlines from either direction are being given half the picture. Several outlets reported that Robinson's fingerprints and palm print were found near the rooftop, which if accurate is inculpatory. Other coverage of the same hearing reports an examiner excluding Robinson from latent prints and a smeared palm print on a Losee Center window. The most economical reading is that these are two different sets of impressions from two different surfaces, and that headline writers have collapsed them. This app cannot resolve which prints were where from the reporting alone; the distinction is exactly the kind of thing a transcript would settle and exactly the kind of thing that gets lost when a hearing is covered in summary.

findings.claim: Kirk's shirt was collected and forensically examined
findings.detail: No public account of it exists, which is the most significant gap this audit found. A garment worn by a gunshot victim is routine evidence and is normally examined for a projectile defect, for its size and margin characteristics, and for residue. That examination would be decisive on the very question currently in dispute: a perforation consistent with a .30 calibre projectile passing through fabric is direct physical proof that a bullet traversed the shirt, established without any reliance on the sealed autopsy or on the medical examiner who never testified. The absence of residue would independently confirm a distant shot rather than a contact event. This app is careful to state what it can: the shirt may well have been collected and examined, and simply not reported, since preliminary hearings present what is needed for probable cause rather than everything held. But nothing published describes it, and nobody covering the competing injury theories appears to have asked.

findings.claim: The lavalier microphone was collected and examined
findings.detail: Also unaccounted for publicly, and it is the physical object at the centre of an entire competing theory. Kirk was holding a handheld microphone and separately wearing a small lavalier affixed to his clothing. Statements that authorities found no evidence of an exploding microphone are negative assertions about the conclusion rather than accounts of an examination, and this app has located no testimony or report describing the device being recovered, booked, or analysed. If it was examined and showed ordinary impact damage, that is a one-sentence disposal of the theory from physical evidence rather than from the hearsay-relayed autopsy. If it was never recovered, that is itself worth knowing given the transport circumstances documented separately here, in which the assembly was very likely torn loose during an emergency evacuation and may simply have been lost.

findings.claim: The scenes were processed and documented
findings.detail: Three were, and their scope is on the record through Faumuina's testimony. The Losee Center rooftop yielded a screwdriver, shoe impressions and the position characterised as a firing perch, and this app has separately logged the gravel impressions there. The courtyard, where Kirk was struck and where the event tent stood, was processed. The wooded area northeast of the Losee Center and across Campus Center Drive produced the rifle wrapped in a towel, with DNA reported on the trigger, the fired cartridge case and two unfired cartridges. Against that, this app has already logged the adjacent roof excluded from the crime scene on a thinly documented explanation, and the uncollected pistol holster a responding officer noticed but did not seize. Scene processing here is neither negligible nor complete.

findings.claim: The defence has sought independent access to the physical evidence
findings.detail: It has, and the move is both routine and telling about where the contest is heading. Robinson's attorneys filed a motion to halt further testing of the bullet jacket and fragments and to permit a defence expert to photograph and examine them. Consumptive or alterating testing is a standard battle in forensic litigation because each examination can degrade the specimen, and a defence entitled to confront the evidence needs the specimen in a comparable state. That the defence is fighting over physical access to the fragments, rather than advancing an alternative account of who fired, is consistent with the posture this app has documented throughout: a systematic attack on the state's proof rather than a third-party theory.

fact_check_gap: Two objects that would settle the mechanism dispute from physical evidence alone — the shirt and the lavalier microphone — appear in no public evidentiary account, while commentary on both sides of that dispute leans on an autopsy whose author never testified and whose report Utah law seals. A shirt perforation is about as direct as physical proof of a projectile gets, requires no expert relay, and would be trivially describable in open court. Separately, unidentified latent prints and a smeared palm print from which Robinson was formally excluded have received almost no attention relative to the prints attributed to him, and no public account says whether the unmatched impressions were searched against any database at all.
