title: The Repackaging Mechanism: How a Self-Qualifying Source Becomes a Confident Claim With 25x the Reach
summary: A traced example, start to finish. An amateur reconstruction that disclaims itself in its own description was repackaged by a downstream channel into a video asserting a mystery vehicle, waving, phone checks and a specific timestamp — none of which appear anywhere in the source it credits. The derivative reached 409,000 views against the original's 16,000. This is the third documented instance of the same mechanism in this app's files.
sources_quality: A — both videos' metadata, descriptions and full auto-caption transcripts were retrieved directly and the absence of the downstream claims in the upstream transcript was verified by term search, which is reproducible by anyone with a transcript downloader
key_takeaway: The primary source is a video by Chuck Keeler, uploaded September 19, 2025, 16,076 views. Its description is unusually honest: he states he is not a professional investigator, explains he was a UVU student years ago and knows the campus, says he searched the internet and found only a few bits of information which he assembled himself, and closes with a written warning that some of the information is speculative and may not accurately reflect actual events. The narration carries the same qualifiers, including that the limp is 'assumed' to be caused by a rifle. Three days later a channel called Crime Scene 2 Courtroom published a derivative video crediting Keeler, which reached 408,905 views — roughly 25 times the original — and which frames the material as new footage showing a mystery vehicle and cell phone usage, describing the suspect stopping at an intersection as an unknown vehicle pulls alongside at 11:44am. A term search of Keeler's complete transcript returns zero occurrences of 'pull', 'alongside', 'wave', 'white', 'SUV', 'truck', 'phone', 'text', or any 11 o'clock time. Every distinctive claim in the video with the large audience is absent from the source it cites, and the source's explicit disclaimer did not travel with them.

findings.claim: The downstream claims appear in the primary source
findings.detail: They do not, and this was checked mechanically rather than impressionistically. Keeler's full auto-caption transcript runs about 2,290 words and was searched term by term. 'Pull' returns zero. 'Alongside' zero. 'Wave' zero. 'White' zero. 'SUV' zero. 'Truck' zero. 'Phone' zero. 'Text' zero. No 11 o'clock time appears at all, so the 11:44 figure has no origin in the cited source. The single 'stop' hit concerns whether the subject paused behind a house near a wooded area, an entirely different proposition. The mystery vehicle, the waving, the phone checks and the timestamp are all introduced downstream.

findings.claim: The primary source presents itself as investigative reporting
findings.detail: It presents itself as the opposite, in writing and in narration. Keeler states plainly that he is not a professional investigator, that he assembled publicly available fragments because he could not find a consolidated account, and that he is drawing on personal familiarity with the campus as a former student. His closing text warns that some of the information is speculative and may not accurately reflect actual events. Within the narration he flags his inferences as inferences — the limp is 'assumed' to result from a rifle in the trousers; whether the rifle was left in a particular wooded area is 'I don't know' followed by 'I think it's very possible'. This is a careful amateur being careful. The failure is not his.

findings.claim: The footage itself is fabricated
findings.detail: There is no basis for that and the provenance Keeler gives is specific and partly traceable. One clip he attributes to a doorbell camera belonging to the brother of a friend. Another he identifies as footage released by TMZ, captured by a resident's home security camera. TMZ is a named outlet that published on this subject, which makes that clip checkable in a way most circulating material is not. The geography he describes also matches the case record: a residential area north of campus, the subject walking west on 800 South and turning onto 800 West with Utah Lake visible in the distance. Hull's testimony has Robinson returning on foot from a neighbourhood to the northeast and places an officer contact at Campus Drive and 800 South. Real footage, real streets, honest framing — then a layer added on top.

findings.claim: This is an isolated instance
findings.detail: It is the third clearly documented instance of the same mechanism in this app's files and the pattern is now the finding rather than any individual case. In the Olivia Swing corpus the two videos that engage the physical evidence carefully drew 96,000 and 156,000 views while the video asserting an Israeli intelligence operation drew 517,000 and the Epstein video 1.3 million. In the Victor Marx matter, a claim about an unreleased text message travelled through a podcast clip with no record ever produced. Here, a 16,000-view source that disclaims itself becomes a 409,000-view assertion. In each case rigour and reach are inversely related, and in each case the qualifiers are the first thing stripped. Anyone assessing a claim in this case should locate the primary source before assessing the claim, because the version that reaches them is systematically the least careful one in the chain.

fact_check_gap: Verifying this took two transcript downloads and a term search — perhaps fifteen minutes of work — and nobody appears to have done it despite the derivative video having been viewed over 400,000 times. The check is available to anyone: retrieve the cited source, search its transcript for the distinctive claim, and see whether the claim is there. When it is not, the appropriate conclusion is not that the underlying footage is fake but that the specific assertion has no support and its author invented it.

Crime Scene 2 Courtroom, 'Tyler Robinson - New Footage Shows Mystery Vehicle and Cell Phone Usage', uploaded September 22 2025, 9:33, 408,905 views — description retrieved directly

title: The Limp: What the Affidavit Actually Specifies, and Whether a Rifle Fits Down a Trouser Leg
summary: The state's gait claim is more specific than commentary suggests — the Utah County affidavit names the right leg and describes restricted bending. That specificity makes it falsifiable: any footage showing left-side stiffness contradicts a named official document. Separately, the naive version of the carry theory has a dimensional problem the state itself appears to have anticipated.
sources_quality: A- for the affidavit's right-leg specification and the investigators' stated reasoning, both reported from the charging document and law-enforcement statements; A for rifle and human dimensions, which are reference figures; NOT ESTABLISHED for the leg-switching observation, which this app could not corroborate in any source
key_takeaway: The Utah County affidavit specifies a stiff RIGHT leg with restricted bending, and investigators stated the limp was not caused by injury or deformity but by a gun, or in their own hedged phrasing perhaps part of a gun, concealed in his trousers. That hedge matters. A Mauser 98 in its standard configuration runs roughly 49 inches; even the shorter K98k pattern is about 43 to 44 inches. Adult male inseam is typically 30 to 34 inches. A complete rifle therefore cannot be concealed down a trouser leg by ten inches or more, and the widely circulated version of the theory is dimensionally impossible. The barrelled action separated from the stock, however, is roughly 33 to 35 inches, which is at the edge of feasible for a tall individual and is consistent with the state's 'perhaps part of a gun' formulation and with the blue backpack Hull described him carrying earlier that morning. On the leg-switching observation: it is a well-formed falsification test because the affidavit fixes the side, but this app could locate no source documenting a switch, and it is not going to perform frame-level gait analysis on this footage itself.

findings.claim: The state's gait claim is vague about which leg
findings.detail: It is specific. Reporting of the Utah County affidavit describes Robinson appearing to walk with a stiff right leg at a relatively slow pace, with the ability to bend that right leg appearing restricted. Investigators stated the limp was not attributable to injury or deformity but to a firearm, or part of one, concealed in his clothing, and that the limp was absent as he approached the shooting position because the weapon was no longer concealed. That specificity is useful to anyone testing the claim: the side is named, so the claim can be contradicted by evidence rather than merely doubted.

findings.claim: A complete Mauser 98 could be concealed down a trouser leg
findings.detail: Not dimensionally. A standard Mauser 98 rifle is approximately 49 inches overall and the shorter K98k pattern approximately 43 to 44 inches. Adult male inseam is typically 30 to 34 inches. The shortest plausible complete configuration therefore exceeds the available concealment length by roughly ten inches at minimum, and that is before accounting for the fact that a trouser leg is not a rigid tube and the object must clear the hip on every stride. The version of this theory circulating in commentary — a whole rifle down one leg — is not physically possible, and criticism of it on that basis is correct. What the criticism generally misses is that this is not quite what investigators said.

findings.claim: Investigators claimed the whole rifle was in his trousers
findings.detail: Their stated formulation was a gun, 'or perhaps part of a gun', tucked in his trousers. That hedge is the interesting word and it appears to anticipate exactly the dimensional objection above. A Mauser 98 separates into a barrelled action and a stock without tools, and the barrelled action alone — barrel of roughly 24 inches plus receiver — runs about 33 to 35 inches, which is at the outer edge of feasible for a tall person and would produce precisely the restricted knee flexion described. Hull separately testified that Robinson returned to campus on foot just after 10:00 a.m. carrying a blue backpack, which supplies an obvious carrier for a detached stock or for the assembly generally. This app has located no testimony resolving how the weapon was actually transported, which is a genuine gap: the question is answerable and central, and the reconstruction differs materially depending on the answer.

findings.claim: The limp switching legs would refute the concealment theory
findings.detail: It would, and it is a properly constructed test, which is why it deserves a straight answer rather than dismissal. A rigid object splinted along one leg produces a consistent, same-side restriction for as long as it is there; it cannot migrate. So stiffness appearing on the left in any footage, or alternating within a continuous sequence, would contradict the affidavit's named right leg and would not be reconcilable with the concealment explanation. This app could not corroborate the observation: no source located documents a switch, and the material available is compressed, low-resolution and multi-generational, which is exactly the condition in which apparent gait asymmetry can be produced by frame interpolation, motion blur, camera angle and stride phase rather than by anatomy. The test is sound; running it credibly requires continuous unedited footage at usable resolution, ideally the original TMZ-sourced clip rather than a screen capture of a re-upload.

findings.claim: Sprinting and jumping after the shot contradicts the earlier limp
findings.detail: It does not, on the state's own account, and this is a case where the obvious objection fails. Investigators say the limp was already absent as he approached the firing position, because the weapon was by then unconcealed. After the shot he is described as running north across the roof and dropping to the ground carrying a long black object visibly rather than hidden. A man is not expected to move like someone with a splinted leg once the splint is gone. The interval between shot and roof departure is now fixed at 74 seconds by Hull's timestamps, which is ample for that movement unencumbered.

findings.claim: The limp's presence and absence across the same camera is documented
findings.detail: By an amateur observer, in a form that is checkable and that cuts toward the state rather than against it. Chuck Keeler's September 2025 reconstruction reports that the same home security camera which recorded the subject walking toward campus with a limp also recorded him walking away from campus afterwards with no limp. He made that observation ten months before Hull testified to a limp or unusual gait on the approach, so it is not derived from the testimony. Keeler is explicit that the causal inference is an assumption. But the underlying observation — same camera, same subject, limp in one direction and not the other — is precisely the pattern a temporary concealment predicts and is not what a genuine physical impairment would produce.

fact_check_gap: No testimony located establishes how the rifle was physically transported to campus, despite investigators grounding the gait evidence in that very question and despite Hull testifying to a blue backpack earlier the same morning. Whether the weapon was complete or separated, and whether the backpack carried any of it, changes the reconstruction materially and is exactly the sort of detail a trial should surface. Separately, the leg-switching claim circulates without anyone having published a frame-referenced demonstration of it against the affidavit's named right leg, which is the only form in which it could be assessed.
external_sources: Utah County affidavit as reported: stiff right leg, restricted bending, relatively slow pace
Law enforcement statements: limp not from injury or deformity but from a gun 'or perhaps part of a gun' concealed in his trousers; limp absent as he approached the shooting position
TMZ, July 7 2026: video of Robinson limping on the day of the shooting; prosecutors' release of limp footage at the preliminary hearing
Hull preliminary-hearing testimony: return on foot just after 10:00 a.m. carrying a blue backpack; shot 12:23:28 and roof departure 12:24:42
Reference dimensions: Mauser 98 ~49 in overall, K98k pattern ~43-44 in, barrelled action ~33-35 in; typical adult male inseam 30-34 in
Chuck Keeler reconstruction, September 19 2025: same camera showing a limp toward campus and none away from it

title: SU-BTT, SU-BTU and the Named Passenger: Why the Routing Is a Maintenance Itinerary
summary: A claim that an Egyptian presidential-fleet Falcon photographed beside Air Force One at the October 13 Gaza summit proves its September presence in Provo was sinister. The observation is real and the aircraft identification is correct. Both cut the other way. And the two details offered as most suspicious — Duncan Aviation and the Wilmington leg — turn out to be the two facilities that service this exact aircraft type.
sources_quality: A for the aircraft identification and flight history, from this app's own ADS-B archive scan and five aviation databases; A for the Duncan Aviation and Dassault service-centre facts, from the companies' own published material and trade press; A- for the Sharm El-Sheikh footage, which is Fox News live coverage; F for the inferential chain, which is circular
key_takeaway: SU-BTT is a Dassault Falcon 7X, MSN 239, operated by the Government of Egypt / Egyptian Air Force — verified across JetPhotos, Airliners.net, OneSpotter, Flightradar24 and PlaneLogger, and already logged in this app as operator-verified before this claim surfaced. So the October 13 sighting at Sharm El-Sheikh establishes nothing that was in dispute. Worse for the argument, an Egyptian government VIP aircraft parked at an Egypt-hosted summit where President el-Sisi greets a visiting head of state is the single most predictable location on earth for that airframe. The post's own logic is circular: the Provo visit is suspicious because the aircraft is presidential fleet, and the proof it is presidential fleet is that it attended a presidential summit. The second proposition confirms the classification; it does nothing to the first. Then there is the detail the post treats as its clincher. It mocks the maintenance explanation while reporting that the occupants took cars from Duncan Aviation at the Provo FBO. Duncan Aviation's Provo facility is a $50 million, 220,000-square-foot business-jet maintenance, repair and overhaul centre — the largest family-owned business jet MRO in the world by its own description — offering full nose-to-tail support on Dassault airframes specifically, and it is also an IS-BAH accredited FBO, which is why it hands out crew cars. And the aircraft's next stop, Wilmington, Delaware, is the site of Dassault's own Falcon Heavy Service Centre at New Castle Airport. A Falcon 7X spending six days at a Dassault-capable MRO and then flying to Dassault's factory heavy service centre before returning to Cairo is not an unexplained movement. It is a maintenance itinerary, and the post documented it without recognising it.

findings.claim: The Sharm El-Sheikh sighting is new evidence that the Provo visit was sinister
findings.detail: It is neither new nor evidence of that. The only proposition it establishes — that SU-BTT is an Egyptian government aircraft — was already documented and uncontested; this app recorded it as operator-verified across five aviation databases well before the claim appeared. An Egyptian state VIP jet being present at a summit in Egypt hosted by the Egyptian president, during which he greets an arriving American president, is what that aircraft exists to do. Presenting it as a revelation is equivalent to discovering the presidential motorcade outside the White House. The argument is also circular in form: the aircraft's Provo presence is said to be suspicious because it belongs to the presidential fleet, and the evidence it belongs to the presidential fleet is that it turned up at a presidential event. Confirming a classification is not the same as establishing a purpose.

findings.claim: The Duncan Aviation detail undercuts the maintenance explanation
findings.detail: It is the maintenance explanation. Duncan Aviation's Provo location is a purpose-built business-jet MRO of roughly 220,000 square feet, developed at a cost near $50 million on some 45 acres at Provo Municipal Airport, and the company describes itself as the largest family-owned business jet MRO in the world. Its published services include major and minor airframe inspections, engine maintenance, avionics retrofits, paint and interior work, with full nose-to-tail support explicitly covering Dassault airframes alongside Bombardier, Embraer and Gulfstream. It is simultaneously an IS-BAH Stage I accredited FBO, which is precisely why arriving crews receive courtesy or rental vehicles. The post presents 'they got cars from Duncan Aviation at the FBO' as tradecraft. It is the standard service an FBO provides to every crew that lands, and the fact that the FBO in question is a Dassault-capable maintenance centre is the answer to the question the post is asking.

findings.claim: The Wilmington, Delaware leg is unexplained
findings.detail: It is the most explicable leg in the entire itinerary once the airframe type is taken into account. SU-BTT is a Dassault Falcon 7X. Dassault operates its own Falcon service centre at New Castle Airport serving Wilmington, Delaware, at 191 North DuPont Highway — a heavy service centre the manufacturer acquired in 2000, on a site performing certified repair work since 1947. So the sequence is: Falcon arrives at an airport whose principal facility is a Dassault-authorised independent MRO, remains six days, departs for the manufacturer's own Falcon heavy service centre, then returns to Cairo the following day. Six days on the ground is consistent with a scheduled inspection and inconsistent with an operational deployment, which would not idle an aircraft for most of a week. Every leg of the route lands somewhere that services this specific make.

findings.claim: SU-BTT was present when Kirk was shot
findings.detail: It had left the state. This app's own ADS-B archive scan places SU-BTT departing Provo at 7:08 a.m. MDT on September 10 and arriving at New Castle/Wilmington at approximately 10:50 a.m. MDT, roughly an hour and a half before the shot at 12:23:28. Note the correction that belongs alongside it, which this app logged against the debunkers rather than the claimants: the second Egyptian aircraft, SU-BND, a Gulfstream IV-SP, was parked on the Provo ramp from 10:06 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and therefore was present during the shooting. Coverage addressing only SU-BTT's early departure misses this. Duncan Provo also services Gulfstream airframes, which supplies the same explanation for the second aircraft as for the first.

findings.claim: The underlying Owens flight-tracking work was sound
findings.detail: Already assessed in this app and it did not hold. The claim of 73 location overlaps between the Egyptian aircraft and Erika Kirk was reviewed independently and roughly 66 percent of the plane-location claims were found to be wrong, in some instances placing the aircraft on a different continent from where the claim required. Owens reportedly misread UTC timestamps as local Utah time, which is the error that generates spurious proximity. FBI Director Kash Patel stated on September 21, 2025 that the investigation had ruled out a connection between the shooting and these flights. Erika Kirk publicly asked Owens to stop, and a debunk was published by Infowars, which is not an outlet with an institutional reflex toward defending official accounts.

findings.claim: The source of this claim is independent of others already assessed here
findings.detail: It is the same account, and this is now the third distinct strand of this case traced to it. The post is from @ProjectConstitu. This app previously identified that account as the origin of the unverified claim that Robinson's defence counsel is Terryl Farnsworth's cousin, promoted under a 'Mormon Mafia' banner, and as the origin of the analysis of the purportedly leaked SUV interior photographs. In all three instances the pattern is identical: a real underlying artefact — a genuine aircraft, a real attorney, real photographs — carrying an inferential load it cannot support, with no document produced in any of the three. A researcher encountering a fourth claim from this source now has a documented base rate to apply.

findings.claim: A named individual links the May and September Provo visits
findings.detail: The claim, made by Candace Owens and amplified through a reaction video, is that a person travelling under a name rendered in auto-captions variously as Wally Makmoodboard, Wed Makmoud, Wid Makmoud and Wedi Makmood — almost certainly Walid or Waleed Mahmoud — was aboard a third Egyptian aircraft, SU-BTU, which arrived at Provo on May 27, 2025 and departed June 2, and was again among four people aboard SU-BTT flying Provo to Wilmington on September 10. The provenance of the name is not stated. ADS-B tracking records aircraft, not passengers, so it cannot be the source. Passenger manifests for state and private aircraft are not public. Owens says only that she can confirm the individual was 'using the name', without saying how. Absent a stated source this app cannot treat the name as established, and notes that Walid Mahmoud is among the most common name combinations in Egypt, so no meaningful identification could be made from it even if the attribution were sound.

findings.claim: Owens presents this as conclusive
findings.detail: She concedes the two points that matter, and they are the ones that dissolve the claim. On the identity: she states that when dealing with governments 'these people just print passports' and that the name is 'obviously' a dead end — that is, she anticipates the name is an alias and cannot be run down. On the role: she twice offers that the person may simply be a pilot, saying 'maybe it's a pilot, I don't know' and later 'maybe Wed is the pilot. That could make sense.' Those concessions reduce the strongest available version of the claim to: the same crew member accompanied the same government fleet's aircraft on two visits to the same maintenance facility. That is not an anomaly. Aircrew are assigned to airframes, and the same pilot ferrying the same jet to the same MRO twice is the expected case rather than a suspicious one.

findings.claim: The May 27 visit weakens the maintenance explanation
findings.detail: It strengthens it substantially, and this is the most useful thing the new claim contributes. A second Egyptian government aircraft visiting Provo in late May, roughly three months before September, is exactly what an ongoing maintenance relationship with a Dassault-and-Gulfstream-capable MRO produces: airframes return to their service centre repeatedly, and the same personnel accompany them. Note also the registrations. SU-BTT and SU-BTU are sequential, which is how fleets are allocated blocks of marks. Three aircraft from one government fleet — SU-BND, SU-BTT, SU-BTU — using the same American MRO across months is a customer relationship, and it is the single most economical account of every datum in this entire thread.

findings.claim: The June 2 departure shows the aircraft went dark
findings.detail: The 'not transponding' observation reproduces a pattern this app has already tested and explained. A raw re-scan of the ADS-B archive for the September flights found a coverage gap over rural southern Utah consistent with sparse ground-receiver coverage and inconsistent with a transponder shutoff, and that finding converged with named officials' statements reached by a different method. ADS-B is a line-of-sight system dependent on volunteer receiver density; absence of data over sparsely populated terrain is the normal condition, not evidence of concealment. Any claim of a deliberate blackout requires showing the aircraft was within reliable receiver coverage and still absent, which no version of this claim has attempted.

findings.claim: The 'military contractors' aboard are documented
findings.detail: The assertion is delivered as personal certainty rather than as evidence. The formulation used is that the speaker is telling the audience 'for a fact' that the plane carried military subcontractors and 'for a fact' that they were dropped in Provo. No manifest, customs record, contract, employer, name beyond the disputed one, or photograph is produced. That is an appeal to the speaker's own authority, which is the weakest form of sourcing and the one this app has repeatedly found unreliable in this case, including on the Panguitch receipt and the Ackman threat claim. It may be true. Nothing available establishes it.

fact_check_gap: The maintenance question was answerable in two searches — what facility sits at Provo Municipal Airport, and what facility sits at Wilmington — and the answers are on the companies' own websites. Nobody arguing either side appears to have run them. So a Dassault Falcon's repeat visits to a Dassault-capable maintenance centre, followed by a flight to Dassault's own heavy service centre, have been treated for months as an unexplained anomaly by claimants and rebutted by debunkers on timing grounds alone, when the simplest explanation covers all three aircraft, both visit windows, and the recurring crew member. Separately, a named passenger has entered circulation with no stated source, in a form auto-captions cannot even spell consistently, and which the claimant herself describes as probably an alias and probably a pilot.

title: The Accurate Energetic Systems Explosion: 16 Dead, ~100 Safety Violations, and a Theory Already Refuted Upstream
summary: A real industrial catastrophe — sixteen workers killed in Tennessee on October 10, 2025, exactly one month after the shooting — has been folded into the exploding-microphone theory as evidence-destruction. The regulator's findings point the other way, the claim that everyone on site died is false, and the theory it serves was already foreclosed by acoustic analysis independent of any of this.
sources_quality: A for the incident facts, from the U.S. Chemical Safety Board, Tennessee Emergency Management Agency and TOSHA's citations; A for the acoustic and autopsy evidence bearing on the upstream theory; F for the connecting claim, which is attributed to an anonymous 'Iranian hacker' and produces no document
key_takeaway: On October 10, 2025 at 7:47 a.m., multiple catastrophic explosions destroyed a building at the Accurate Energetic Systems facility at Bucksnort in Hickman County, Tennessee, killing sixteen employees. One further employee was seriously injured and six more reported injuries. Roughly 24,600 pounds of explosives were in the building and about 23,000 pounds detonated; debris was thrown up to 700 feet and the blast was felt more than twenty miles away. AES manufactures explosive products for military, aerospace, mining, avalanche control and commercial demolition. The Chemical Safety Board and ATF opened investigations, and officials have described a chain reaction of blasts. The decisive fact for present purposes came later: Tennessee OSHA cited the company for nearly 100 safety violations and proposed over $3 million in fines, characterising a pattern of willful and serious failures, and victims' families have since sought $150 million. An explosives plant carrying a regulator's finding of willful safety failures exploding is the most ordinary industrial-disaster narrative there is. A covert demolition staged to destroy evidence does not arrive with a pre-existing paper trail of documented negligence; that is the signature of the mundane explanation, not the sinister one.

findings.claim: Every employee on site was killed, eliminating all witnesses
findings.detail: Factually wrong, and the error is load-bearing rather than incidental. Sixteen employees were fatally injured, but one further employee was seriously injured and survived, and six additional employees reported injuries. There are survivors, and there are also the employees who were not in that building at 7:47 in the morning, the company's wider workforce, its records, its regulators and its contract counterparties. The version of this claim circulating asserts that the blast killed 'every single employee who worked on-site', which is the premise the witness-elimination theory requires. It is not what happened. A theory that needs total elimination cannot survive the survivors.

findings.claim: The regulatory findings are consistent with a staged explosion
findings.detail: They point firmly the other way. Tennessee OSHA cited Accurate Energetic Systems for close to 100 safety violations with more than $3 million in proposed penalties, describing a pattern of willful and serious failures. That is an inspectorate concluding, on the physical and documentary record of the site, that this facility was being run unsafely. Deliberate demolition of a plant to destroy evidence produces an unexplained event at a compliant facility; it does not produce a hundred pre-existing citations for willful failures. The regulator's findings are the strongest available evidence about causation and they describe an accident waiting to happen at a plant holding twelve tons of explosives in one building.

findings.claim: The theory this serves is still live
findings.detail: It was foreclosed before this facility entered the story, and by evidence that touches none of the disputed institutional links. Rob Maher of Montana State University, the leading academic authority on gunshot audio forensics, identified in podium-adjacent audio the crack-and-pop signature of a supersonic rifle shot with roughly 240 milliseconds separating the ballistic shock wave from the muzzle blast. A ballistic crack is an N-wave generated only by an object moving through air faster than sound, and the crack-to-blast interval encodes distance to the muzzle, yielding roughly 153 metres — the same neighbourhood as the 112-metre Losee-to-courtyard measurement this app computed from map data. A charge detonating at a victim's throat produces one report from one place, with no crack and no separation. Whatever happened in Tennessee, it cannot make a stationary device produce a supersonic projectile's acoustic signature. The autopsy findings — five bullet fragments including a jacket fragment, and a wound track through C2-C7 into the thorax and cranium — point the same way.

findings.claim: The claim has identifiable sourcing
findings.detail: Reporting attributes it to an anonymous 'Iranian hacker', and no document has been produced at any point in the chain. That attribution deserves to be set beside something already in this app's files: NewsGuard documented pro-Iranian networks amplifying, within days of the killing, the specific narrative that Israel was responsible and the suspect was framed, as part of more than 6,000 Kirk mentions across Russian, Chinese and Iranian state outlets between September 10 and 17. A claim about the mechanism of Kirk's death sourced to an anonymous Iranian figure sits squarely in a category this app has already found to be actively seeded. That does not make it false by association — amplification is not evidence about truth, a rule this app applies in every direction — but it does mean the provenance warrants more scrutiny than an anonymous tip normally would, not less.

findings.claim: The supporting details hold up
findings.detail: None of the three is verified and each has an ordinary explanation. That AES held a Department of Defense contract worth around $425,000 in May 2025 is checkable in public federal procurement data, but even if accurate it establishes nothing: AES is a defence explosives manufacturer and holding DoD contracts is its business rather than an anomaly. That the company removed website pages concerning miniaturised shaped charges is unverified without archive comparison, and a firm whose plant has just killed sixteen people and which faces a nine-figure damages demand has obvious counsel-driven reasons to reduce its public product footprint. That managers left shortly before the blast is unverified and unremarkable at 7:47 on a working morning in a multi-building facility. The Fort Huachuca element recycles an allegation this app has already tested and found unsupported.

findings.claim: The one-month interval is meaningful
findings.detail: It is calendar pattern-matching. September 10 to October 10 is a round number in a base-ten calendar and carries no causal information. Fatal industrial incidents occur in the United States regularly, and explosives manufacturing is among the more hazardous sectors; any given month will contain candidate events for a coincidence of this kind. The interval feels significant because it is tidy, which is precisely why it should be discounted rather than credited. Note also that circulating accounts cannot keep the date straight, with some placing the explosion on October 19 and 'five weeks after' rather than October 10 and one month — the exactness that makes the claim compelling is not stable in the tellings that rely on it.

findings.claim: Nothing about this event warrants attention
findings.detail: It warrants a great deal, on its own terms and entirely apart from this case. Sixteen people were killed at work. A regulator found close to a hundred violations and a pattern of willful failure. Families are pursuing a $150 million claim. The Chemical Safety Board, which investigates to prevent recurrence rather than to assign blame, has the matter open. That is a serious industrial-safety story with real victims and real accountability questions, and it is being consumed instead as a plot device in someone else's theory. The families of those sixteen workers are owed an answer about why twelve tons of explosive were in one building at a plant with that citation history.

findings.claim: The May 2025 miniaturised-charge contract exists
findings.detail: It does, and this app located it directly in public federal procurement data rather than taking anyone's word. Award N0016425PJ538, Department of the Navy, $440,494, period of performance May 1 to August 25, 2025, described as a requirement for MINIATURIZED-XS DEMOLITION CHARGES. The circulating claim gives $425,000 in May 2025 for miniaturised shaped charges, which is close enough that it is plainly referring to this record; the nearest match to the exact figure quoted is a separate $424,384 Navy award for engineered products beginning January 2024, so the claim may be conflating two entries. Either way, the underlying contract is real and correctly dated. That is worth stating plainly because this app has spent most of this session finding that specific checkable claims in this case dissolve, and this one does not.

findings.claim: That contract distinguishes Accurate Energetic Systems in any way
findings.detail: It is one line among forty-seven, in a portfolio that is entirely this. A USASpending query for the company returns 47 prime awards totalling $82,094,707 since October 2020, and the miniaturised-charge order is the eighteenth largest at $440,494 — roughly half of one percent of the total. The larger items are M18A1 Claymore mines at $13.76m, $12.08m, $1.65m and $1.42m; Navy MK 179 and MK 180 production units at $10.19m, $1.91m and $1.35m; and repeated TNT demolition block and supplementary charge orders at $8.28m, $7.35m, $6.05m, $3.77m, $3.36m and $2.49m. The catalogue also includes Bangalore torpedoes, MIL-SPEC Composition C4, linear shaped charge kits, PBXN-301, LX-14, pentolite pellets and CAD/PAD items. Customers include the Army, the Navy, ATF and the TSA, the last buying 1,500 pounds of C4. Discovering that this company sold small demolition charges to the Navy is discovering that a bakery sells bread.

findings.claim: A covert weapon would be procured this way
findings.detail: This is the structural problem with the claim and it is fatal. Every datum being cited as evidence of a black operation was retrieved by this app in a single unauthenticated API call to a public government website, complete with award identifiers, dollar values, performance dates, awarding sub-agency and line-item product descriptions. Military ordnance of this kind carries National Stock Numbers and moves through a procurement system built for transparency. An intelligence service arranging an assassination device does not order it on a Navy purchase order with the words demolition charges in the description field, where any member of the public can find it in thirty seconds. The visibility of the record is evidence of routine catalogue procurement, and the claim depends on treating that visibility as if it were a leak.

findings.claim: Unusual aircraft activity over the site accompanied the explosion
findings.detail: None found. This app queried the adsb.lol historical archive for 2025-10-10 and parsed the 30-minute heatmap slots covering 12:00 to 14:00 UTC, which brackets the 12:47 UTC blast (07:47 local). Within 40 kilometres of the site, 84 distinct aircraft were recorded. Not one was below 5,000 feet. Twenty-two had a minimum altitude between 5,000 and 15,000 feet, seven between 15,000 and 25,000, and fifty-five were at 25,000 feet or above. The ten closest tracks passed at between 0.5 and 4.9 kilometres laterally, at minimum altitudes of 33,800, 33,975, 41,000, 41,000, 36,950, 37,000, 44,975, 34,950 and 37,000 feet, with a single exception at 6,675 feet that is consistent with Nashville terminal traffic — the airport lies roughly fifty miles east. This is the profile of an ordinary morning of transiting airline traffic over middle Tennessee. Nothing loitered, nothing orbited, nothing descended.

findings.claim: The ADS-B result is a complete picture of what was airborne
findings.detail: It is not, and the limit should be stated rather than glossed. ADS-B records cooperative traffic only. An aircraft transmitting nothing, or a military aircraft using encrypted Mode 5 without an ADS-B Out broadcast, would not appear in this dataset at any altitude. Ground-receiver coverage also varies, though the 84 tracks recovered here indicate coverage over this area was adequate. So the finding is precisely this: no cooperative aircraft was anywhere near the site at low altitude in the two-hour window around the explosion. That does not exclude an aircraft that chose not to be seen, and no dataset available to a member of the public could. What it does mean is that the burden sits with anyone asserting an air component, because the ordinary evidence for one is absent.

fact_check_gap: The TOSHA citations — nearly 100 violations, over $3 million proposed, willful and serious failures — are the most relevant evidence about why this building exploded and are almost entirely absent from material connecting the event to this case. Separately, both cross-checks requested here were runnable from public sources in minutes: federal procurement data returned the company's complete 47-award, $82 million contract history including the specific May 2025 order being cited, and the adsb.lol historical archive returned 84 aircraft tracks around the blast window showing nothing below 5,000 feet. Neither claimants nor debunkers appear to have run either. The procurement record in particular cuts against the claim it is offered to support, since it demonstrates that this is a catalogue supplier whose entire public business is exactly the product in question.

title: Auditing the Kirk Family's Public Statements Against the Record
summary: A systematic check of what she has said publicly since September 10 against what the evidence establishes. The audit finds no statement of hers that the record contradicts. It also finds something that was not the object of the search: the fact-checking literature about Erika Kirk is almost entirely composed of debunked claims made about her, not by her.
sources_quality: A for her statements themselves, which are on video and in transcripts from her September 12 address, the September 21 memorial and a CBS News town hall; A for the four independent fact-checks of claims made about her; the assessments below concern accuracy, and this entry is explicit about which items are checkable and which are not
key_takeaway: Her documented statements are: that she was not in Utah because her mother was undergoing medical treatment in Phoenix and Charlie told her home needed her, with the plan being to travel together to Colorado State next; that in her September 12 address 'they killed Charlie because he preached a message of patriotism, faith and of God's merciful love'; that the movement would not die and the cries of this widow would echo like a battle cry; an account of his final moments at the hospital; that she had hoped she might be pregnant after his death; and, at the September 21 memorial, that she forgave the man who killed her husband and that the answer to hate is not hate. This app could not find a statement of hers that the record contradicts. Two carry tension worth naming rather than scoring: she said 'they' before any suspect was publicly identified, against a prosecution theory of a single actor, and she attributed the killing to her husband's patriotism and faith where prosecutors later narrowed to his positions on gay marriage and transgender rights. Both were said within 48 hours by a grieving spouse with no access to evidence, and both read as characterisation of her husband rather than assertion of forensic fact. Meanwhile the fact-check literature bearing her name is dominated by fabrications about her: trafficking, Epstein recruitment, a name change, and lost custody, all independently debunked.

findings.claim: Any statement by Erika Kirk is contradicted by the established record
findings.detail: This app looked and did not find one. Her account of why she was in Arizona rather than Utah — her mother's medical treatment in Phoenix, and Charlie telling her home needed her with a plan to travel together to Colorado State — is not contradicted by anything located. Her hospital account, her statement about hoping she was pregnant, and her memorial remarks are personal testimony not susceptible to external check and not disputed by any party. The succession question, on which this app previously attached a qualification, has since been resolved in her favour: Kirk named her as his preferred successor on a recording made at an Aspen donor retreat in August 2025 before roughly 200 people, and donors and board members independently confirmed it. A negative finding is still a finding, and it should be recorded with the same weight this app gives its positive ones.

findings.claim: Her September 12 use of 'they' conflicts with the single-actor theory
findings.detail: There is a formal tension and it should be named without being inflated. Speaking on September 12 she said 'they killed Charlie because he preached a message of patriotism, faith and of God's merciful love.' Robinson was identified publicly that same day, and the prosecution has maintained throughout that he acted alone. But the plural in political speech ordinarily denotes an ideological adversary rather than a count of perpetrators, and she was speaking within 48 hours of her husband's murder with no access to investigative material. Reading it as a claim of conspiracy requires assuming she was making a forensic assertion in a eulogy. Recorded because it is a real divergence in form between what she said and what the state alleges, and because it has been cited in both directions — as evidence she knew more, and as evidence she was inciting — neither of which the words support.

findings.claim: Her stated motive matches the prosecution's
findings.detail: They differ, though the difference is chronological rather than contradictory. She attributed the killing to her husband's patriotism, faith and message of God's merciful love. Prosecutors narrowed their theory on July 29, 2026 to Kirk's opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights specifically — a proposition this app rates at 45-68% and the least certain of its six assessments. She spoke ten and a half months before that narrowing, on the basis of knowing her husband rather than of knowing the evidence. A widow characterising why her husband was hated is not making the same kind of statement as a prosecutor articulating an aggravating circumstance, and the two should not be scored against each other as though they were competing factual claims.

findings.claim: The circulating claims about her have survived checking
findings.detail: Systematically not, and the volume is the striking part. The allegation that Epstein files or federal lawsuits connect her to child trafficking: no credible evidence, and the underlying material does not show or allege it. The Romanian trafficking claim: four independent fact-checkers found no evidence, and the 'adoption' language that seeded it came from a holiday campaign inviting Americans to sponsor Christmas gifts for orphans in Constanța, delivered by U.S. soldiers at a NATO base. The claim that she filed to drop the Kirk surname: traced to a parody account. The claim she lost custody of her children: unsupported, and traceable to Representative Anna Paulina Luna saying Erika 'lost her kids', which Luna subsequently said was a misspeak and that she had meant the children lost their father. Four separate fabrications, four separate debunks.

findings.claim: The asymmetry between claims by her and claims about her is incidental
findings.detail: It is the most substantive result of this audit and it inverts the question that prompted it. Searching for fact-checks of Erika Kirk's statements returns, almost without exception, fact-checks of statements about Erika Kirk — and all of those come back false. This app has now audited a number of figures in this case by the same method. Rob McCoy characterised the killing as a professional hit on reasoning that inverts the evidence. Victor Marx claimed to have been first to announce a death that timestamped Wikipedia edits show others reached earlier. Candace Owens's Panguitch account was contradicted by the named restaurant owner, her Ackman claim denied by two parties, and her flight-tracking analysis found roughly 66% wrong. Against that comparison set, the person whose public statements this app cannot fault is the one about whom the largest volume of false claims circulates.

findings.claim: Her statements are fully verifiable
findings.detail: Much of what she has said is unverifiable in principle and should be left there rather than scored. Her account of Charlie's final moments at the hospital, the content of their last conversation, his telling her home needed her, her hope that she might be pregnant — these are private matters attested by one witness, and no external record could confirm or refute them. This app does not treat unverifiable as suspicious. The one item with a documentary hook is her stated possession of Charlie's phone, which bears on how previously unseen messages reached Andrew Wilson and is logged separately; even there, possession of a spouse's phone is unremarkable and the open question concerns who supplied material to a broadcaster, not whether she was truthful about having it.

findings.claim: Charlie Kirk's parents have made no public statement
findings.detail: A joint statement was issued on behalf of the immediate family — his parents Robert and Kathryn, his wife Erika, and his sister Mary — released through Erika Kirk's account. It describes Charlie as a beloved husband, son, brother, friend and father, and states that every court proceeding serves as a painful reminder of his death and of the loss that has irrevocably impacted their lives and the lives of his children. It expresses gratitude for support and prayers received. Its operative provision is the last one: the family states it will not be commenting further out of respect for the judicial process, and asks for privacy. In the immediate aftermath neither the parents nor Erika issued anything, with the public record consisting of the President's statement that the family was devastated; the joint statement came later and is tied explicitly to the court proceedings rather than to the killing.

findings.claim: Charlie Kirk's mother's first name is settled in public sources
findings.detail: Sources conflict. Several biography pages give the mother as Kimberly, or Kimberly Ann Kirk. The family's own joint statement names her as Kathryn. Where a document issued on a family's behalf enumerates its own members, that is the better authority, and this app records her as Kathryn while noting the discrepancy so anyone encountering the other version knows it exists. A correction belongs here: an earlier revision of this entry disparaged the sources carrying 'Kimberly' as a single low-quality class, which this app had not established. The same search results included TMZ, HollywoodLife, Hello Magazine and Primetimer, which are staffed publications, and this app did not determine which source originated the Kimberly rendering. The authority of the family's own statement does not depend on any judgement about the other sources and should not have been argued as though it did.

findings.claim: Erika Kirk lost custody of her children
findings.detail: Unfounded, with the origin fully traced and the originator's own correction on the record. The claim spread after Representative Anna Paulina Luna said in a podcast interview that Kirk had 'lost her kids'. Luna subsequently stated that she had misspoken and meant that the children had lost their father. Lead Stories and Snopes both examined it in January 2026 and found no evidence; a search of court records and news reporting returned nothing, and representatives for Erika Kirk responded to the claims. The consequence was not confined to the original assertion: it generated a secondary wave of commentary accusing her of abandoning her children, built entirely on a remark its speaker retracted. This app notes that the subjects of the rumour are two children born in 2022 and 2024 who are private individuals with no public role.

findings.claim: The volume of a party's public commentary in this case tracks their proximity to it
findings.detail: It runs close to the inverse, and setting this alongside the hearing-transcript result makes the pattern hard to miss. The immediate family — the people with the greatest stake and the most direct knowledge of the man — issued one joint statement and expressly declined to say more out of respect for the judicial process. The medical examiner, the fingerprint examiner and the firearms examiners spoke only in court. Meanwhile the loudest and most prolific commentary has come from figures who, as this app established by searching all 186,789 words of the preliminary hearing, appear in the proceeding zero times. A claim's prominence in this case is close to uncorrelated with its author's access to the underlying facts, and in several documented instances is inversely correlated with it.

fact_check_gap: The question of whether Erika Kirk has said anything untrue appears not to have been examined by anyone, while enormous effort has gone into fabricating and then debunking claims about her. That imbalance is itself informative about where scrutiny in this case has been directed. The genuine open items are narrow and none concerns her veracity: who supplied unseen Kirk messages to Andrew Wilson, and whether any written succession instrument predates the Aspen recording. Note also that this app previously stated the succession claim more sceptically than the evidence warranted and has corrected that.
external_sources: Erika Kirk's first public address, September 12 2025, streamed from Turning Point USA headquarters (ABC News, PBS NewsHour, Fox News, BBC full remarks)
September 21 2025 memorial at State Farm Stadium: her statement forgiving her husband's killer and that the answer to hate is not hate

title: The 'Fake Hands' Claim: A Language Model Asked the Wrong Question, and a Mortician Answering It
summary: A viral claim that the hands visible at Charlie Kirk's open casket were wax or a prop originated with someone submitting photographs to ChatGPT and asking whether the hands were real. The model said they looked artificial and listed its reasons. Every reason it gave is a textbook description of an embalmed body, which is what a funeral director pointed out — the only source examined in this app's media work so far where the effect of the video was to raise the accuracy of the conversation rather than lower it.
sources_quality: A for the transcript, retrieved directly from the video's own auto-generated captions; A- for the mortuary science content, which is standard professional material stated by a practitioner and independently consistent with published embalming practice; the ChatGPT output is quoted as reported within the video
key_takeaway: The video is 'Charlie Kirk Conspiracy: Are His Hands Fake? | Mortician Reacts' by the channel Lauren the Mortician, published September 18, 2025, running nine minutes with roughly 135,000 views. It reconstructs, then dismantles, a claim that spread after the public viewing. Someone photographed the casket, submitted the images to ChatGPT and asked whether the hands were real. The model replied that they looked artificial: the texture too smooth, the colour flat and waxy, no visible veins, pores or natural warmth, the positioning stiff and mannequin-like, and it contrasted them with an adjacent hand bearing pink nail polish which it called clearly real. The mortician's response identifies the flaw in one line: the question asked was whether the hands were real, not whether they were deceased hands. Every indicator the model listed is a normal consequence of arterial embalming, and the hand it identified as clearly real was a living person's. She summarises it as the model having read out her mortuary science textbook while believing it was exposing a fraud.

findings.claim: The features cited as proof of artificiality are evidence of anything unusual
findings.detail: Each is a documented consequence of the embalming process, and taken together they are a description of a prepared body rather than of a prop. Arterial embalming firms the tissues and removes circulation, which produces the smooth, waxy appearance directly. Cosmetics are then applied to restore colour. Before embalming, blood settles to the lowest points of the body, leaving the hands and face flat, sunken and sallow; embalming reverses that by filling the tissues and evening the tone, which is a principal reason the procedure exists. Absent circulation there is no vascular prominence, and absent life there is no warmth — the model listed the absence of warmth in a corpse as though it were anomalous. Hands in a casket are deliberately positioned by the funeral director, so stiffness and arrangement reflect a decision rather than a defect. The contrast the model drew was between a living hand and an embalmed one, and it correctly perceived a difference while misattributing its cause entirely.

findings.claim: The absence of a wedding ring indentation indicates the body is not genuine
findings.detail: Two ordinary explanations, either sufficient. Men's rings typically sit differently from women's: larger knuckles mean the ring passes over the joint and rests loosely on the finger rather than compressing it, so a permanent indentation is not necessarily present in life. And embalming fills fine wrinkles and restores tissue volume — the practitioner's analogy is to a natural botox effect — which would erase a faint ring line if one existed. The inference from no indentation to no genuine body requires assuming that a mark which may never have existed should survive a process specifically designed to plump depleted tissue.

findings.claim: The hand positioning was unusual
findings.detail: Embalmers position bodies differently as a matter of routine. The reasons offered are all standard: rigor, swelling, injury, family preference, or the embalmer's own judgement about what looks natural. The specific question raised online was why the hands lay lower in the casket rather than in the classic hand-over-hand pose. Where rigor or swelling makes the conventional position look forced, an embalmer will choose another. The observation that a body was not posed in the single arrangement a member of the public expects is not an observation about the body.

findings.claim: The undone bottom suit button was significant
findings.detail: It is ordinary menswear convention, and the video disposes of it with a detail anyone can check: there are photographs of Kirk alive wearing suits the same way. Leaving the bottom button of a jacket unfastened is standard tailoring etiquette of long standing, conventionally traced to Edwardian court fashion. Recorded because it illustrates the general mechanism at work in this cluster of claims, in which unfamiliarity with a domain — embalming, tailoring, funeral practice — is mistaken for detection of an anomaly within it.

findings.claim: The colour of the hands was unremarkable
findings.detail: The practitioner's own view is that the cosmetic work was poor, and this app records it because it is a criticism from inside the profession rather than a defence of everything visible. Her assessment is that the embalmer was attempting to cover bruising and, rather than colour-correcting it, painted over it: too heavy, too dark, and the wrong shade. Her conclusion is that what people are reading as artificial is embalming with a bad paint job, and that this reflects on the embalmer rather than on the body. This app has no basis to evaluate the cosmetic quality and does not adopt the judgement, but it is worth noting that the most credible expert account located does identify a genuine irregularity and locates it in workmanship.

findings.claim: The timeline was too compressed for autopsy and embalming
findings.detail: Addressed directly and consistent with the record established elsewhere in this app. A high-profile homicide produces an automatic autopsy as standard procedure regardless of the decedent's identity, and this app has separately documented the medical examiner's findings entering the preliminary hearing through Agent Hull's testimony. On timing, the practitioner's position is that autopsy and embalming within a 24-hour window is achievable, particularly where family, law enforcement and senior officials are involved and a funeral home prioritises accordingly. The competing claim examined in the video — that there was no refrigeration, no embalming and no autopsy, and that the hands would require a week to look as they did — is inconsistent with the documented autopsy alone.

findings.claim: This video degraded the information environment
findings.detail: It improved it, and that makes it worth logging on its own account. This app has examined a series of video sources on this case and found a consistent pattern in the other direction: rigour inversely correlated with reach, qualifiers stripped in transmission, claims amplified twenty-five fold beyond a source that never made them, and three separate strands traced to a single unverified account. Here a practitioner applied domain knowledge to a claim originating in a general-purpose language model's answer to a malformed question, and resolved it correctly. The methodological lesson is the transferable part: the model was asked whether hands were real rather than whether they were deceased, and answered the question it was given with unwarranted confidence. Its output then circulated as forensic finding. That is the same failure mode this app documented in the machine-generated pages on Erika Kirk's father and on Victor Marx's service record, and the correction here came from someone with a mortuary science textbook rather than from a fact-checker.

fact_check_gap: No mainstream fact-check of the wax-hands claim was located, and the correction that exists came from a practitioner on YouTube rather than from any newsroom. That is worth noting because the claim was trivially answerable by anyone who had asked a funeral director, and because the underlying error — treating a language model's confident description of a corpse as evidence of fraud — is now a recurring source of false claims in this case rather than an isolated incident.

title: The Full Preliminary Hearing Transcript: 186,789 Words, and What Was Never Asked
summary: All five days of the Robinson preliminary hearing obtained and searched — roughly 24 hours of proceedings. It confirms the four camera angles, fixes the chain of custody for the TPUSA video, sharpens the fingerprint exclusion considerably, and reproduces the ATF findings verbatim. It also produces a null result that may be the most consequential item: across the entire record, the SD card is never mentioned once.
sources_quality: A — complete auto-caption transcripts of all five hearing days, retrieved directly and searched locally, totalling 186,789 words. This is court proceedings in open session, the highest-grade source available to this app, and every finding below is reproducible from the same files. Auto-captions occasionally garble proper nouns, so names are given as rendered and flagged where uncertain.
key_takeaway: Five days: 48,039 words, 50,492, 21,555, 47,009 and 19,694. The single most important result is an absence. A search of all 186,789 words for 'SD card' and 'memory card' returns nothing. The removal of a memory card from a camera behind the victim — the act that has generated a court ruling's worth of public controversy, two incompatible TPUSA explanations, and a livestream watched by three hundred thousand people — was never put to a witness. Not the removal, not Bowyer's claim that police commanded it, not Kolvet's claim it was to prevent theft. What the record does establish is the chain from that point onward: Agent Hull testified that Farnsworth provided a flash drive to a Lieutenant O'Brien at a local agency, then shortly afterwards supplied downloadable electronic versions to Agent Mortonson, and that an 1102 statement was collected from Farnsworth on May 6, 2026 — nearly eight months after the killing. That statement was offered as an exhibit and defence counsel Nester objected on hearsay and constitutional grounds. Farnsworth did not testify.

findings.claim: The SD card removal was examined at the preliminary hearing
findings.detail: It was never mentioned. Searching the complete five-day transcript for 'SD card' and 'memory card' returns zero results across 186,789 words. The chain of custody that was established begins with a flash drive already in existence: Hull testified that Farnsworth provided a flash drive to Lieutenant O'Brien with a local agency, and that downloadable electronic versions followed to Agent Mortonson. What happened before that flash drive existed — which camera, which card, who removed it, on whose instruction, and what became of the other three — is not in the record. That is a striking omission given that the same hearing produced a ruling requiring the state to supply original unaltered footage. The public dispute and the judicial record do not overlap at this point at all.

findings.claim: Farnsworth's account was tested
findings.detail: It was not. His account entered as a written 1102 statement collected on May 6, 2026, offered by the state as an exhibit, with Hull confirming he had also spoken to Farnsworth personally and identifying him as the owner-operator or director of Visual Impulse, TPUSA's videographer. Defence counsel Kathryn Nester objected that the statement was hearsay and raised constitutional concerns under the standing objection. Farnsworth did not appear. This now forms a pattern rather than an isolated instance: the two individuals who handled the most contested physical evidence in this case — the medical examiner with the body, and Farnsworth with the video — both entered the record through documents relayed by others rather than through testimony subject to cross-examination. Both were objected to. Both objections were overruled under the preliminary-hearing standard.

findings.claim: All four Visual Impulse videos reached investigators
findings.detail: Confirmed on the record, and it answers a question this app had flagged as open in the benign direction. Defence asked whether Visual Impulse provided four videos and the witness answered that he believed there were four total videos encompassing everything they provided, then agreed that the one shown was only one of the four. So all four angles were furnished to investigators and are presumably in discovery; showing one at a probable-cause hearing is ordinary. The single card removal therefore appears to have been prioritisation rather than withholding, which is the least sinister available reading and the one the record supports. One qualification survives in the witness's own phrasing: four videos encompassed everything they provided, which is a statement about what was handed over rather than about everything that was recorded.

findings.claim: Robinson was excluded from prints at the scene
findings.detail: Substantially more precise than earlier reporting conveyed, and weaker than the headline version. Of the latent prints and the palm print recovered, only three latents — designated 11B, 11C and 11D — were of comparable or poor comparable value, and an examiner identified as Ms. Farmer excluded Tyler Robinson as the source of any of those three. Other prints on the window did not have adequate value for comparison at all. Critically, subsequent FBI examination of those same three prints returned inconclusive. So one examiner excluded him on prints of poor quality and a second laboratory could not reach a conclusion on them, which is materially different from a clean exclusion. The location matters more than the exclusion does: this is the glass window at the northeast corner of the Losee Center, confirmed in testimony as the area where video shows an individual dropping from the roof. Unidentified impressions at the descent point are worth noting even when the prints are poor.

findings.claim: The ATF ballistics findings match what circulated publicly
findings.detail: Word for word. The examiner read from the report that the comparison showed all discernible class characteristics and neither sufficient agreement nor sufficient disagreement of individual characteristics, and that the result was inconclusive; and separately that exhibits 6B through 6E, the lead fragments, are not suitable for microscopic comparison. Exhibit six is described as one .30 calibre class deformed damaged bullet jacket fragment and four lead fragments recovered from Kirk at autopsy. That confirms every element this app logged: five fragments, only one a jacket, only the jacket comparable, class characteristics present and consistent, individual characteristics insufficient. Day four also records the land impression width measurement and the direction of twist, which are the class comparisons that did not exclude the weapon.

findings.claim: The examiner overstated what firearms comparison can establish
findings.detail: The opposite, and this is a notable moment in the record that has gone unreported. On day five the witness confirmed under questioning that Department of Justice laboratory language requires examiners to state that their evidence cannot be described as infallible, that they may not assert a zero error rate, and that they shall not assert that a likelihood ratio of any magnitude provides an absolute identification or source attribution of an individual to an evidentiary sample. That is the discipline's own limitation, stated on the stand, and it is precisely the framework this app described from the PCAST and AFTE literature. Anyone claiming the ballistics prove the case, or that they clear the defendant, is contradicted by the examiner's own testimony about what the method can do.

findings.claim: The shot time is corroborated by more than one source in the record
findings.detail: Multiple independent confirmations across days. A witness on day one testified to hearing the shot at 12:23 while Kirk was answering a question, and described seeing him lean left. Day two places the figure crouching and crawling at the southwest corner of the Losee roof at around 12:23, with the witness noting the video timestamp reads 12:22. Day four references a video timestamp of 12:23:47 with the suspect on the gravel near the northeast side of the building. Those are consistent with the 12:23:28 figure Hull gave for the shot and with a departure at 12:24:42. Worth recording from cross-examination: the day-one witness who fixed the time at 12:23 conceded that his report did not state the direction the shot came from.

findings.claim: The limp appears in sworn testimony
findings.detail: It does, described consistently and independently of any online analysis. The witness noted the figure was wearing different clothing and was walking with what he called a gate or a limp, that he seemed to be having issues walking, and identified it both coming up the parking structure stairs and on the sidewalk north of the Losee building before moving south across its front. A caution for anyone searching these transcripts: the string 'limp' also appears on day four as an abbreviation for land impression width in the firearms examination, an entirely unrelated meaning, and a naive keyword search will conflate the two.

findings.claim: A white SUV features anywhere in the hearing record
findings.detail: Zero occurrences of 'white SUV', 'white vehicle', 'white car' or 'white truck' across all five days. This app has now checked the recurring white mid-size SUV observation against reporting, against the charging materials as described, and against the complete preliminary hearing transcript, and found no reference in any of them. That does not mean no such vehicle appears in any frame of any footage; it means no party to the proceeding considered one relevant enough to raise. The vehicle in the record remains the grey Dodge Challenger, with a passing van mentioned in connection with the escape across Campus Drive.

findings.claim: The autopsy route into the record is as this app described
findings.detail: Confirmed directly. Hull testified that a medical examiner's death investigator, identified as Officer Bullock, was at Timpanogos Hospital when Kirk was pronounced, and that an autopsy was conducted by the Utah Medical Examiner's Office late in the evening of September 10 and possibly into the following day. Under cross-examination Hull confirmed he was not present at the autopsy and that anything he knew came from his meeting with the medical examiner and from the report. Day two records argument over non-publication of the autopsy report itself. This is exactly the posture logged at anomaly A8: the findings reached the court through an investigator who did not perform the examination, from a document the public cannot read, with its author absent.

findings.claim: Tyler Bowyer or Andrew Kolvet appear anywhere in the hearing record
findings.detail: Neither appears once across 186,789 words, searched with spelling variants to allow for caption errors — bowyer, boyer, bower, boyar for the first; kolvet, colvet, kolvit, calvet, kolbet for the second. Zero hits each. They were not witnesses, were not referred to by witnesses, and were not the subject of any question from either side. This matters because these are the two men whose competing public explanations for the memory-card removal produced contradiction X50 in this app. The dispute that has consumed enormous public attention was conducted entirely outside the only forum with subpoena power, and the proceeding never examined either account because neither man was ever put in a position to give one under oath.

findings.claim: Erika Kirk or Mikey McCoy feature in the proceeding
findings.detail: Zero hits for either across all five days. Neither testified nor was mentioned. That is unremarkable in itself — a probable-cause hearing calls the witnesses needed to establish the elements, and a widow and a chief of staff who were not eyewitnesses to the shooting are not among them — but it is worth recording given how much of the public argument in this case concerns their conduct. Every claim this app has assessed about McCoy's movements at the scene, and every claim about Erika Kirk's statements and succession, exists entirely outside the legal record.

findings.claim: Candace Owens's claims were addressed in court
findings.detail: Her name appears twice, both on day five, and both are the same passage captured twice: a question put in what is plainly a media exchange rather than testimony, asking what the speaker thinks about Candace Owens. The answer given is that everyone has a point of view and that the speaker will go with the evidence in court. No claim of hers was examined, no witness was asked about her material, and nothing she has released was offered as an exhibit. The single most prolific source of public claims in this case has no presence in the proceeding at all.

findings.claim: Turning Point USA has a substantive presence in the record
findings.detail: Twenty references, all confined to two narrow functions. First, as the organisation that contracts Visual Impulse to film its events, which is the context for Farnsworth's 1102 statement and the four videos. Second, and substantively, testimony that on the morning of September 10 Robinson went from the parking structure into the amphitheatre or quad area and there made contact with representatives from TPUSA before returning to his vehicle. That is the only factual assertion about the organisation in the entire hearing, and this app had it from reporting; it is now court-confirmed. Nothing about the organisation's security arrangements, its post-event conduct, its statements, or its internal disputes was placed before the court.

findings.claim: The public controversy and the legal proceeding examine the same material
findings.detail: They barely intersect, and setting the two rosters side by side is the clearest way to see it. The courtroom contains Agent Hull, Sergeant Faumuina, ATF examiners Carner and Oliver, fingerprint examiner Farmer, officer Bagley, the medical examiner's investigator Bullock, defence counsel Nester and Burt, and Judge Graf. The public dispute contains Bowyer, Kolvet, Owens, McCoy, Erika Kirk and a large YouTube ecosystem. Exactly one person appears in both, and only in one direction: Terryl Farnsworth, who is the subject of the loudest public allegations and who in court exists solely as an unexamined written statement admitted over a hearsay objection. The consequence is structural rather than sinister. The forum with cross-examination has never tested the claims generating the attention, and the people generating the attention have never been subject to cross-examination. Anyone forming a view from either arena alone is working from a record the other one does not contain.

fact_check_gap: The gap is now precisely locatable. Everything downstream of the flash drive is documented in sworn testimony. Everything upstream of it — the removal of a card from one of four cameras, whether anyone directed it, and what became of the other three cards — exists only in competing public statements by TPUSA officials and in footage shown on a podcast. The one forum with subpoena power and cross-examination never touched it. Given that the same judge ruled twice on the integrity of this video evidence, that omission is itself the most answerable outstanding question in the case, and it will only be answered at trial if someone asks.
